elterngeld-ni-elt-02.claim: limits changes to unpaid months or Plus-to-Basis conversion, omitting the hardship exception.
elterngeld-ni-elt-02.quote: Sollten Sie die Angaben zu Ihrem Bezugszeitraum ändern wollen, können Sie dies nur für Monate tun, für die das Elterngeld noch nicht ausgezahlt wurde. (Ausnahme: Die Umwandlung von Elterngeld Plus-Monaten in Basiselterngeld-Monate ist auch rückwirkend möglich.) Hierbei gilt jedoch, dass die Änderung rechtzeitig vor der Anweisung der Auszahlung bei der Elterngeldstelle eingegangen sein muss. Die Anweisung erfolgt in der Regel etwa eine Woche vor dem Zahltermin, den Sie auf Ihrem Bescheid finden.
elterngeld-ni-elt-02.tr: If you wish to change the details of your benefit period, you can do so only for months for which parental allowance has not yet been paid. (Exception: converting Elterngeld Plus months into basic parental allowance months is also possible retrospectively.) However, the change must have reached the parental allowance office in good time before the payment instruction is issued. The instruction is generally issued about one week before the payment date shown in your decision notice.
elterngeld-ni-elt-02.example: A parent with established particular hardship asks to change a recently paid Basis life month within the statutory retrospective and overall periods. That exception can be assessed; approval is not automatic.
elterngeld-ni-elt-02.context: The one-week processing advice follows. The finding concerns only the closed unpaid-month rule and its missing hardship exception; no actual refusal or universally unlawful processing lead time is established.
elterngeld-ni-elt-02.scope: 2026 claim within the overall benefit period and three-life-month retrospective limit; established special hardship; previously paid month.

elterngeld-be-elt-02.claim: turns the premature-birth thresholds into upper limits.
elterngeld-be-elt-02.quote:
Wenn Ihr Kind nach dem 31. August 2021 und mindestens sechs Wochen vor dem errechneten Geburtstermin zur Welt kommt, können Sie bis zu vier weitere Basis-Elterngeldmonate beziehen.

Wenn das Kind

- bis zu 6 Wochen vor dem errechneten Termin geboren wird, erhalten Sie einen zusätzlichen Monat Basis-Elterngeld

- bis zu 8 Wochen vor dem errechneten Termin geboren wird, erhalten Sie zwei zusätzliche Monate Basis-Elterngeld

elterngeld-ni-elt-01.claim: says ElterngeldPlus is always half the Basis amount.
elterngeld-ni-elt-01.quote:
Basiselterngeld bekommt ein Elternteil in der Regel für maximal 12 Monate. Ein Monat Basiselterngeld entspricht zwei Monaten Elterngeld Plus. Elterngeld Plus können Sie also doppelt so lange wie das Basiselterngeld beziehen (max. 24 Monate), bekommen aber jeden Monat nur den halben Betrag vom Basiselterngeld. Am Ende der Bezugsdauer haben Sie bei Basiselterngeld und bei Elterngeld Plus die gleiche Summe erhalten, nur über einen anderen Zeitraum verteilt.

Sie können auch beide Varianten miteinander kombinieren (z.B. 10 Monate Basiselterngeld und 4 Monate Elterngeld Plus). Arbeiten dürfen Sie sowohl beim Bezug von Basiselterngeld als auch beim Bezug von Elterngeld Plus. Wenn Sie während des Elterngeldbezuges Geld verdienen, wird Ihnen dieses auf Ihr Elterngeld angerechnet. Arbeiten Sie während des Bezuges von Basiselterngeld, verringert sich Ihre Elterngeldhöhe in der Regel. Beim Bezug von Elterngeld Plus können Sie viel mehr dazu verdienen, ohne dass dies Auswirkungen auf die Höhe Ihres Elterngeldes hat. Eine Erwerbstätigkeit empfiehlt sich also in Kombination mit dem Bezug von Elterngeld Plus. Wie viel Sie zum Elterngeld dazu verdienen können, ohne dass sich Ihr Elterngeld mindert, können Sie mithilfe des Elterngeldrechners ermitteln.
elterngeld-ni-elt-01.tr:
One parent generally receives basic parental allowance for a maximum of 12 months. One month of basic parental allowance corresponds to two months of Elterngeld Plus. You can therefore receive Elterngeld Plus for twice as long as basic parental allowance (maximum 24 months), but receive only half the basic parental allowance amount each month. At the end of the benefit period, you will have received the same total with basic parental allowance and Elterngeld Plus, simply spread over a different period.

You can also combine the two variants (for example, 10 months of basic parental allowance and 4 months of Elterngeld Plus). You may work while receiving either basic parental allowance or Elterngeld Plus. If you earn money while receiving parental allowance, this is counted against your allowance. Working while receiving basic parental allowance generally reduces the amount. When receiving Elterngeld Plus, you can earn much more in addition without affecting its amount. Employment is therefore recommended in combination with Elterngeld Plus. You can use the parental allowance calculator to determine how much you can earn alongside parental allowance without reducing it.
elterngeld-ni-elt-01.example: With statutory Elterngeld net income of €2,000 before birth and €1,200 during receipt, and no supplements or offsets, Basis is €520. The Plus ceiling is €650, so actual Plus is also €520 rather than €260.
elterngeld-ni-elt-01.context: Following paragraph distinguishes earnings effects and refers to calculator, but does not limit the first half-payment equation to a no-income case.
elterngeld-ni-elt-01.scope: 2026 birth; positive post-birth earnings; no special supplements or offsetting benefits.

elterngeld-bavaria-paid-basis-hardship.claim: excludes changes to paid Basis months without the hardship exception.
elterngeld-bavaria-paid-basis-hardship.quote: Ja, Sie können bis zum Ende des Bezugszeitraums Änderungen vornehmen. Ausgenommen sind Lebensmonate, für die Sie bereits Basiselterngeld erhalten haben. Unter bestimmten Voraussetzungen können Sie auch ElterngeldPlus-Monate in Basiselterngeld-Monate umwandeln. Wichtig: Sie müssen jede Änderung schriftlich beantragen. Änderungen sind bis zum Ablauf des 32. Lebensmonates des Kindes möglich, wirken jedoch maximal drei Lebensmonate zurück.
elterngeld-bavaria-paid-basis-hardship.tr: Yes, you can make changes until the end of the benefit period. Life months for which you have already received Basiselterngeld are excluded. Under certain conditions you can also convert ElterngeldPlus months into Basiselterngeld months. Important: You must apply for every change in writing. Changes are possible until the end of the child’s 32nd life month, but take effect retrospectively for no more than three life months.
elterngeld-bavaria-paid-basis-hardship.law: BEEG §7(2) normally bars changes to amounts already paid, but expressly permits them in cases of particular hardship. The overall benefit period and three-life-month retrospective limit still apply. Plus-to-Basis conversion is a separate exception. The FAQ gives the conversion exception but categorically excludes paid Basis months.
elterngeld-bavaria-paid-basis-hardship.example: Hypothetical: During an ongoing benefit period, an otherwise eligible parent seeks to change an already paid Basis month within the statutory retrospective window following a situation that meets the particular-hardship standard. Payment alone does not make that change legally impossible; the authority must assess the statutory requirements.
elterngeld-bavaria-paid-basis-hardship.context: The next FAQ explains Plus-to-Basis conversion and the ordinary concurrent-Basis limit. Neither supplies the missing hardship route for paid Basis months. This does not concern changing income facts or correcting an unlawful decision.
elterngeld-bavaria-paid-basis-hardship.scope: Current ordinary 2026 birth unless stated otherwise; published wording only, not evidence of administrative decisions or actual harm.

elterngeld-nrw-planning-paid-months-hard.claim: names Plus-to-Basis conversion as the only exception for paid months.
elterngeld-nrw-planning-paid-months-hard.quote:
Ja, das ist möglich. Am besten beantragen Sie die Änderungen, bevor die Lebensmonate beginnen, die Sie ändern möchten. Denn für nachträgliche Änderungen gibt es Einschränkungen:
• Lebensmonate, für die das Elterngeld schon ausgezahlt wurde, können nicht mehr geändert werden – mit einer Ausnahme: Wenn Elterngeld Plus ausgezahlt wurde und Sie stattdessen nun lieber Basiselterngeld wollen, ist das noch möglich.
• Rückwirkend können Sie die letzten 3 Lebensmonate ändern lassen.
• Nach dem Ende des Bezugszeitraums sind gar keine Änderungen mehr möglich.
elterngeld-nrw-planning-paid-months-hard.tr:
Yes, that is possible. It is best to apply for changes before the life months you want to change begin. There are restrictions on retrospective changes:
• Life months for which parental allowance has already been paid can no longer be changed—with one exception: If ElterngeldPlus was paid and you would now prefer Basiselterngeld, that is still possible.
• Retrospectively, you can have the last three life months changed.
• No changes are possible after the benefit period ends.
elterngeld-nrw-planning-paid-months-hard.law: BEEG §7(2) permits changes to already paid amounts in cases of particular hardship, subject to the overall benefit period and three-life-month retrospective limit. Plus-to-Basis conversion is a separate exception. Calling conversion the one exception leaves out the statutory hardship route.
elterngeld-nrw-planning-paid-months-hard.example: Hypothetical: Within the ongoing benefit period and statutory retrospective limit, an otherwise eligible parent asks to alter a paid Basis month because circumstances meet the particular-hardship standard. The fact that Basis was paid is not an absolute bar.
elterngeld-nrw-planning-paid-months-hard.context: The downloadable current NRW hint sheet expressly gives the hardship exception. The allegation is confined to the planning article’s categorical one-exception wording.
elterngeld-nrw-planning-paid-months-hard.scope: Current ordinary 2026 birth unless stated otherwise; published wording only, not evidence of administrative decisions or actual harm.

Eine Änderung ist – außer in den Fällen besonderer Härte – unzulässig, wenn für die betroffenen Monate das Elterngeld bereits ausgezahlt wurde.
ctx.tr: You can subsequently change the decision about allocation of the benefit period until the benefit period ends. A retrospective change is possible only for the last three months before the start of the month in which the amendment application arrived. elterngeld-nrw-hint-basis-always-higher.claim: says monthly Basis is always higher than Plus.
elterngeld-nrw-hint-basis-always-higher.quote:
Hinweise zur Wahl der Leistungsvariante:
• Die Höhe des Elterngelds ist in einem Monat, für den Sie (Basis-)Elterngeld beziehen, immer höher als in einem Monat, in dem Sie Elterngeld Plus beziehen.
elterngeld-nrw-hint-basis-always-higher.tr:
Guidance on choosing the benefit variant:
• The amount of parental allowance in a month for which you receive (Basis-)Elterngeld is always higher than in a month in which you receive ElterngeldPlus.
elterngeld-nrw-hint-basis-always-higher.law: Under BEEG §4a(2), Plus is calculated using the normal income-loss calculation and capped at half the hypothetical Basis entitlement without relevant post-birth income. If the actual Basis amount with earnings is below that cap, actual monthly Plus can equal actual monthly Basis. The universal claim that Basis is always higher is therefore wrong. Minimums, supplements and offsets have separate rules.
elterngeld-nrw-hint-basis-always-higher.example: Hypothetical: Assuming relevant pre-birth monthly income of €2,000, relevant post-birth monthly income of €1,000, the 65% rate, no supplements and no offsets, actual Basis is €650. The Plus cap is half of €1,300, also €650. Monthly Plus and monthly Basis can therefore both be €650.
elterngeld-nrw-hint-basis-always-higher.context: The same sheet correctly describes a separate calculation in months with work. Its following bullet discusses total payments over a longer period, including minimum-payment and duration limits; those qualifications do not make monthly Basis always larger.
elterngeld-nrw-hint-basis-always-higher.scope: Current ordinary 2026 birth unless stated otherwise; published wording only, not evidence of administrative decisions or actual harm.

ctx.quote: In Monaten, in denen neben dem Elterngeldbezug keine Erwerbstätigkeit ausgeübt wird, entspricht der Anspruch in einem Elterngeld Plus-Bezugsmonat der Hälfte des Anspruchs, der beim Bezug von (Basis-)Elterngeld bestehen würde, mindestens jedoch 150 Euro. Wird in Monaten, in denen eine Erwerbstätigkeit ausgeübt wird, Elterngeld Plus gewählt, erfolgt für diese Monate eine eigene Anspruchsberechnung. Der Anspruch beträgt höchstens die Hälfte des (Basis-)Elterngelds, das zustünde, wenn in diesem Monat keine Erwerbstätigkeit ausgeübt werden würde, mind. jedoch 150 Euro.
ctx.tr: In months without employment alongside parental allowance, entitlement in an ElterngeldPlus month is half the entitlement that would exist for (Basis-)Elterngeld, but at least 150 euros. If ElterngeldPlus is chosen in months with employment, a separate entitlement calculation is made for those months. The entitlement is at most half the (Basis-)Elterngeld that would be due without employment in that month, but at least 150 euros.

ctx.quote:
• Üben Sie während des Elterngeldbezugs eine Teilerwerbstätigkeit aus, können Sie insgesamt mehr Elterngeld erhalten, wenn Sie für die Monate mit Teilerwerbstätigkeit die Leistungsvariante Elterngeld Plus wählen. Dies gilt allerdings nur mit den folgenden Einschränkungen:
- Erhalten Sie auf Grund Ihres hohen Teilzeiteinkommens nur den Mindestbetrag in Höhe von 300 Euro bzw. 150 Euro, bleibt die Wahl der Leistungsvariante ohne Einfluss auf die Gesamthöhe des zustehenden Elterngelds.
- Können Sie Ihren Elterngeld Plus-Anspruch zeitlich nicht voll ausschöpfen, können sich durch die Wahl der Leistungsvariante Elterngeld Plus Nachteile ergeben.
ctx.tr:
• If you work part-time while receiving parental allowance, you can receive more parental allowance in total by choosing ElterngeldPlus for the months with part-time work. However, this applies only with the following restrictions:
- If your high part-time income means you receive only the minimum amount of300 euros or150 euros, your choice of variant does not affect the total amount of parental allowance due.
- If you cannot fully use your ElterngeldPlus entitlement within the available time, choosing ElterngeldPlus may cause disadvantages.

lawMarks: actual monthly Plus can equal actual monthly Basis

elterngeld-nrw-overlap-severe-disability.src: North Rhine-Westphalia family portal: Planning parental allowance
elterngeld-nrw-overlap-severe-disability.claim: restricts the disability exception to severe disability.
elterngeld-nrw-overlap-severe-disability.quote: Die Regelung gilt jedoch nicht für Frühchen und Mehrlingsgeburten. Um die besonderen Belastungen aufzufangen, können Eltern von Frühchen und Mehrlingsgeburten auch weiterhin ohne Einschränkungen gleichzeitig Basiselterngeld beziehen. Gleiches gilt für Eltern eines Neugeborenen, bei dem ein Arzt eine Schwerbehinderung feststellt und für Eltern, die bereits ein schwerbehindertes Kind haben, das beim Geschwisterbonus berücksichtigt wird.
elterngeld-nrw-overlap-severe-disability.tr: The rule does not apply to premature babies or multiple births, however. To accommodate the particular burdens, parents of premature babies and multiple births can continue to receive Basiselterngeld simultaneously without restrictions. The same applies to parents of a newborn whose severe disability is established by a doctor, and to parents who already have a severely disabled child taken into account for the sibling bonus.
elterngeld-nrw-overlap-severe-disability.law: BEEG §4(6) exempts a newborn whose disability within SGB IX §2(1), sentence 1, is medically established; it does not require severe disability. The sibling route refers to BEEG §2a(1) with §2a(2), sentence 3, which extends the age limit for a qualifying disabled sibling to 14. SGB IX §2(2) separately uses a disability degree of at least 50 for severe disability. The page narrows both disability routes by requiring Schwerbehinderung.
elterngeld-nrw-overlap-severe-disability.example: Hypothetical: After a 2026 birth, the newborn has a medically established disability within SGB IX §2(1), sentence 1, but is not severely disabled. Otherwise eligible parents may use the disability exception to concurrent Basis receipt; the planning article’s severe-disability wording omits that case.
elterngeld-nrw-overlap-severe-disability.context: The preceding article passage gives the ordinary one-month/first-twelve-month limit. The linked current NRW hint sheet refers simply to children with disability, contradicting the planning article’s narrower wording. Ordinary overall entitlement and all other eligibility conditions remain.
elterngeld-nrw-overlap-severe-disability.scope: Current ordinary 2026 birth unless stated otherwise; published wording only, not evidence of administrative decisions or actual harm.

ctx.quote:
Beide Elternteile können Basiselterngeld für einen Monat parallel beziehen. Der gemeinsame Elterngeld-Monat kann allerdings nur bis zum 12. Lebensmonat des Kindes genommen werden. Damit können beide Elternteile beispielsweise im Geburtsmonat parallel Basiselterngeld beziehen und sich zusammen um die Betreuung ihres Neugeborenen kümmern.
Wenn Eltern mehr als einen Monat gleichzeitig Elterngeld beziehen möchten, muss sich mindestens ein Elternteil für das Elterngeld Plus entscheiden. Mit dieser Änderung soll die partnerschaftliche Aufteilung von Sorgearbeit und Erwerbstätigkeit zwischen den Elternteilen gefördert werden.
ctx.tr:
Both parents can receive Basiselterngeld in parallel for one month. However, the shared parental-allowance month can only be taken up to the child’s twelfth life month. For example, both parents can receive Basiselterngeld in parallel in the birth month and care for their newborn together.
If parents want to receive parental allowance simultaneously for more than one month, at least one parent must choose ElterngeldPlus. This change is intended to encourage parents to share care and paid work as partners.

ctx.quote: Nur während der ersten zwölf Lebensmonate können beide Elternteile in höchstens einem Lebensmonat gleichzeitig Basiselterngeld beziehen. Diese Regelung gilt nicht bei Kindern, die mindestens sechs Wochen vor dem voraussichtlichen Tag der Entbindung geboren wurden, bei Mehrlingen oder bei (Geschwister-)Kindern mit Behinderung. Wenn Eltern mehr als einen Monat gleichzeitig Elterngeld beziehen möchten, muss sich mindestens ein Elternteil für das Elterngeld Plus entscheiden.
ctx.tr: Only during the first twelve life months may both parents receive Basiselterngeld simultaneously in at most one life month. This rule does not apply to children born at least six weeks before the expected delivery date, to multiple births, or to children or siblings with a disability. If parents want to receive parental allowance simultaneously for more than one month, at least one parent must choose ElterngeldPlus.

lawMarks: it does not require severe disability

elterngeld-pforzheim-thirty-hours.src: Pforzheim: Financial help for families and single parents
elterngeld-pforzheim-thirty-hours.claim: gives a 30-hour work limit for parental allowance.
elterngeld-pforzheim-thirty-hours.quote: Elterngeld wird nach der Geburt des Kindes an Mütter oder Väter gezahlt, die ihre Erwerbstätigkeit wegen der Betreuung ihres Kindes unterbrechen oder auf 30 Wochenstunden einschränken und die übrigen Anspruchsvoraussetzungen erfüllen. Auch Eltern, die vor der Geburt des Kindes nicht erwerbstätig waren, Studierende oder Auszubildende erhalten Elterngeld.
elterngeld-pforzheim-thirty-hours.tr: Parental allowance is paid after the child’s birth to mothers or fathers who interrupt their employment to care for their child or reduce it to 30 hours per week and meet the other eligibility conditions. Parents who were not employed before the birth, students and trainees also receive parental allowance.
elterngeld-pforzheim-thirty-hours.law: For a current birth, BEEG §1(6) allows ordinary employment averaging up to 32 hours a week over the child’s life month. The page retains the earlier 30-hour figure without limiting it to births before 1 September 2021. Training and suitable day-care work have separate exceptions; the hours rule alone does not establish entitlement.
elterngeld-pforzheim-thirty-hours.example: Hypothetical: An otherwise eligible parent after a 2026 birth reduces ordinary work to an average of 31 hours a week over the life month. That satisfies the current work limit even though the city gives 30 hours.
elterngeld-pforzheim-thirty-hours.context: The passage expressly keeps other eligibility requirements and mentions non-employed parents, students and trainees. None of the surrounding Elterngeld sections gives the current 32-hour figure or a historical birth-date limitation.
elterngeld-pforzheim-thirty-hours.scope: Current ordinary 2026 birth unless stated otherwise; published wording only, not evidence of administrative decisions or actual harm.

elterngeld-bremen-eighteen-month-applica.src: Bremen service portal: Apply for parental allowance
elterngeld-bremen-eighteen-month-applica.claim: sets a general application cutoff at the end of life month 18.
elterngeld-bremen-eighteen-month-applica.quote:
Ein Antrag auf Elterngeld kann erst nach Geburt des Kindes gestellt werden.
Die Leistungsgewährung erfolgt frühestens ab Geburt und rückwirkend höchstens für die letzten 3 Lebensmonate vor dem Monat der Antragstellung. Wichtig: Soll das Elterngeld ab der Geburt des Kindes gezahlt werden, ist der unterschriebene Antrag innerhalb der ersten 4 Lebensmonate einzureichen.
Die Eltern können in der Zeit vom Tag der Geburt bis zur Vollendung des 18. Lebensmonats des Kindes Elterngeld beantragen.
elterngeld-bremen-eighteen-month-applica.tr:
An application for parental allowance can only be made after the child’s birth.
Benefits are granted no earlier than birth and retrospectively for at most the last three life months before the application month. Important: If parental allowance is to be paid from birth, the signed application must be submitted within the first four life months.
Parents can apply for parental allowance from the day of birth until the end of the child’s 18th life month.
elterngeld-bremen-eighteen-month-applica.law: BEEG §7(1) limits retrospective payment to the last three life months before the application month. It has no general month-18 application cutoff. Under §4(1), ElterngeldPlus can run through life month 32, with uninterrupted receipt from month 15 by at least one parent. A later application can therefore still concern valid later Plus months.
elterngeld-bremen-eighteen-month-applica.example: Hypothetical: In an ordinary 2026-birth case, father A receives 24 Plus amounts in life months 1–24. Mother B has no countable maternity-benefit entitlement and neither parent has any other deemed or actual Basis months. B meets all eligibility conditions, has no earlier application and submits a first application during life month 22 for Plus in months 25–28. This uses the ordinary shared 28 Plus amounts with the income-reduction condition met; receipt continues without a gap after month 15. A blanket month-18 application cutoff would wrongly exclude the application.
elterngeld-bremen-eighteen-month-applica.context: The page repeats the month-18 cutoff in its basic information but also says Plus may run after month 14 and discusses receipt through month 32 in premature-birth examples. The finding is about filing an application, not a guaranteed payment or retrospective recovery of all earlier months.
elterngeld-bremen-eighteen-month-applica.scope: Current ordinary 2026 birth unless stated otherwise; published wording only, not evidence of administrative decisions or actual harm.

elterngeld-opr-thirty-hours.src: Current parental allowance service: eligibility conditions
elterngeld-opr-thirty-hours.claim: limits work during parental allowance to an average of 30 hours a week.
elterngeld-opr-thirty-hours.quote: Sorgeberechtigte haben Anspruch auf Elterngeld, wenn Sie ihren Wohnsitz oder gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt in Deutschland haben, mit ihrem Kind in einem Haushalt leben, dieses selbst betreuen, erziehen und keine Erwerbstätigkeit bzw. nur eine Teilzeitbeschäftigung von nicht mehr als 30 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt, ausüben. Anspruchsberechtigt sind auch getrennt lebende Eltern mit geteiltem Sorgerecht und Alleinerziehende.
elterngeld-opr-thirty-hours.tr: Persons with custody are entitled to parental allowance if they have their residence or habitual abode in Germany, live in a household with their child, personally care for and raise the child, and do not work or only work part-time for an average of no more than 30 hours per week. Parents living separately with shared custody and single parents are also eligible.
elterngeld-opr-thirty-hours.law: BEEG §1(6) treats work averaging no more than 32 hours per week in the life month as not full-time. Under §28(1), the former 30-hour rule continues only for children born before 1 September 2021. The page presents 30 hours as its general eligibility ceiling.
elterngeld-opr-thirty-hours.example: Hypothetical: A parent of a child born in 2026 works an average of 31 hours per week in the relevant life month and meets all other statutory conditions. Section 1(6) allows that work schedule, whereas the page’s general 30-hour ceiling excludes it.
elterngeld-opr-thirty-hours.context: The service links a current application specifically for births from 1 April 2025 and an August 2025 income appendix. Those documents correctly state 32 hours; their complete relevant sentences are retained as counterevidence. The finding concerns the service page’s general ceiling, not its actual application form or administrative practice. The same page’s 25–30-hour bonus description is context only, not a separate finding.
elterngeld-opr-thirty-hours.scope: Current guidance for ordinary children born in 2026, with all other statutory eligibility and applicable planning conditions assumed. Published wording only; no administrative outcome, actual refusal, harm or intent inferred.

missions-visa-four-week-cutoff.claim: say applications close four weeks before travel.
missions-visa-four-week-cutoff.quote: Die Bearbeitung des Visaantrags dauert mindestens 15 Tage. Die Antragstellung ist 6 Monate bis 4 Wochen vor dem Reisetermin möglich. Beachten Sie, dass die Botschaft keine Garantie für Ihr Reisedatum übernimmt. Es obliegt dem Antragsteller, den Visumsantrag rechtzeitig zu stellen.
missions-visa-four-week-cutoff.tr: Processing a visa application takes at least 15 days. Applications can be submitted from six months to four weeks before the travel date. Please note that the embassy provides no guarantee for your travel date. It is the applicant’s responsibility to submit the visa application in good time.
missions-visa-four-week-cutoff.example: Hypothetical: a visa-required tourist with the formally required application materials ready 21 days before departure could read the page as saying lodging is already impossible, although the ordinary statutory latest point is fifteen days.
missions-visa-four-week-cutoff.context:
[1] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; German: The page states a possible lodging interval, followed by a disclaimer of any guarantee for the intended travel date. It also contains current fees and an ordinary fifteen-day processing statement.
[2] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; German: The current page includes a 2026 jurisdiction notice. Its categorical application interval is separate from the later processing estimate.
[3] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; German; PDF page 1: The August 2025 adult tourism checklist is directly linked from the current application parent. The timing condition is stated as possible lodging, without an urgency qualification.
[4] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; English; PDF page 1: The current English August 2025 adult tourism PDF states the same lodging interval. Its separate processing estimate is two to four weeks.
[5] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; German; PDF page 1: The current August 2025 checklist covers minors applying for tourism, visits or medical treatment. The parent’s direct PDF link was followed.
[6] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; English; PDF page 1: The current English August 2025 minors PDF repeats the categorical four-week lodging boundary.
missions-visa-four-week-cutoff.scope: Acceptance does not guarantee a decision before the desired trip. Individual extended examination, lawful appointment arrangements and operative nationality-specific Article 25a measures require separate consideration; they do not establish a universal four-week lodging cutoff. Later urgent lodging is assessed under Article 9(1). Visa-free travellers and protected free-movement families have distinct rules.

missions-visa-filing-window.law: Visa Code Article9(1) permits ordinary short-stay applications within six months before travel, normally at least15 calendar days beforehand; seafarers performing duties have nine months. In justified individual urgency the consulate or central authorities may permit later lodging. The page's three-month earliest lodging restriction excludes the ordinary three-to-six-month interval. Appointments and processing estimates do not change the legal lodging window.
missions-visa-filing-window.example: Hypothetical: a visa-required tourist planning a February trip could infer in October that filing is too early, although a date within six months falls inside the ordinary legal window.

missions-visa-filing-window.scope:
Normally file at least 15 calendar days before travel; justified urgency rules apply. A six-month legal window does not guarantee a chosen appointment slot. Confirm destination competence, lawful residence or justified nonresident lodging, nationality exemptions and qualifying family rules before using an ordinary tourist checklist. Material counterevidence: the Kathmandu linked English FAQ correctly says six months; Kampala’s tourism and medical sections on the same page correctly say six months; Nicosia’s English counterpart correctly says six months. The finding concerns the conflicting named passages, not uniformly restrictive embassy practice. Their similar template wording does not establish independent drafting.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Tirana: Only ordinary visa-required tourist applicants habitually resident in Albania, Germany competent main destination; ordinary Albanian biometric-passport visitors visa-free. Conflicting German counterpart CORRECTLY says applications possible at earliest SIX months. The Albanian original and its aligned English translation, including the three-month lodging limit, were independently approved in the recorded 20 October 2026 review. Two-week advice is a recommendation, not an alleged binding cutoff. Full-page disclaimer says information without guarantee/completeness and based on embassy knowledge when prepared; it is not marked historical. Ordinary15calendar/urgent discretion/seafarer9 remain separate.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Sofia: Ordinary short-stay applicants who still require a visa, for example a visa-required national ordinarily resident inBulgaria with the specific 'Card of a Foreigner granted Asylum' that current German/English guidance excludes from residence-document visa exemption. Ordinary holders of qualifying Bulgarian residence permits/national longstay visas and visa-free nationals are excluded. The Bulgarian page itself states those ordinary residence documents remove the short-stay visa need from31March2024. Main general disclaimer says information reflects knowledge at drafting and may have changed; it does not archive this currently linked instruction. Appointment booking and processing estimates are distinct; no universal right to later urgent acceptance alleged.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Tegucigalpa: Additional embassy instance of existing missions-visa-filing-window; coordinator should append this version rather than create a duplicate case or replace prior versions. Only ordinary visa-required applicants within competent territory/destination conditions. Urgent late lodging remains discretionary, ordinary15-calendar-day deadline and seafarer9month rule are separate. No service-refusal or actual practice is inferred. The embassy's own consular section is included; honorary consul not attributed.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Tel Aviv, German Embassy Kingston: Visa-required ordinary Schengen applications within the respective embassy jurisdiction, Germany competent as main destination. In Kingston, Bahamas applications administered in Miami are excluded; an example may use a Jamaican resident. The three-month cap is the allegation; the15day sentence is a processing recommendation here, not proof that justified urgent exceptions are excluded. Six-month correct Kingston checklists, nine-month seafarer rule and English-only publication scope are preserved. No appointment, acceptance in every urgent case or visa grant is guaranteed.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Bogotá: Additional publication instances of existing missions-visa-filing-window, not a separate case. Only visa-required third-country nationals lawfully resident in Colombia with Germany as competent main destination. Ordinary15-calendar-day advance rule, justified urgent discretion and seafarer9-month rule separate. No guarantee of appointment or grant; ordinary visa-free Colombian travellers excluded.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Managua: Only ordinary visa-required short-stay applicants with Germany as competent main destination; most ordinary Nicaraguan visitors are visa-free. This is an additional publication instance of stable missions-visa-filing-window, not independent drafting. IMPORTANT conflicting advice: current German counterpart says applications can be made at earliest SIX months, and the linked Spanish visitor checklist says applications are received only within a maximum SIX-month period before travel. Those correct same-site/same-language instructions materially conflict with the quoted THREE-month cap. Appointment booking is distinct; ordinary15-calendar-day advance lodging, justified urgent discretion and seafarer9-month rule remain separate.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Lima: Ordinary visa-required lawful residents of Peru whose main destination is Germany; Peruvian shortstay visa exemption is explained on the current parent and is not challenged. Both dated19June2024 detail pages remain linked from current German/Spanish visa hubs. German current text independently verified in normal browser. The three-month claim concerns lodging, not only appointment release. The German checklist separately asks six months from entry and Spanish one year from application; those are different from the precise six-month-after-final-departure target and are not part of this case. No inference about actual refusal, urgent-case approval or national visas.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Port-of-Spain: Only visa-required applicants within the embassy's current consular jurisdiction, with Germany competent as main destination. Visa-free Trinidad/Tobago nationals travelling for ordinary short visits and jurisdictions represented by another mission are excluded. The linked checklist correctly gives six months; this finding concerns the contrary Step1 sentence and does not imply every mission pathway gives the wrong window. The Step2 'ALL ... no later than15days' statement is separately unresolved and does not establish a right to urgent acceptance. Appointments/processing and Article9 exceptions remain separate.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Montevideo: German publication only. The current German visa hub links this page; the current Spanish counterpart omits an earliest-lodging limit. The appointment bullet expressly states when an application may be submitted, so the allegation concerns lodging rather than a separate appointment booking window. The surrounding ordinary 15-day and discretionary urgent rules remain applicable; the quote does not address them. Similar template wording is not proof of independently drafted guidance.

versions.quote: As of 29 March 2019, the Embassy has outsourced the submission of Schengen Visa applications. The German Visa Application Centre is operated by VFS Global . Visa applicants have to make their Schengen Visa appointments at VFS Global directly and submit the visa application at the Visa Application Centre: VFS Global German Visa Application Centre The average processing time is 7 – 14 days. Applications shall be made no more than three months before the start of the intended visit.

Запазване на дата и час за подаване на заявлението
Моля да си запазите дата и час, за да подадете Вашето заявление. Можете да подадете Вашето заявление най-рано три месеца преди началото на планираното пътуване.
В най-натоварените туристически периоди може да се наложи да изчакате, преди да можете да подадете заявлението в Посолството.
Личното явяване при подаване на заявлението е задължително необходимо. Кандидатът за виза не може да се представлява от друго лице. Възможно е обаче представянето на допълнителни/поискани по-късно документи и получаването на готовия паспорт и от упълномощено лице - след предварително уведомяване/по предварителна уговорка.
Info
Важно указание:
Моля не изпращайте на Визовата служба документи, които не са поискани – най-вече преди подаване на заявлението. Тези документи не могат да се съхраняват тук и/или да бъдат разпределени правилно. Моля да носите всички документи винаги направо при явяването Ви при нас.
versions.tr:
Booking a date and time to lodge the application
Please book a date and time to lodge your application. You may lodge your application at the earliest three months before the start of the planned trip.
During the busiest tourist periods, you may have to wait before you can lodge the application at the embassy.
Personal appearance when lodging the application is absolutely necessary. The visa applicant cannot be represented by another person. However, additional/later requested documents may be presented and the completed passport collected by an authorised person, after prior notification/prior arrangement.
Info
Important notice:
Please do not send the visa office documents that have not been requested, especially before lodging the application. These documents cannot be stored here and/or properly assigned. Please always bring all documents directly when appearing before us.

versions.quote:
Wo muss ich mein Visum beantragen?

Achtung: Unseriöse Visa-Agenturen!
Unsere Auslandsvertretung arbeitet nicht mit Vermittlern oder Agenturen zusammen. Insbesondere haben diese keinen besonderen Zugang zu unserer Terminvergabe.

Schengen-Visa können werktags nach vorheriger Terminvereinbarung im Konsulat der deutschen Botschaft beantragt werden. Termine können ausschließlich über das Kontaktformular der Botschaft vereinbart werden. Eine unmittelbar bevorstehende Reise ohne dringenden Reisegrund ist kein Notfall. Schengen-Visa können frühestens 3 Monate vor Reiseantritt beantragt werden.

Die Bearbeitungsdauer beträgt abhängig von der Staatsangehörigkeit des Antragstellers in der Regel 10 bis 15 Arbeitstage ab dem Zeitpunkt, ab dem Sie alle antragsbegrünenden Unterlagen vollständig eingereicht haben. Die vorzulegenden Antragsunterlagen sind in der nachfolgenden Checkliste aufgeführt.

Der Antrag mit Erklärung wird im Original abgegeben. Da alle anderen Originalunterlagen zurückgegeben werden, sind diese und die Pässe zusätzlich auch in Kopie vorzulegen.

Die Deutsche Botschaft akzeptiert ausschließlich Visumsanträge, bei denen Deutschland oder Frankreich das Hauptreiseziel ist und sich ihr gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt (Lebensmittelpunkt) in Honduras befindet.
versions.tr:
Where must I apply for my visa?

Warning: Disreputable visa agencies!
Our mission does not work with intermediaries or agencies. In particular, they have no special access to our appointment allocation.

Schengen visas can be applied for on working days by prior appointment at the German embassy's consular section. Appointments can only be arranged through the embassy's contact form. An immediately approaching trip without an urgent travel reason is not an emergency. Schengen visas can be applied for at the earliest 3 months before travel.

Depending on the applicant's nationality, processing generally takes10 to15 working days from the point when all supporting documents have been submitted in full. The documents to submit are listed in the checklist below.

The application with declaration is submitted in the original. Because all other original documents are returned, these and the passports must additionally be provided as copies.

The German embassy accepts only visa applications for which Germany or France is the main destination and the applicant's habitual residence (centre of life) is in Honduras.

versions.quote:
When should I apply for a visa?

You can apply for a Schengen visa three months before your trip at the earliest.

You may apply for a new Schengen visa even though your current Schengen visa is still valid.

We recommend to apply for a Schengen visa no later than two weeks before your trip. The processing time usually takes 3 days. Please check the opening hours of the visa section and holidays during which the German Embassy Tel Aviv is closed.

Preparing your application

Please prepare your application as follows:

• Please fill out the visa application form.
• Please compile the documents you need to submit with your application. If documents or supporting documentation are missing, your application may be rejected. See below the information sheet for your type of visa!
• Please make an appointment to submit your application. You may submit your application three months before the start of your planned trip at the earliest, but should not be scheduled later than 15 days prior to your travel date to ensure sufficient time to process your application.

Info
Beware of commercial visa agencies!
Our office does not work with brokers or agencies. These individuals and organisations are NOT able to secure appointments with us. The only cost involved is the visa fee charged by the Embassy. Applications, checklists and appointments are provided free of charge.

Important information:
Please do not send the Visa Section any documents unless requested to do so, particularly not before you have applied for a visa. We are not able to store such documents and will not know to which application they belong. Please always bring all the necessary documents with you to your appointment.

Antrag vorbereiten
Bereiten Sie Ihren Antrag in folgenden drei Schritten vor:
 Füllen Sie bitte das Visa-Antragsformular aus
 Stellen Sie bitte die begleitenden Antragsunterlagen zusammen. Fehlende Unterlagen oder Nachweise können zur Ablehnung des Antrags führen. Wir haben für Sie je nach Reisezweck die passende Checkliste zusammengestellt: Merkblatt zu Schengenvisa
 Buchen Sie bitte einen Termin, um Ihren Antrag zu stellen. Sie können Ihren Antrag frühestens drei Monate vor Antritt der geplanten Reise stellen. Hier gelangen Sie zum Terminvergabesystem der Deutschen Botschaft Bogotá
Info
Achtung: Unseriöse Visa-Agenturen!
Unsere Auslandsvertretung arbeitet nicht mit Vermittlungen oder Agenturen zusammen. Insbesondere haben diese keinen besonderen Zugang zu unserer Terminvergabe. Für das Verfahren ist ausschließlich die von der Auslandsvertretung erhobene Visumgebühr fällig. Die Ausgabe der Anträge und Checklisten und die Terminbuchung sind kostenlos.
Wichtiger Hinweis:
Bitte übersenden Sie der Visastelle unaufgefordert keine Unterlagen – vor allem nicht vor Beantragung. Diese Unterlagen können hier nicht aufgehoben und/oder zugeordnet werden. Bitte bringen Sie vollständige Unterlagen immer direkt zum Termin mit.

Hierbei handelt es sich um Aufenthalte von weniger als 90 Tagen in einem Zeitraum von 180 Tagen in den Schengen-Staaten ohne Aufnahme einer Erwerbstätigkeit, auch wenn es sich nur um einen Transit in den Schengen-Staaten handelt.

Generell gilt:
Als deutsche Auslandsvertretung sind wir für Ihren Antrag zuständig, wenn Deutschland Ihr Hauptreiseziel ist.
Antragsteller*innen für ein Schengen-Visum reichen ihren Visumantrag in der Botschaft ein. Termine zur Antragstellung können hier gebucht werden.

These are stays of fewer than90days within a180day period in the Schengen states without taking up employment, including transit stays in the Schengen states.

General rule:
As a German mission abroad, we are responsible for your application if Germany is your main travel destination.

KUJDES: Vetë shtetasit shqiptarë nuk kanë nevojë për vizë hyrjeje për qëndrime turistike në hapësirën Schengen.
Për të aplikuar për vizë ju nevojitet një datë dhe orë takimi. Ju lutem rezervojeni përmes sistemit online të caktimit të takimeve.
Aplikimi është i mundur deri tre muaj përpara datës së planifikuar udhëtimit. Përpunimi i aplikimit zgjat minimalisht tre ditë pune. Ju rekomandojmë që këkesën për vizë ta dorëzoni jo më vonë se dy javë përpara nisjes së udhëtimit.
Dokumentet dhe dëshmitë duhet të paraqiten në origjinal dhe fotokopje. Dokumentet origjinale do të kthehen sërish. Duhet mbajtur në konsideratë që të gjitha dokumentet e dorëzuara që nuk janë në gjermanisht ose anglisht, duhet të kenë bashkëngjitur përkthimin përkatës në gjuhën gjermane.
Lutemi të lexoni me kujdes këtë fletë-informacioni dhe formularin e aplikimit si dhe t’u përmbaheni saktësisht udhëzimeve.
Aplikimet e plotësuara në mënyrë të mangët apo dokumentacioni i paplotë mund të çojnë në refuzimin e aplikimit.

missions-working-days.quote: Votre demande est examinée par le service des visas de l'ambassade d'Allemagne, qui décide de l'octroi d'un visa. Le service des visas vérifie que votre demande est conforme aux dispositions légales en vigueur. Le code des visas prévoit un délai de traitement de 15 jours ouvrables. Aucune information sur l'état d'avancement de votre demande ne sera communiquée pendant le délai de traitement de votre demande. Passé ce délai, les informations ne peuvent être communiquées qu'au demandeur en personne, à son représentant légal ou à un tiers muni d'une procuration écrite. missions-working-days.tr: Your application is examined by the German embassy’s visa section, which decides whether to issue a visa. The visa section checks whether your application complies with the legal provisions in force. The Visa Code provides for a processing period of 15 working days. No information on the status of your application will be provided during its processing period. After this period, information may only be provided to the applicant personally, their legal representative, or a third party holding written authorisation. Please understand that, for capacity reasons, the visa section cannot be reached by telephone. You can, however, send us a message using the contact form.
missions-working-days.example: Hypothetical: a tourist could read the detailed page as allowing the ordinary statutory period to exclude weekends. Article 23 counts calendar days.
missions-working-days.context:
[1] German Embassy Rabat / Federal Foreign Office; French: The full surrounding sentence attributes the period to the Visa Code. The current parent, dated 6 November 2025, directly links the tourism detail and correctly uses calendar days. This internal correction is disclosed rather than treating all mission guidance as uniform.
[2] German missions in India / Federal Foreign Office; English: The full answer permits extensions to thirty or sixty days. Earlier answers on the same FAQ correctly give fifteen calendar days and a forty-five-day maximum. The contradictory answers coexist in current application guidance; no observed processing practice is inferred.
[3] German Embassy Luanda / Federal Foreign Office; German: The page correctly describes the ordinary fifteen-calendar-day rule but extends it to sixty. The Portuguese counterpart repeats the sixty-day maximum. The current visa hub directly links the German application page.
missions-working-days.scope: Start point is an admissible lodged application. Individual scrutiny, justified urgency and applicable Article 25a measures can alter timing; appointment waits and document transport are different issues. The comparison concerns the asserted statutory unit, not a guaranteed total turnaround.

missions-visa-passport-age-at-expiry.claim: says your passport must still be under ten years old when the visa expires.
missions-visa-passport-age-at-expiry.quote: passport with at least two blank pages, the validity date of which must exceed the visa’s validity for at least three months, and which may not be older than 10 years at the expiry of the visa
missions-visa-passport-age-at-expiry.law: The ordinary issue-age test is issue within the previous ten years at application and separately at external entry. There is no general requirement to remain within that issue-age limit until visa expiry; the passport must still be recognised, valid and meet the separate validity margin.
missions-visa-passport-age-at-expiry.example: Hypothetical: a tourist has a recognised passport issued on 1 November 2016 and valid through 1 August 2027, enters on 25 October 2026 and leaves on 5 November 2026, with a visa expiring on 20 November 2026. The issue-age test is met at application and entry, and the validity margin is met; the website’s visa-expiry age test would nevertheless reject that document condition.
missions-visa-passport-age-at-expiry.context: [1] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; English: The full passport bullet separately requires two blank pages, a three-month validity margin and an issue-age test at visa expiry. The German counterpart instead gives a general maximum ten-year document age. This comparison concerns the point at which issue age is tested, not passport recognition, continuing validity or the separate age condition at entry.
missions-visa-passport-age-at-expiry.scope: The passport must be recognised, valid and meet the ordinary post-departure validity margin and blank-page conditions. An ordinary external entry after the ten-year issue-age limit is not made lawful by this finding. Emergency validity waivers and qualifying free-movement family rules require separate analysis. This is not a claim that every extended passport is recognised.

missions-visa-insurance-extra-fifteen-da.pub: Tashkent mission and Nicosia North Office
missions-visa-insurance-extra-fifteen-da.claim: require insurance beyond the intended stay: 15 extra days in Tashkent and one day after return in the North Office checklists.
missions-visa-insurance-extra-fifteen-da.quote: Reisekrankenversicherung + 1 Kopie: Geltung für das gesamte Hoheitsgebiet der Schengener Staaten, Deckungssumme von mindestens 30.000 Euro für die geplante Zahl an Aufenthaltstagen einschließlich einer Zusatzfrist von 15 Tagen. missions-visa-insurance-extra-fifteen-da.tr: Travel medical insurance + 1 copy: valid throughout the territory of the Schengen states, with cover of at least 30,000 euros for the planned number of days of stay including an additional period of 15 days. The health insurance can be taken out either in Germany (by the inviting person or online) or in Uzbekistan.
missions-visa-insurance-extra-fifteen-da.law: Insurance must cover the days of your intended stay. The 15 extra days of visa validity do not need cover.
missions-visa-insurance-extra-fifteen-da.example: Assume a seven-day Schengen stay, with return home on day seven and otherwise adequate insurance for every stay day. Tashkent’s wording calls for 22 insured days; the North Office’s separate wording calls for at least eight. Ordinary insurance must cover the actual intended stay, including arrival and departure days. These are hypothetical effects of the wording; no extra purchase or expense was observed.
missions-visa-insurance-extra-fifteen-da.context:
[1] German Embassy Tashkent / Federal Foreign Office; German: The insurance row appears in the mandatory document list and also specifies whole-Schengen coverage and at least €30,000. The next sentence allows insurance obtained in Germany or Uzbekistan. The full checklist and current TLScontact notice were read. The Russian language switch repeats the extra-period instruction; it is the same local drafting lineage, not a second mismatch theme.
[2] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; German; PDF page 2: A mandatory checkbox row in the currently linked North-office PDF requires insurance beyond the stay, rather than describing optional protection.
[3] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; English; PDF page 2: The English row explicitly requires a day after return. The current main page links this document with a 9 March 2025 date.
[4] Federal Foreign Office / German mission; Turkish; PDF page 2: The Turkish translation repeats the day-after-return insurance condition. It belongs to the same North-office drafting lineage.
missions-visa-insurance-extra-fifteen-da.scope: Insurance must cover the actual intended stay throughout the required territory and meet the other Article 15 conditions; changed travel dates can require changed coverage. A recommendation to buy a longer policy is permissible. For a multiple-entry application, proof concerns the first intended visit, with an obligation to insure later visits. Article 15’s professional-coverage and diplomatic-passport exemptions and qualifying free-movement family rules require separate assessment. Nationality or document exemptions may remove the visa requirement; Germany must be the competent destination and consular jurisdiction must be correct. Actual Schengen arrival and departure days must be covered. Voluntary extra coverage is lawful; this finding does not dispute insurance for a changed or longer intended stay.

missions-missing-support-documents.claim: says any missing document means your application cannot be accepted.
missions-missing-support-documents.quote: Please make sure to submit all the documents on the list with 1 copy when you show up for your appointment. Applications with missing documents cannot be accepted.
missions-missing-support-documents.law: Article 19 sets formal admissibility conditions, including the form, passport, photograph, applicable biometrics and fee. Missing supporting evidence alone does not make an otherwise admissible application unreceivable; it can lead to a request or refusal on the merits.
missions-missing-support-documents.example: Hypothetical: an applicant with a valid form, passport, photo, applicable biometrics and fee, inside the filing window, lacks an employment letter. That may weaken the case or lead to a request/refusal, but is not by itself an Article 19 bar to lodging.
missions-missing-support-documents.context: [1] German Embassy Singapore / Federal Foreign Office (mission-authored, directing applicants to VFS); English; PDF page 1: The sentence follows an instruction to bring all listed papers. The list includes bank/employment and accommodation evidence, not just formal admissibility items. The parent HTML gives milder advice that incomplete applications may cause delay or refusal and permits further documentation. That context does not qualify the PDF’s categorical statement.
missions-missing-support-documents.scope: Missing Article 19 core elements can justify nonacceptance, subject to its humanitarian/national-interest/international-obligation exception. Applicable fee and biometric exemptions must be honoured. Necessary supporting evidence can still be requested and failure to establish a condition can justify merits refusal. Qualifying free-movement family applications have special rules.

Passport
The passport must be signed by the holder, it must have been issued within the last 10 years, it must have at least one free page and it must be valid for at least 3 months after the end of the planned trip.
missions-visa-blank-pages.law: Your passport needs at least two blank pages.
missions-visa-blank-pages.example: Hypothetical: an ordinary tourist with only one blank passport page could think the current checklist’s travel-document condition is met, although Article 12(b) requires two.
missions-visa-blank-pages.context: [1] German Embassy Muscat / Federal Foreign Office; English; PDF page 1: The complete one-page tourist/visit checklist gives the correct ten-year issue and three-month validity conditions beside the one-page statement. The current parent’s actual download resolves to this hash; other indexed PDF hashes were not substituted.
missions-visa-blank-pages.scope: Qualifying free-movement family members have distinct entry-document rules. The Article 12(a) emergency waiver concerns the validity margin; it does not turn the ordinary two-page requirement into one page.

missions-passport-validity-recommendatio.claim: calls the required three months of passport validity a recommendation.
missions-passport-validity-recommendatio.quote: The passport must be valid for at least the duration of your trip. However, we recommend traveling with a passport which is valid for at least 3 months counting from the date of anticipated return to Singapore. If you apply for a residence permit for Germany your passport has to extend the duration of the visa you are applying for by at least three months. The passport needs to contain at least two blank pages.
missions-passport-validity-recommendatio.law: An ordinary Schengen application normally requires passport validity for at least three months beyond intended final Schengen departure; Article 12 permits a justified-emergency waiver.
missions-passport-validity-recommendatio.example: Hypothetical: a visa-required tourist with two months of passport validity after departure could treat the third month as optional. Ordinarily a new travel document or an applicable waiver is needed.
missions-passport-validity-recommendatio.context: [1] German Embassy Singapore / Federal Foreign Office; English: The preceding sentence requires validity only for the trip. The page also covers Schengen applications. The current, directly linked tourist PDF correctly imposes the three-month margin after Schengen departure; the finding is this general-page statement, not the whole mission's instructions.
missions-passport-validity-recommendatio.scope: Justified emergency waiver under Article 12(a); qualifying free-movement family-member rules require separate assessment. Visa-free travel and national visas have separate frameworks. Return to Singapore and departure from Schengen may be different dates.

missions-visa-residence-wait.pub: Missions in Japan, Oman and Qatar
missions-visa-residence-wait.claim: require six months of residence before you can apply.
missions-visa-residence-wait.quote: If Germany is your main destination regardless of whether your first entry may be, the visa application can only be submitted to the representation responsible for your place of residence. If you have only recently arrived in Japan and/or are only staying here temporarily or have been here for less than six months or – if applicable - do not have a corresponding Japanese residence permit, you must apply at a diplomatic mission of your previous place of residence.
missions-visa-residence-wait.law: A genuine legal resident may apply to the competent destination state’s consulate for that district without a fixed six-month residence wait. Legally present nonresidents have a separate justified-application route.
missions-visa-residence-wait.example: Hypothetical: a visa-required worker who has legally moved to Japan two months earlier and genuinely resides there plans a German holiday. The passage sends that resident back to a previous country even though Article 6(1) contains no six-month waiting period.
missions-visa-residence-wait.context:
[1] German missions in Japan / Federal Foreign Office; English in Japanese navigation: In a list joined by “or”, the paragraph requires recently arrived, temporary or under-six-month applicants to apply at the mission of their previous residence. Lack of an appropriate permit is a separate condition. The current English visa index repeats the instruction and links this page.
[2] German Embassy Muscat / Federal Foreign Office; English: The answer first describes ordinary resident jurisdiction, then adds a completed six-month residence condition. A tourist visitor is not necessarily resident; the contradiction is confined to the separate newly legally resident scenario. The current English visa index directly links this FAQ. Its general legal-change disclaimer is preserved in the full source.
[3] German Embassy Doha / Federal Foreign Office; English: The full sentence limits non-Qatari applicants to residents with this length of legal residence, then permits immigration confirmation in addition to a QID. This general page expressly covers Schengen holidays as well as national visas; only the short-stay application condition is assessed here.
missions-visa-residence-wait.scope: A visit, entry stamp or short temporary presence does not automatically establish residence. Evidence of real legal residence and correct consular district is lawful. Germany must be the competent destination or representation must apply. Justified applications by legally present nonresidents are a separate Article 6(2) route; visa-free and free-movement cases require their own analysis.

versions.quote: If Germany is your main destination regardless of whether your first entry may be, the visa application can only be submitted to the representation responsible for your place of residence. If you have only recently arrived in Japan and/or are only staying here temporarily or have been here for less than six months or – if applicable - do not have a corresponding Japanese residence permit, you must apply at a diplomatic mission of your previous place of residence.

The German Embassy in Muscat can generally only receive applicants who are residents of Oman or Yemen. This means that an applicant needs to have his legal residency in Oman (or Yemen) at least 6 months prior to filing an application at the German Embassy.

Qatari citizens and non-Qatari residents who have been legally residing in Qatar for at least the past six months can apply for visa at the German Embassy Doha. In addition to the QID, the Embassy reserves the right to ask for a written confirmation by immigration.

missions-automatic-overstay-next-refusal.claim: says a past overstay without contacting the aliens authority before visa expiry automatically means the next visa will be refused.
missions-automatic-overstay-next-refusal.quote: If you overstay and do not contact an Aliens Department in Germany before the expiration date of your visa, you will automatically be denied your next Schengen visa. If contacted in time, the Aliens Department will examine the reason (e.g. illness, cancelled flights) and decide on a possible extension based on the extenuating circumstances.
missions-automatic-overstay-next-refusal.law: Past overstay alone is not a separate automatic-refusal rule. It may be decisive evidence in the individual assessment; an operative entry ban, refusal-of-entry alert or another statutory ground can require refusal.
missions-automatic-overstay-next-refusal.example: Hypothetical: a former visa holder who overstayed years earlier without the specified contact, has no current entry ban and now satisfies the stay allowance could read the FAQ as making any new holiday application automatically futile. The actual outcome must depend on the current statutory grounds and individual evidence.
missions-automatic-overstay-next-refusal.context: [1] German Embassy Kampala / Federal Foreign Office; English: The complete answer conditions this consequence on overstaying and not contacting the aliens authority in Germany before the visa expires. It then explains that timely contact allows that authority to examine extenuating circumstances for a possible extension. Neither sentence supplies an exception to the categorical next-visa consequence. The current visa hub directly links this FAQ; the current Schengen application page also refers applicants to it.
missions-automatic-overstay-next-refusal.scope: An operative refusal-of-entry alert or entry ban, an exhausted 90-in-180-day allowance, reasonable doubts about departure, or another applicable statutory ground can still require refusal. Past overstay is relevant evidence and may be decisive after individual assessment. Nationality or document exemptions may remove the need for a visa. Qualifying free-movement family members have special rules. Correct destination competence and consular jurisdiction must also be established.

missions-eu-family-insurance.pub: Doha and Kuala Lumpur missions; VisaMetric referred by the Moscow mission
missions-eu-family-insurance.claim: ask family of EU citizens to meet ordinary tourist conditions.
missions-eu-family-insurance.quote:
Applicants must prove that they are in possession of adequate and valid travel medical insurance, covering emergency medical, hospitalisation and repatriation (including in case of death). The minimum cover should be of 30,000 EUR. This insurance must be valid for the entire Schengen area and throughout the duration of the stay.
Applicants for a uniform visa for more than two entries (multiple entries) shall be in possession of travel medical insurance covering their stays; at the time of application, they need to prove that they have a travel medical insurance covering the period of their first intended visit, and sign the related statement in the application form.
missions-eu-family-insurance.law: Qualifying family members accompanying or joining an EU citizen exercising free movement receive entry-visa facilitation free of charge and as soon as possible. Ordinary tourist insurance and accommodation proof are not additional conditions on that route. Independent family visits and most visits to Germans in Germany require separate analysis.
missions-eu-family-insurance.example: Hypothetical: a visa-required spouse accompanying a French citizen on a two-week German holiday could read the checklist as requiring purchased travel insurance even after proving the relationship and joint travel. This example assumes both qualify under the Directive.
missions-eu-family-insurance.context:
[1] German Embassy Doha / Federal Foreign Office; English: The complete EU/EEA-relative checklist imposes €30,000 insurance covering emergency treatment and repatriation throughout Schengen. Relationship and travel-document rows were read too. No accompanying/joining exception qualifies the insurance instruction.
[2] VisaMetric (external provider referred by German Embassy Moscow; the PDF attributes decisions to the German mission); German; PDF page 2: The two-page leaflet is for visits up to ninety days by EU/EEA/Swiss citizens’ family members. The mandatory bullets require EU-issued insurance, whole-Schengen coverage and €30,000. The mission’s current Erforderliche Unterlagen referral reaches this provider list, whose EU-family download was followed. A separate older referral on the mission page returned 404; the working current referral was used.
[3] German Embassy Kuala Lumpur / Federal Foreign Office; English: This dedicated German-or-EU-family checklist expressly exempts EU spouses from insurance, but requires accommodation and tells applicants to identify a family member living in Germany instead of their spouse in Malaysia.
missions-eu-family-insurance.scope: The applicant must actually qualify under free-movement law. Independent visits to a relative, most visits to a German citizen in Germany, extended-family facilitation cases, and stays beyond three months can require different analysis. Relevant returnee cases can engage EU rights. Abuse, fraud and permitted public-policy/security restrictions remain possible. A qualifying residence card may remove the visa requirement entirely.

missions-age-24-boundary.law: For ordinary passports and ID cards, the age at application determines the band: below 24 normally gives six years; age 24 and above normally gives ten. The lower fee band ends on the 24th birthday; an already issued document does not expire merely because its holder turns 24.
missions-age-24-boundary.example: Hypothetical: a 20-year-old choosing a 48-page passport in Montenegro could expect ten years instead of six, while a 40-year-old in Pakistan could expect an ordinary ID to last only six years instead of ten.

[2] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current table explicitly introduces the section for applicants aged 24 or older and lists the ordinary ID at €89 with six-year validity. missions-age-24-boundary.scope: The comparison concerns ordinary documents issued in the stated age band. missions-optional-fingerprints.pub: Mission guidance including Rabat, Caracas and Seoul, plus the German Institute Taipei
missions-optional-fingerprints.claim: say fingerprints in the ID card are optional.
missions-optional-fingerprints.quote: Fingerabdrücke: Bei der Antragstellung entscheiden Sie, ob Ihre Fingerabdrücke in dem Ausweis-Chip gespeichert werden sollen. Die Kombination von Lichtbild und Fingerabdrücken ermöglicht staatlichen Stellen bei hoheitlichen Kontrollen eine eindeutige Zuordnung von Ausweisinhaber und Ausweis.
missions-optional-fingerprints.tr: Fingerprints: when applying, you decide whether your fingerprints should be stored in the identity-card chip. Combining the photograph and fingerprints allows state authorities carrying out official checks to establish an unambiguous link between the cardholder and the card.
missions-optional-fingerprints.law: Ordinary new ID cards contain two fingerprints from age six, subject to statutory physical-impossibility rules. Older valid cards and temporary documents require separate treatment.
missions-optional-fingerprints.example: Hypothetical: an adult could expect to refuse fingerprint storage when applying for a replacement card. The ordinary application requires those fingerprints.
missions-optional-fingerprints.context:
[1] German Embassy Rabat / Federal Foreign Office; German; PDF page 1: The sentence offers a decision about storage. The leaflet is dated July 2024, includes a general accuracy caveat, and remains linked as an application leaflet by the current passport/ID hub. Its adjacent online-function paragraph concerns a different feature.
[2] German Embassy Caracas / Federal Foreign Office; German: Dated 24 June 2022; still linked from the current passport/ID hub. The passage offers choice without an age or impossibility qualification.
[3] German Embassy Antananarivo / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current passport/ID navigation leads to the page. The surrounding explanation describes declining fingerprint storage without disadvantage rather than a medical or age exemption.
[4] German Embassy Buenos Aires / Federal Foreign Office; Spanish: Current ID instructions dated 12 November 2025 offer storage on request and require a choice. The German counterpart dated 14 November 2025 repeats the choice. The page correctly permits 16+ applicants to apply without parental authorisation; that is not challenged.
[5] German Institute Taipei / Federal Foreign Office (ancillary institute, not embassy or consulate); German: The current A–Z service index directly links this older ID article under Personalausweis. The separate main document hub provides more current instructions. Included as a related German Institute instance, outside the embassy/consulate count.
[6] German Embassy Bishkek / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current passport/ID index’s actual ID-information link was independently followed. The full article presents storage as an applicant choice and contains no specific mandatory-fingerprint qualification elsewhere. The comparison concerns ordinary new ID applications from age six; statutory medical and age exceptions remain applicable. The separate fee bullets are documented in the fee case.
[7] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current application article offers fingerprint storage on request. Its under-sixteen consent paragraph is a separate, correct distinction; it does not qualify the general fingerprint choice.
[8] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The article gives applicants a fingerprint-storage choice. The separate generic minor-attendance passage is qualified by its form for applicants sixteen and above, so no additional parental-consent finding is made.
[9] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: Both the introductory optional-storage description and the declaration paragraph offer a choice. The latter expressly says declining storage causes no disadvantage. The under-sixteen application rule and necessary identity evidence are separate.
[10] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The complete article expressly says declining fingerprint storage causes no disadvantage. Its separate under-sixteen rule and requests for necessary citizenship/name evidence do not cure the opt-out statement.
[11] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The complete application article gives the applicant a choice and says refusal causes no disadvantage. Its correct current fees and under-sixteen rule were checked separately.
[12] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current Service page links this ID article. The general description calls fingerprints an optional additional security feature without confining that choice to exempt applicants or historic cards.
[13] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current passport/loss hub links this article. Its functions FAQ requires applicants to declare whether they want fingerprint storage. The article distinguishes under-sixteen applicants separately.
[14] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current passport/ID hub leads to this article. Its functions FAQ describes fingerprint storage as voluntary; ordinary application and delivery arrangements are distinct procedures.
[15] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current passport/ID hub links the article. Its biometrics description makes storage optional. The fee components are a separate confirmed comparison; no actual counter practice was observed.
[16] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current passport hub has an actual related-content link to this article. It offers optional storage. Its older fee components are assessed separately.
[17] German mission / Federal Foreign Office; German: The current adult-ID article links this additional electronic-ID article. Its general biometrics passage offers optional storage; the link was confirmed in fresh HTML, rather than inferred from a search result.
missions-optional-fingerprints.scope: Children under six do not give fingerprints. Permanent medical impossibility is exempt; temporary inability follows the applicable temporary-impossibility rules. The finding concerns new applications, not whether a lawfully issued older card remains valid.

versions.tr: The new identity card differs from a passport in that storage of fingerprints is voluntary, whereas storage in a passport is mandatory. This decision must be declared in writing when applying.

versions.quote: Der seit November 2010 ausgestellte Personalausweis hat ein Scheckkartenformat und ist mit einem elektronischen Chip ausgestattet. Auf Wunsch können als weiteres biometrisches Sicherheitsmerkmal – neben dem Lichtbild - Fingerabdrücke gespeichert werden. Diese biometrischen Sicherheitsmerkmale dürfen nur von hoheitlichen Behörden ( z.B. Grenzbeamten, Polizei) ausgelesen werden.
versions.tr: The identity card issued since November 2010 is credit-card sized and has an electronic chip. On request, fingerprints can be stored as an additional biometric security feature alongside the photograph. These biometric security features may only be read by authorities exercising public powers (for example, border officers or police).
