missions-abolished-child-passport.pub: German Embassy Antananarivo; German Embassy Gaborone; German Embassy Nicosia
missions-abolished-child-passport.claim: still offer the abolished Kinderreisepass or its extension.
missions-abolished-child-passport.quote: Bitte beachten Sie, dass Ihr Pass- oder Personalausweisantrag nur bearbeitet werden kann, wenn alle Unterlagen vollständig eingereicht und die Gebühren gezahlt worden sind. Die Bearbeitungsdauer für Reisepässe und Personalausweise beträgt etwa vier bis sechs Wochen, da diese in Deutschland hergestellt werden. Die Dokumentenherstellung ist auf Ihren Wunsch auch im Expressverfahren gegen Zahlung eines Zuschlags in Höhe von 32,00 € möglich; hierdurch verkürzt sich der Herstellungsprozess um ca. acht Arbeitstage. Anträge auf Ausstellung oder Verlängerung von Kinderreisepässen werden innerhalb von zwei Werktagen bearbeitet. Bei Eilbedürftigkeit können Sie auch einen bis zu einem Jahr gültigen, vorläufigen Reisepass erhalten, der oft am selben Tag ausgestellt werden kann.
missions-abolished-child-passport.tr: Please note that your passport or identity-card application can only be processed once all documents have been submitted in full and the fees have been paid. Processing passports and identity cards takes approximately four to six weeks because they are produced in Germany. At your request, the documents can also be produced by an express procedure for an additional €32.00; this shortens production by approximately eight working days. Applications to issue or extend children’s passports are processed within two working days. In urgent cases you can also obtain a temporary passport, valid for up to one year, which can often be issued on the same day.
missions-abolished-child-passport.law: The Kinderreisepass document type can no longer be newly issued or extended from 1 January 2024. Lawfully issued older documents can retain their validity; children can receive ordinary biometric passports.
missions-abolished-child-passport.example: Hypothetical: parents whose child’s old passport has expired could plan a two-day Kinderreisepass application from the leaflet, although that type can no longer be issued or extended.
missions-abolished-child-passport.context: Antananarivo: the current-linked preparation leaflet expressly offers issuance and extension in two working days. Gaborone: passport prose expressly offers issuance for children under twelve, with its USA-visa qualification. Nicosia: the English validity paragraph expressly offers one-year issuance and annual extension; the German counterpart correctly announces abolition. Shared templates and conflicting guidance are not independent drafting origins.
missions-abolished-child-passport.scope:
Only fresh applications after 31 December 2023 are challenged, excluding completion of any grandfathered pre-2024 application. Qualifying older Kinderreisepässe can retain validity under PassG §28, subject to expiry, identifiability and other invalidity grounds. Ordinary biometric passports for children, eligible identity cards and temporary passports remain separate options. No actual issue, extension, charge or refusal was observed.

Antananarivo: the October 2022 leaflet is linked as the required preparation document from the current passport page with updated ordinary fees. The full processing paragraph offers issue/extension in two working days. The source-currentness and browser limitations recorded in the original review remain; this filter is not a fresh source check.

Gaborone: current-linked passport prose expressly offers issuance to children under twelve, with its USA-visa qualification retained. The separate referral of consular matters to Pretoria conflicts with the passport offer; service responsibility and actual availability were not resolved by this wording finding.

Nicosia: the current English service menu links the English passport page with its issuance/annual-extension paragraph. The German counterpart correctly announces abolition. The finding concerns the conflicting English statement, not ordinary passports for children.

Editorial narrowing on 21 October 2026 removes fee-table and appointment/personal-appearance mentions as sole evidence. Retained quotations and original review dates are unchanged; no fresh source or legal-merits review is implied.

missions-id-parental-consent.claim: says applicants under 18 must come with both parents.
missions-id-parental-consent.quote: Zusätzliche Unterlagen für minderjährige Antragsteller (d.h. unter 18 Jahre) : 10. Der Antragsteller muss persönlich vorsprechen, dabei muss er von beiden Sorgeberechtigten Eltern begleitet werden, die ein Original und eine Kopie ihres Reisepasses und Personalausweises vorweisen müssen. Ist ein Elternteil verhindert, muss seine Zustimmung zur Ausstellung/Erteilung des Personalausweises durch eine deutsche Behörde, einen deutschen Notar oder eine deutsche Auslandsvertretung (auch Honorarkonsuln) beglaubigt werden. 11. Wenn die Eltern verheiratet sind: Heiratsurkunde und/bzw. Nachweis der Namensführung/-änderung durch die Eheschließung. 12. Falls die Eltern nicht verheiratet sind: wirksame Vaterschaftsanerkennung. 13. Falls einer der Elternteile das alleinige Sorgerecht innehat: Sorgerechtsbeschluss oder Sterbeurkunde des verstorbenen Elternteils. 14. Schulbescheinigung
missions-id-parental-consent.tr: Additional documents for minor applicants (i.e. under 18): 10. The applicant must appear in person, accompanied by both parents with parental responsibility, who must present the original and a copy of their passport and identity card. If a parent cannot attend, their consent to issuance of the identity card must be certified by a German authority, a German notary or a German mission abroad (including honorary consuls). 11. If the parents are married: marriage certificate and/or proof of surname or surname change through marriage. 12. If the parents are unmarried: valid acknowledgement of paternity. 13. If one parent has sole parental responsibility: custody order or death certificate of the deceased parent. 14. School certificate.
missions-id-parental-consent.law: A legally capable applicant aged sixteen or seventeen may apply for an ID card personally. Under-sixteens need the lawful representative to apply; identity and citizenship evidence remain necessary.
missions-id-parental-consent.example: Hypothetical: a legally capable 17-year-old could believe an absent parent's authenticated consent is essential to apply for a new ID card. The ordinary application may be made by that applicant.
missions-id-parental-consent.context: [1] German Embassy Rabat / Federal Foreign Office; German; PDF page 2: The heading applies to all under-18s. Item 10 permits authenticated consent if one parent is absent; item 13 addresses sole custody. Neither limits the parental requirement to under-16 ID applicants. The July 2024 PDF remains linked as current application guidance.
missions-id-parental-consent.scope: Below 16, custody/representation requirements and evidence are legitimate. Lack of legal capacity can require representation. Identity, name and citizenship evidence may still be requested at 16 or 17; that is distinct from parental permission.

The German rules on citizenship are based on the principle of avoiding dual citizenship . This means that a German citizen who voluntarily applies for and accepts a foreign nationality on principle loses the German nationality automatically. This rule does not apply to Germans who receive the other citizenship by law (e.g. children born in Canada to parents that hold German citizenship at the time of the birth of the child may be dual citizens by law), or who applied for and received a citizenship of a member state of the European Union or Switzerland after August of 2007.

The German rules on citizenship are based on the principle of avoiding dual citizenship. This means that a German citizen who voluntarily applies for and accepts a foreign nationality on principle loses the German nationality automatically. This rule does not apply to Germans who receive the other citizenship by law or who applied for and received a citizenship of a member state of the European Union or Switzerland after August of 2007.

Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit

Es gilt weiterhin, dass deutsche Staatsangehörige grundsätzlich die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit verlieren, wenn sie eine fremde Staatsangehörigkeit (außer EU-Staaten und Schweiz) auf eigenen Antrag hin erwerben (§ 25 Abs. 1 StAG), ohne vorher eine Genehmigung zur Beibehaltung der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit beantragt und erhalten zu haben.

Deutsche, die eine ausländische Staatsangehörigkeit erwerben, können jedoch seit dem 01.01.2000 unter erleichterten Voraussetzungen ihre deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit beibehalten. Dabei sind nach § 25 Abs. 2 StAG bei der Entscheidung über eine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung öffentliche und private Belange abzuwägen. Bei Deutschen im Ausland ist insbesondere zu berücksichtigen, ob diese fortbestehende Bindungen an Deutschland haben und über ausreichende Kenntnisse der deutschen Sprache verfügen. Außerdem müssen sie glaubhaft darstellen, weshalb der Erwerb der fremden Staatsangehörigkeit in ihrer konkreten Situation für sie vorteilhaft ist oder bestehende Nachteile beseitigt.

Bitte beachten Sie, dass Ihnen die Genehmigung zur Beibehaltung der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit vor Erwerb der ausländischen Staatsangehörigkeit ausgehändigt worden sein muss.

Seit dem 28.08.2007 verlieren Deutsche, die eine Staatsangehörigkeit eines Mitgliedsstaates der EU oder der Schweiz erwerben, nicht mehr automatisch die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit (§ 25 Abs. 1 S. 2 StAG). Hierzu bedarf es keiner Beibehaltungsgenehmigung.
versions.tr:
Loss of German nationality

It continues to be the case that German nationals generally lose German nationality when they acquire a foreign nationality (except EU states and Switzerland) on their own application (section 25(1) StAG) without having previously applied for and received permission to retain German nationality.

Since 1 January 2000, Germans who acquire a foreign nationality have nevertheless been able to retain German nationality under less restrictive conditions. Under section 25(2) StAG, public and private interests must be weighed when deciding on a retention permit. For Germans abroad, particular consideration is given to whether they retain ties to Germany and possess sufficient German language skills. They must also plausibly explain why acquisition of the foreign nationality is advantageous in their specific situation or removes existing disadvantages.

Please note that permission to retain German nationality must have been handed to you before acquisition of the foreign nationality.

Since 28 August 2007, Germans who acquire the nationality of an EU Member State or Switzerland no longer automatically lose German nationality (section 25(1), sentence 2 StAG). No retention permit is required for this.

versions.quote:
Bei Annahme einer fremden Staatsangehörigkeit:

Der häufigste Fall, der zum Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit führt, ist die Annahme einer anderen Staatsangehörigkeit auf Antrag, ohne vorher eine sogenannte Beibehaltungsgenehmigung besitzen. Lediglich bei Annahme einer Staatsangehörigkeit eines anderen EU-Staates oder der Schweiz gilt eine Ausnahme. Auch die Nachregistrierung im serbischen Personen- und Staatsangehörigkeitsregister, wenn z.B. ein Kind mit einem deutschen und einem serbischen Elternteil in Deutschland geboren wird, gilt als Antragserwerb einer fremden Staatsangehörigkeit. Eine Nachregistrierung führt nur dann nicht zum Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit, wenn diese vor Vollendung des 18. Lebensjahres vorgenommen wird.
versions.tr:
When acquiring a foreign nationality:

The most common case leading to loss of German nationality is acquiring another nationality on application without previously holding a so-called retention permit. An exception applies only when acquiring the nationality of another EU state or Switzerland. Subsequent registration in the Serbian civil-status and nationality register, for example where a child with one German and one Serbian parent is born in Germany, also counts as acquiring a foreign nationality on application. Subsequent registration does not lead to loss of German nationality only if it occurs before the age of 18.

versions.quote:
Sie möchten eine fremde Staatsangehörigkeit annehmen und die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit nicht verlieren? Dann können Sie vorab eine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung beantragen.

Was ist eine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung?

Der Erwerb einer ausländischen Staatsangehörigkeit auf eigenen Antrag oder den Antrag des gesetzlichen Vertreters führt grundsätzlich zum Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit. Sie können sich davor schützen, indem Sie eine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung beantragen. Alle Informationen zur Beantragung der Beibehaltungsgenehmigung finden Sie auf der Webseite des Bundesverwaltungsamts.

Sie benötigen keine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung, wenn Sie die Staatsangehörigkeit eines anderen EU-Staates, oder der Schweiz beantragen möchten.

WICHTIG: Die Beibehaltungsgenehmigung schützt Sie nur vor dem Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit,
- nachdem sie Ihnen ausgehändigt wurde und
- solange sie gültig ist.
Die Urkunde ist grundsätzlich nur zwei Jahre gültig. Das Ablaufdatum finden Sie auf Ihrer Urkunde.

Sollten Sie absehen, dass sich Ihre Einbürgerung in Tansnia verzögert, beantragen Sie bitte sechs Monate vor Ablauf eine zweite Genehmigungserklärung mit dem BVA. Auch diese muss Ihnen ausgehändigt sein, um Sie vor dem Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit zu schützen.

Eine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung kann nicht nachträglich ausgestellt werden. Wenn Sie bereits eine fremde Staatsangehörigkeit auf Antrag angenommen haben, haben Sie ggf. die Möglichkeit die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit durch Einbürgerung wieder zu erlangen.
versions.tr:
Would you like to acquire a foreign nationality without losing German nationality? You can apply beforehand for permission to retain German nationality.

What is a retention permit?

Acquiring a foreign nationality on one's own application or the application of one's legal representative generally leads to loss of German nationality. You can protect yourself by applying for a retention permit. All information about applying for a retention permit is available on the Federal Office of Administration's website.

You do not need a retention permit if you wish to apply for the nationality of another EU state or Switzerland.

IMPORTANT: The retention permit protects you against loss of German nationality only
- after it has been handed to you and
- while it remains valid.
The certificate is generally valid for only two years. You will find the expiry date on your certificate.

If you foresee that your naturalisation in Tanzania will be delayed, please apply to the Federal Office of Administration for a second permission declaration six months before expiry. This too must have been handed to you to protect you against loss of German nationality.

A retention permit cannot be issued retrospectively. If you have already acquired a foreign nationality on application, you may have an opportunity to regain German nationality by naturalisation.

versions.quote:
Verlust durch Annahme einer fremden Staatsangehörigkeit

Der häufigste Verlustgrund der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit ist der Erwerb einer fremden Staatsangehörigkeit auf eigenen Antrag.

Wer als deutscher Staatsangehöriger, egal ob in Deutschland oder im Ausland, auf Antrag eine fremde Staatsangehörigkeit erwirbt, verliert dadurch seine deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit, sofern nichts anderes gesetzlich geregelt ist. Dieser Verlust tritt automatisch per Gesetz ein, ohne dass es dazu einer besonderen Erklärung bedarf oder die deutschen Behörden davon Kenntnis erlangen. Dabei spielt es keine Rolle, wie eine Person die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit erworben hat.

Ein solcher Verlust kann allein dadurch verhindert werden, dass einem zuvor auf eigenen Antrag hin eine Genehmigung zur Beibehaltung der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit erteilt worden ist. Im Zusammenhang mit Passausstellung, Geburt von Kindern, Familiennachzug und sonstigen Anlässen wird geprüft, ob die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit weiterhin besteht. Der Umstand, dass jemand noch seinen deutschen Reisepass oder Personalausweis besitzt, wird dabei nur als Indiz gewertet. Bei Zweifeln kann ein Verfahren zur Feststellung der Staatsangehörigkeit durchgeführt werden.

Seit einer gesetzlichen Neuregelung am 28. August 2007 können EU-Bürger und Schweizer in Deutschland eingebürgert werden, ohne ihre bisherige Staatsangehörigkeit aufgeben zu müssen. Gleichzeitig ist der bisherige automatische Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit beim Erwerb einer fremden Staatsangehörigkeit im Verhältnis zu den EU-Mitgliedsstaaten und der Schweiz entfallen. Mit Wirkung vom 28.08.2007 benötigen Deutsche, die zusätzlich zu ihrer deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit die Staatsangehörigkeit eines EU-Mitgliedsstaates oder der Schweiz annehmen möchten, somit keine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung mehr.
versions.tr:
Loss through acquisition of a foreign nationality

The most common ground for losing German nationality is acquiring a foreign nationality on one's own application.

A German national who acquires a foreign nationality on application, whether living in Germany or abroad, thereby loses German nationality unless the law provides otherwise. This loss occurs automatically by law, without any special declaration or the German authorities becoming aware of it. It does not matter how the person acquired German nationality.

Such a loss can only be prevented by having previously obtained, on one's own application, permission to retain German nationality. Whether German nationality continues is checked in connection with passport issuance, children's births, family reunification and other occasions. Possession of a German passport or identity card is treated only as an indication. In cases of doubt, nationality determination proceedings may be conducted.

Since a legislative change on 28 August 2007, EU citizens and Swiss nationals can be naturalised in Germany without relinquishing their previous nationality. At the same time, automatic loss of German nationality through acquisition of a foreign nationality ceased in relation to EU Member States and Switzerland. With effect from 28 August 2007, Germans wishing to acquire nationality of an EU Member State or Switzerland in addition to German nationality therefore no longer need permission to retain German nationality.

versions.quote:
Ztráta německého občanství v důsledku přijetí jiného státního občanství

Nejčastějším důvodem ztráty německého státního občanství je nabytí státního občanství jiného státu na vlastní žádost.

Německý státní příslušník, který na vlastní žádost nabyde cizí státní občanství, ztratí německé státní občanství bez ohledu na to, zda žije v Německu či v zahraničí, nevyplývá-li ze zákona něco jiného. Ztráta německého občanství nastává v tomto případě ze zákona automaticky, není k ní zapotřebí žádné zvláštní prohlášení a není ani nutné, aby o ní byly informovány německé úřady. Přitom nezáleží na způsobu, jakým dotyčná osoba německé státní občanství nabyla.

Jediným způsobem, jak ztrátě německého státního občanství v takovýchto případech zabránit, je získat předem na vlastní žádost úřední souhlas s ponecháním německého státního občanství. V souvislosti s vydáním cestovního pasu, narozením potomků, slučováním rodin, jakož i z dalších důvodů dochází k prověřování, zda je daná osoba stále německým státním příslušníkem. Skutečnost, že je daná osoba držitelem německého cestovního pasu či občanského průkazu je přitom považována pouze za jednu z indicií.

V případě pochybností lze zahájit postup pro určení státní příslušnosti.

Počínaje 28. srpnem 2007, kdy vstoupila v platnost nová zákonná úprava, mohou občané EU a Švýcarska nabýt německé státní občanství, aniž by se museli vzdát svého dosavadního státního občanství. Zároveň již od tohoto data nedochází k automatické ztrátě německého státního občanství v případech, kdy se německý státní příslušník stane občanem jiného členského státu EU či Švýcarska. S účinností od 28. 8. 2007 tedy již Němci, kteří chtějí mít německé státní občanství i státní občanství jiného členského státu EU nebo Švýcarska, nepotřebují úřední souhlas s ponecháním německého státního občanství.
versions.tr:
Loss of German nationality as a result of acquiring another nationality

The most common reason for losing German nationality is acquiring another state's nationality on one's own application.

A German national who acquires foreign nationality on their own application loses German nationality regardless of whether they live in Germany or abroad, unless the law provides otherwise. In this case German nationality is lost automatically by law; no special declaration is needed, nor is it necessary for the German authorities to be informed. It does not matter how the person acquired German nationality.

The only way to prevent loss of German nationality in such cases is to obtain prior official permission, on one's own application, to retain German nationality. In connection with issuing a passport, children's births, family reunification and for other reasons, checks are made as to whether the person is still a German national. Possession of a German passport or identity card is regarded only as one indication.

In cases of doubt, a procedure to determine nationality may be initiated.

Since 28 August 2007, when new legislation came into force, EU and Swiss citizens can acquire German nationality without giving up their existing nationality. Since that date, German nationality is also no longer automatically lost when a German national becomes a national of another EU Member State or Switzerland. With effect from 28 August 2007, Germans wishing to hold German nationality and nationality of another EU Member State or Switzerland therefore no longer need official permission to retain German nationality.

versions.quote:
Wer als deutscher Staatsangehöriger, egal ob in Deutschland oder im Ausland, auf Antrag eine fremde Staatsangehörigkeit erwirbt, verliert dadurch seine deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit, sofern nichts anderes gesetzlich geregelt ist. Dieser Verlust tritt automatisch per Gesetz ein, ohne dass es dazu einer besonderen Erklärung bedarf oder die deutschen Behörden davon Kenntnis erlangen. Dabei spielt es keine Rolle, wie eine Person die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit erworben hat.

Ein solcher Verlust kann allein dadurch verhindert werden, dass einem zuvor auf eigenen Antrag hin eine Genehmigung zur Beibehaltung der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit erteilt worden ist. Im Zusammenhang mit Passausstellung, Geburt von Kindern, Familiennachzug und sonstigen Anlässen wird geprüft, ob die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit weiterhin besteht. Der Umstand, dass jemand noch seinen deutschen Reisepass oder Personalausweis besitzt, wird dabei nur als Indiz gewertet. Bei Zweifeln kann ein Verfahren zur Feststellung der Staatsangehörigkeit durchgeführt werden.

Seit einer gesetzlichen Neuregelung am 28. August 2007 können EU-Bürger und Schweizer in Deutschland eingebürgert werden, ohne ihre bisherige Staatsangehörigkeit aufgeben zu müssen. Gleichzeitig ist der bisherige automatische Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit beim Erwerb einer fremden Staatsangehörigkeit im Verhältnis zu den EU-Mitgliedsstaaten und der Schweiz entfallen. Mit Wirkung vom 28.08.2007 benötigen Deutsche, die zusätzlich zu ihrer deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit die Staatsangehörigkeit eines EU-Mitgliedsstaates oder der Schweiz annehmen möchten, somit keine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung mehr.

Für in Ungarn wohnhafte Deutsche, die auf eigenen Antrag vor dem 28.08. 2007 in die ungarische Staatsangehörigkeit eingebürgert wurden, gilt damit: Mit dem Erwerb der ungarischen Staatsangehörigkeit ging die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit regelmäßig verloren, wenn nicht zuvor eine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung erteilt wurde. Nach der Einbürgerung geborene Kinder erwerben dann nicht mehr die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit vom vormals deutschen Elternteil. Umgekehrt gilt, dass diese Kinder bei Geburt vor dem Einbürgerungstermin des Elternteils die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit regelmäßig erworben haben.

Für in Ungarn wohnhafte Deutsche, die auf eigenen Antrag ab dem 28.08. 2007 in die ungarische Staatsangehörigkeit eingebürgert wurden, tritt dagegen kein Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit ein.
versions.tr:
Anyone who, as a German national, whether in Germany or abroad, acquires a foreign nationality on application thereby loses German nationality unless the law provides otherwise. This loss occurs automatically by operation of law, without requiring a special declaration or the German authorities to become aware of it. It does not matter how the person acquired German nationality.

Such a loss can only be prevented by previously obtaining permission, on one's own application, to retain German nationality. In connection with issuing passports, births of children, family reunification and other occasions, it is checked whether German nationality still exists. Possessing a German passport or identity card is treated only as an indication. If there is doubt, a nationality determination procedure may be conducted.

Since a legislative change on 28 August 2007, EU citizens and Swiss nationals can be naturalised in Germany without giving up their previous nationality. At the same time, the previous automatic loss of German nationality on acquiring a foreign nationality ceased in relation to EU Member States and Switzerland. With effect from 28 August 2007, Germans who wish to acquire the nationality of an EU Member State or Switzerland in addition to German nationality therefore no longer require retention permission.

For Germans resident in Hungary who were naturalised as Hungarian citizens on their own application before 28 August 2007, this means that German nationality was generally lost on acquiring Hungarian nationality unless retention permission had previously been granted. Children born after naturalisation then no longer acquire German nationality from the formerly German parent. Conversely, children born before the parent's naturalisation date generally acquired German nationality at birth.

For Germans resident in Hungary who were naturalised as Hungarian citizens on their own application on or after 28 August 2007, there is no loss of German nationality.

missions-th-uder-optional-fingerprints.claim: describes new ID-card fingerprints as optional on its currently linked service page.
missions-th-uder-optional-fingerprints.quote:
Fingerabdrücke
Auf Wunsch des Antragsstellers können auf dem Ausweis Fingerabdrücke abgelegt werden. Die Kombination von Lichtbild und Finderabdrücken ermöglicht eine ein­deutige Zuordnung von Ausweisinhaber und Ausweis. Lichtbild und Fingerabdrücke dürfen nur von hoheitlichen Stellen wie z. B. Polizeivollzugsbehörden oder Personalausweisbehörden zur Überprüfung der Echtheit des Ausweises und der Identität des Ausweisinhabers genutzt werden.
missions-th-uder-optional-fingerprints.tr:
Fingerprints
At the applicant’s request, fingerprints can be stored on the identity card. The combination of photo and fingerprints allows a clear assignment between holder and card. Photo and fingerprints may be used only by sovereign authorities such as police enforcement bodies or identity-card authorities to check the authenticity of the card and the holder’s identity.
missions-th-uder-optional-fingerprints.law: For an ordinary new German ID card, PAuswG §5(5),(9) and Regulation (EU) 2025/1208 Article3(5) require two fingerprints. PAuswG §9(3) excludes children below six; §5(9) and the Regulation preserve physical-impossibility exceptions. An ordinary adult without such an exception cannot choose a fingerprint-free permanent card. This is distinct from voluntary use of the online identification function.
missions-th-uder-optional-fingerprints.example: Hypothetical: a 30-year-old German applicant without a physical-impossibility exception applies for a new ordinary ID card in October 2026 and asks to omit fingerprints. The service page offers storage on request; current law makes the biometrics mandatory for that application.
missions-th-uder-optional-fingerprints.context: The page is linked by the current Uder service index and directly from its correct February 2026 fee notice. Its introduction recalls the 2010 launch; complete relevant introductory and biometric sections are retained as historical framing. The operative Fingerabdrücke paragraph uses present-tense optional storage. The claim is limited to currently offered guidance for a new card; existing old cards and online-function choice are separate.
missions-th-uder-optional-fingerprints.scope: Ordinary new permanent German ID card for an adult with no physical-impossibility exception. No allegation that fingerprints are required on all old cards, or for children under six, or that optional online identification use is compulsory.

ctx.quote:
Biometrische Daten
Der neue Personalausweis enthält ein digitales Foto und auf Wunsch zwei digitale Fingerabdrücke. Diese so genannten biometrischen Merkmale dienen ausschließlich den staatlichen Behörden zur sicheren Feststellung Ihrer Identität. Welche Behörden das sind, ist im Gesetz über Personalausweise und den elektronischen Identitätsnachweis festgelegt: Polizeivollzugsbehörden, die Zollverwaltung, die Steuerfahndungsstellen der Länder sowie die Personalausweis-, Pass- und Meldebehörden.
Die für den neuen Personalausweis freiwillig abgegebenen Fingerabdrücke werden im Übrigen nach der Produktion des Ausweises gelöscht und nicht in Datenbanken oder Registern gespeichert. Sie liegen ausschließlich auf dem Ausweis vor. Die Lichtbilder werden wie bisher dezentral in Ihrer Personalausweisbehörde aufgehoben.
ctx.tr:
Biometric data
The new identity card contains a digital photo and, on request, two digital fingerprints. These biometric characteristics serve exclusively to allow government authorities to establish identity reliably. The Identity Card Act specifies those authorities: police enforcement bodies, customs administration, state tax-investigation offices, and identity-card, passport and registration authorities.
Fingerprints given voluntarily for the new identity card are deleted after production and are not stored in databases or registers. They exist solely on the card. Photos continue to be retained locally by the identity-card authority.

Notice: Collection and storage of fingerprints on the identity card takes place on the applicant’s voluntary decision. A decision against storage entails no legal or practical disadvantage. Fingerprints are stored only electronically on the identity card and are not printed on it. They are deleted at the card manufacturer and identity-card authority no later than handover of the card. missions-ljubljana-id-parental-attendanc.claim: requires guardians to attend whenever an applicant is a minor, including 16- and 17-year-old ID-card applicants.
missions-ljubljana-id-parental-attendanc.quote:
Allgemeine Informationen
Die Botschaft ist für die Ausstellung von Pässen und Personalausweisen an deutsche Staatsangehörige, die in Slowenien wohnhaft sind, zuständig.
Die Ausstellung muss persönlich während der Schalterstunden in der Botschaft beantragt werden. Ist die antragstellende Person minderjährig, müssen auch ihre Sorgeberechtigten persönlich in der Botschaft vorsprechen.
missions-ljubljana-id-parental-attendanc.tr:
General information
The embassy is responsible for issuing passports and identity cards to German nationals resident in Slovenia.
Issue must be applied for personally during the embassy’s counter hours. If the applicant is a minor, their persons with parental responsibility must also attend the embassy in person.
missions-ljubljana-id-parental-attendanc.law: PAuswG §9(2) allows legally capable young people aged at least 16 to perform procedural acts under the Identity Card Act. Guardians apply for children below 16; their separate duty to ensure a first application if a 16-year-old fails to apply does not make guardian attendance a universal condition for an older teenager’s own ID-card application. Passport applications have different representation rules.
missions-ljubljana-id-parental-attendanc.example: Hypothetical: a legally capable 17-year-old German resident of Slovenia attends the embassy alone in October 2026 to replace their ID card, with all required identity evidence and an appointment. The blanket minor-attendance instruction calls for a guardian. Under PAuswG §9(2), the teenager may apply personally. This example concerns an ID card, not a passport or travel consent.
missions-ljubljana-id-parental-attendanc.context: The current mission service menu directly links this guide. The general information expressly covers both passports and ID cards and then applies a guardian-attendance condition to minors without an ID-specific age16 qualification. The same page’s download list correctly offers an ID application form for persons over16, retained as countercontext. The page has current2026fee amounts; its capture date is not an asserted publication date. The currently linked additional ID declaration also limits guardian signatures to applicants under16, retained as further countercontext. That PDF has mixed fingerprint wording: its biometrics introduction says on request while the following capture section says mandatory. No fingerprint allegation is made here.
missions-ljubljana-id-parental-attendanc.scope: Legally capable German ID-card applicant aged16–17 at the competent mission; ordinary eligibility, identity evidence and appointment satisfied. No claim about passport applicants, under16s, parental travel consent or actual refusal. The over16/bis16 wording on download labels is not a separate boundary allegation.

missions-kuala-lumpur-schengen-passport-.law: Visa Code Article 12 requires a valid travel document whose validity ordinarily extends at least three months after final intended departure from the Member States, contains at least two blank pages and was issued within the previous ten years. In a justified emergency the three-month obligation may be waived. Ordinary Schengen applications do not require six months after returning to Malaysia; national visas and protected free-movement family travel need separate analysis.
missions-kuala-lumpur-schengen-passport-.example: Hypothetical: a visa-required applicant lawfully resident in Malaysia visits a German spouse who has always lived in Germany, returns directly from Germany to Malaysia on 1 December 2026, and holds a recognised passport issued in2020 with two blank pages and valid until1April2027. Its four-month margin satisfies the ordinary Article 12 validity rule, but the checklist's six-month condition excludes it on that criterion alone. Assume no Directive2004/38 derived free-movement rights and all other application conditions; this does not guarantee visa approval.
missions-kuala-lumpur-schengen-passport-.context: The checklist is for Schengen visas for spouses or parents of German/EU citizens. The main Schengen parent page gives a three-month passport margin, material contradictory guidance. Application essentials say requested documents may vary on individual review; that does not qualify the stated minimum6month passport requirement. missions-kuala-lumpur-schengen-passport-.scope: Confined to ordinary short-stay visa applications within Article 12, e.g. a visa-required spouse visiting a static German national. This is not a claim that every German/EU family case falls under the ordinary Visa Code: qualifying mobile-EU family members have separate entry/facilitation rights. National D visas, the other country's entry conditions, passport recognition, lawful residence, two blank pages and ten-year issue age remain separate. No observed refusal or actual embassy policy inferred. The current parent Schengen page correctly requires only three months after departure. This finding concerns the conflicting family checklist, not uniform mission advice.

missions-luanda-retention-permit.claim: requires a German retention permit before naturalisation in Angola.
missions-luanda-retention-permit.quote:
Wenn Sie sich als Deutscher in Angola einbürgern lassen und Ihre deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit nicht verlieren möchten, müssen Sie vorab eine Beibehaltungsgenehmigung beantragen und ausgehändigt bekommen. Die Bearbeitungsdauer durch das BVA dauert derzeit ca. ein Jahr.

Kernpunkte der Antragsprüfung sind Art und Umfang der fortbestehenden Bindungen an Deutschland und der zu erwartenden Nachteile bei einem Verzicht auf die Einbürgerung in Angola.

Zuständig für die Erteilung von Beibehaltungsgenehmigungen für im Ausland lebende Deutsche ist das Bundesverwaltungsamt in Köln, welches ein Merkblatt zum Verfahren herausgebracht hat.

Wichtig: Wer durch Geburt in Angola die angolanische Staatsangehörigkeit und gleichzeitig durch Abstammung von einem deutschen Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit erworben hat, besitzt beide Staatsangehörigkeiten, ohne dass es eines Antrages auf Einbürgerung oder auf Beibehaltungsgenehmigung bedarf.
missions-luanda-retention-permit.tr:
If you are a German and become naturalised in Angola and do not wish to lose your German nationality, you must apply for and receive a retention permit beforehand. Processing by the BVA (Federal Office of Administration) currently takes about one year.

The key points in examining the application are the nature and extent of continuing ties to Germany and the disadvantages to be expected from foregoing naturalisation in Angola.

The Federal Office of Administration in Cologne is responsible for issuing retention permits for Germans living abroad and has published an information leaflet on the procedure.

Important: A person who acquired Angolan nationality by birth in Angola and simultaneously German nationality through descent from a German parent possesses both nationalities without needing an application for naturalisation or a retention permit.
missions-luanda-retention-permit.law: From 27 June 2024, acquiring a foreign nationality by application does not itself cause loss of German nationality and no German retention permit is required. The 2024 reform repealed StAG §25 through Article 1 No 16, commencing under Article 6(1) three months after publication on 26March2024. Earlier acquisitions remain governed by then-applicable law, other loss grounds remain possible, and Angolan nationality law is separate.
missions-luanda-retention-permit.example: Hypothetical: a German citizen acquires Angolan nationality by application on 20October2026 without obtaining a German retention permit. Assume that Angolan law permits the acquisition without renunciation of German nationality and no independent German loss ground applies. German nationality does not disappear merely because of that acquisition, despite the page's instruction to obtain a permit beforehand.
missions-luanda-retention-permit.context: The entire Beibehaltung section is retained, including the distinct birth/descent dual-nationality exception. The main page is presented as current general service advice, contains no27June2024 cutoff, and remains in the embassy service navigation. The nearby passport checklist requests a retention certificate only 'ggf.'; that conditional evidence request can concern earlier acquisitions and is not independently alleged false.
missions-luanda-retention-permit.scope:
Only foreign nationality acquired on or after 27June2024. The reform does not reverse earlier losses; their application-acquisition, EU/Swiss and retention exceptions require the law at the relevant time. Other German loss grounds remain. This finding concerns German retention law and does not establish eligibility for Angolan nationality or its dual-nationality rules. No actual individual loss or refusal observed.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Luanda: Only foreign nationality acquired on or after27June2024. The reform does not reverse earlier losses; their application-acquisition, EU/Swiss and retention exceptions require the law at the relevant time. Other German loss grounds remain. This finding concerns German retention law and does not establish eligibility for Angolan nationality or its dual-nationality rules. No actual individual loss or refusal observed.

5) Conservação
Se pretende naturalizar-se como alemão em Angola e não quer perder a sua cidadania alemã,  deverá solicitar e obter primeiro uma autorização de conservação. O tempo de processamento deste pedido pelo BVA atualmente leva cerca de um ano.
Os pontos principais da análise do requerimento são o tipo e a dimensão dos vínculos existentes com a Alemanha e as desvantagens a serem esperadas em caso de desistência da naturalização em Angola.
Responsável pela emissão de autorizações de conservação para alemães residentes no estrangeiro é o Bundesverwaltungsamt (Escritório Federal de Administração), que publicou um folheto  sobre o procedimento Bundesverwaltungsamt.

If you intend to become naturalised as a German in Angola and do not want to lose your German citizenship, you must first apply for and obtain permission to retain it. Processing of this application by the BVA currently takes about one year.

missions-cotonou-schengen-window.law: For ordinary Schengen applications, Visa Code Article 9(1) allows lodging no more than six months before the intended visit, ordinarily no later than 15 calendar days before it. Seafarers performing duties have nine months; in justified individual cases of urgency, later lodging may be allowed. The six-month reform applies from 2 February 2020.
missions-cotonou-schengen-window.example: Hypothetical: a Benin resident planning a German holiday starting1June wishes to lodge on 1February, four months ahead. The detail tells them to wait until1March, although ordinary lodging is within the lawful six-month interval. Germany must be competent and the person must satisfy applicable procedural requirements.

Third preparation bullet; lead-in Votre demande passe par les trois étapes suivantes. Parent separately recommends appointment booking no earlier than six months; disclosed counterevidence.
missions-cotonou-schengen-window.scope:
Ordinary short-stay lodging where Germany is the competent main destination; no actual rejection observed. National visas, seafarers and justified urgent late applications have separate rules. The current incoming parent recommends booking an appointment at the earliest six months before travel; the finding concerns this detail's inconsistent three-month lodging rule, not the whole embassy's guidance.

The French current parent recommends booking appointments up to six months before travel; that correct booking text is essential contrary guidance and does not remove the explicit detailed lodging restriction. Six months is ordinary lodging maximum, nine for seafarers; appointments/processing and ordinary15-day advance rule with justified urgent discretion are distinct. missions-san-salvador-kinderreisepass-ad.src: Reisepässe und Personalausweise — Änderung des Wohnorts im Pass
missions-san-salvador-kinderreisepass-ad.claim: offers a change of residence in an abolished Kinderreisepass.
missions-san-salvador-kinderreisepass-ad.quote:
Änderung des Wohnorts im Pass

Wenn Sie Ihren Wohnort gewechselt haben, sollte dies auch im Pass geändert werden. Dies können Sie bei der Botschaft beantragen

Dazu legen Sie folgende Unterlagen vor (Original + Kopie):

• Reisepass/ Kinderreisepass
• Salvadorianische Aufenthaltsgenehmigung (Carnet de Residente)
• sofern ihr letzter Wohnort in Deutschland war oder wenn noch ein Wohnort innerhalb Deutschland im Pass eingetragen ist: Ihre Abmeldebestätigung aus Deutschland
• ausgefüllter Antrag (Antrag auf Änderung des Wohnortes), der erst in der Botschaft unterschrieben wird

Hinweise

Bei minderjährigen Antragstellern müssen die Sorgeberechtigten ebenfalls in der Botschaft vorsprechen und den Antrag unterschreiben.

Der Antrag wird persönlich gestellt. Eine Bevollmächtigung ist nicht möglich.

Die Änderung des Wohnorteintrags ist gebührenfrei.

Für den Passinhaber hat die Korrektur des Wohnorts folgenden Vorteil:

Die Ausstellung eines neuen Reisepasses in der Botschaft wird einfacher, schneller und günstiger, da Rückfragen bei der Passbehörde am letzten Wohnort entfallen.

Eine Anmeldung bei der Botschaft im melderechtlichen Sinn ist nicht möglich, weil das deutsche Melderecht nicht im Ausland gilt. Sie können sich allerdings gerne in die Krisenvorsorgeliste eintragen.
missions-san-salvador-kinderreisepass-ad.tr:
Changing the place of residence in the passport

If you have changed your place of residence, this should also be changed in your passport. You can apply for this at the embassy

To do so, submit the following documents (original + copy):

• Passport/ children's passport (Kinderreisepass)
• Salvadoran residence permit (Carnet de Residente)
• if your last place of residence was in Germany or if a place of residence in Germany is still entered in the passport: your German deregistration confirmation
• completed application (application to change the place of residence), to be signed only at the embassy

Notes

For minor applicants, the persons with parental responsibility must also appear at the embassy and sign the application.

The application is made in person. Authorising a representative is not possible.

Changing the residence entry is free of charge.

Correcting the place of residence has the following advantage for the passport holder:

Issuing a new passport at the embassy becomes easier, faster and cheaper, because enquiries with the passport authority at the previous place of residence are unnecessary.

Registration at the embassy for registration-law purposes is not possible, because German registration law does not apply abroad. You are, however, welcome to enter your details in the crisis-preparedness list.
missions-san-salvador-kinderreisepass-ad.law: The 2023 passport reform abolished issuance, extensions and updates of Kinderreisepässe from 1 January 2024 (BGBl.2023 I No.271, Article 1 and Article 7(3)); PassG §28 preserves the remaining validity of qualifying old documents. The current official PassVwV4.4a and5.4 expressly prohibit change stickers from that date, including changes of the place of residence. The embassy's current section invites an address-change application and lists Kinderreisepass as a document to submit. This is an affirmative offer of an update, rather than merely accepting an old document as identity evidence.
missions-san-salvador-kinderreisepass-ad.example: Hypothetical: in October2026 a German child moves within El Salvador and holds a Kinderreisepass issued in December2020 with a six-year validity ending in December2026. A parent follows the page and requests a residence-entry update in that document. The remaining validity can survive abolition, but the prohibited Kinderreisepass update is unavailable. An ordinary passport or other suitable document is a separate option; the example does not imply any destination must accept the old document.
missions-san-salvador-kinderreisepass-ad.context: The full address-change accordion is quoted, including the ordinary Reisepass alongside Kinderreisepass, parental appearance, personal application and free-of-charge statements. Änderung des Wohnorts im Pass

Wenn Sie Ihren Wohnort gewechselt haben, sollte dies auch im Pass geändert werden. Dies können Sie bei der Botschaft beantragen

• Salvadorianische Aufenthaltsgenehmigung (Carnet de Residente)

Bei minderjährigen Antragstellern müssen die Sorgeberechtigten ebenfalls in der Botschaft vorsprechen und den Antrag unterschreiben.

Changing the place of residence in the passport

If you have changed your place of residence, this should also be changed in your passport. You can apply for this at the embassy

To do so, submit the following documents (original + copy):

• Passport/ children's passport (Kinderreisepass)
• Salvadoran residence permit (Carnet de Residente)
• if your last place of residence was in Germany or if a place of residence in Germany is still entered in the passport: your German deregistration confirmation

For minor applicants, the persons with parental responsibility must also appear at the embassy and sign the application.

missions-conakry-urgent-lodging-bar.law: Visa Code Article 9(1) sets an ordinary latest lodging point of 15 calendar days before the intended visit. In justified individual cases of urgency, the consulate or central authorities may allow applications to be lodged later than 15 calendar days before the intended visit. Guinea Decision 2026/1733 Article 2 suspends specified provisions of Articles 14, 16, 23 and 24, and does not suspend Article 9. Its Article 1 limits its personal scope to Guinean nationals and excludes protected free-movement families. Longer processing requirements do not establish a universal statutory ban on later lodging.
missions-conakry-urgent-lodging-bar.example: Hypothetical: a non-Guinean national lawfully residing in Guinea requests lodging ten days before a short German tourist trip to accompany a terminally ill spouse whose doctor has unexpectedly allowed only an immediate travel window. Assume Germany is competent and the consulate finds justified individual urgency. Article 9 permits later lodging; the page says no application after the deadline will be accepted. This does not guarantee that the consulate will find urgency justified, grant a visa or finish before departure.

missions-conakry-urgent-lodging-bar.scope:
The finding concerns categorical exclusion of all later lodging, including justified individual urgent cases. The ordinary 15-calendar-day rule remains valid. Article 9 creates discretion to allow later lodging, not a universal right to an appointment, urgent visa or approval. missions-valletta-retention-permit.claim: states that acquiring a non-EU/non-Swiss nationality on application automatically loses German nationality without a prior retention permit.
missions-valletta-retention-permit.quote:
Gemäß §25 des Staatsangehörigkeitsgesetzes (StAG) verliert ein Deutscher, der auf Antrag eine ausländische Staatsangehörigkeit erwirbt, grundsätzlich automatisch seine deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit, sofern er nicht vorab die schriftliche Genehmigung zur Beibehaltung der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit („Beibehaltungsgenehmigung“) erhalten hat.

Der automatische Erwerb einer ausländischen Staatsangehörigkeit ohne Antrag führt nicht zum Verlust der deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit. Wer somit durch Geburt eine ausländische und gleichzeitig durch Abstammung von einem deutschen Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit erworben hat, hat beide Staatsangehörigkeiten, ohne dass es eines Antrages auf Beibehaltungsgenehmigung bedarf.

Einbürgerung in Mitgliedsstaaten der Europäischen Union

Seit einer am 28.08.2007 in Kraft getretenen Änderung des Staatsangehörigkeitsgesetzes verliert ein Deutscher seine deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit nicht mehr, wenn er nach diesem Stichtag die Staatsangehörigkeit eines EU-Mitgliedstaates oder der Schweiz erwirbt.

Altfälle sind von dieser Regelung jedoch nicht betroffen. Sollte der Antragserwerb also vor dem 28.08.2007 erfolgt sein, ohne dass eine gültige Beibehaltungsgenehmigung vorlag, hat der automatische Verlust der deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit gem. § 25 StAG weiterhin Bestand. Unter Umständen kann jedoch ein Antrag auf Wiedereinbürgerung gestellt werden.
missions-valletta-retention-permit.tr:
Under section 25 of the Nationality Act (StAG), a German who acquires a foreign nationality on application generally automatically loses German nationality unless they have previously received written permission to retain German nationality (a retention permit).

Automatic acquisition of a foreign nationality without an application does not lead to loss of German nationality. A person who acquired a foreign nationality by birth and simultaneously German nationality by descent from a German parent therefore holds both nationalities without needing to apply for a retention permit.

Naturalisation in Member States of the European Union

Since an amendment to the Nationality Act entered into force on28 August 2007, a German no longer loses German nationality when acquiring the nationality of an EU Member State or Switzerland after that date.

Earlier cases are not covered by that rule. If acquisition on application occurred before28 August 2007 without a valid retention permit, automatic loss of German nationality under section 25 StAG remains effective. In some circumstances, an application for renaturalisation may nevertheless be made.
missions-valletta-retention-permit.law: For foreign nationality acquired on or after 27 June 2024, acquisition by application does not itself cause loss of German nationality and no German retention permit is required. Article 1 No 16 of the 2024 modernisation act repealed StAG § 25, commencing under Article 6(1) three months after publication on 26 March 2024. Earlier acquisitions require the law then applicable; other loss grounds and the other state's nationality law remain separate.
missions-valletta-retention-permit.example: A German resident in Malta acquires Canadian citizenship by application on 20 October 2026 without a German retention permit. Assume no independent German loss ground and no required renunciation. That acquisition itself does not remove German nationality, despite the page's automatic-loss instruction. Canadian law is assumed for the illustration and not assessed here.
missions-valletta-retention-permit.context: The entire Beibehaltung section and following EU/Swiss subsection are quoted. Birth/descent and28 August 2007legacy qualifications are material and preserved. Article date2017 remains but current service navigation still links the page, with no historical-only marker or2024qualification in the full main text.
missions-valletta-retention-permit.scope:
Only the German-law consequence of foreign nationality acquired on or after 27 June 2024. Earlier losses are not retroactively reversed; former EU/Swiss exceptions and permit rules matter for earlier acquisitions. Birth acquisition, other loss grounds and foreign nationality law remain separate. No individual refusal or actual loss observed. The obsolete 2017 article remains accessible from the mission's expanded Service menu. A separate main-body nationality tile on the service landing page points to central AA guidance; this finding concerns the linked legacy article and does not imply every mission pathway gives the same advice.

Additional reviewed publication instance(s) — German Embassy Valletta: Only the German-law consequence of foreign nationality acquired on or after27 June 2024. Earlier losses are not retroactively reversed; former EU/Swiss exceptions and permit rules matter for earlier acquisitions. Birth acquisition, other loss grounds and foreign nationality law remain separate. No individual refusal or actual loss observed. The obsolete 2017 article remains accessible from the mission's expanded Service menu. A separate main-body nationality tile on the service landing page points to central AA guidance; this finding concerns the linked legacy article and does not imply every mission pathway gives the same advice.

missions-kinderreisepass-residence-chang.claim: say a residence change can be entered in a Kinderreisepass.
missions-kinderreisepass-residence-chang.quote:
Wohnortänderung in Ihrem deutschen Reisepass

Wenn Sie nicht mehr in Deutschland gemeldet sind, kann Ihr aserbaidschanischer Wohnort in einen Reisepass, vorläufigen Reisepass, Kinderreisepass oder Kinderausweis eingetragen werden.

Falls Sie nicht persönlich vorsprechen, um Ihre Wohnortänderung eintragen zu lassen, können Sie jemanden bevollmächtigen; er benötigt eine schriftliche Vollmacht und muss ein Identifikationsdokument vorweisen.
Anträge auf Wohnortänderungen können nur nach Terminvereinbarung angenommen werden. Sie dazu die Botschaft über das Kontaktformular.

Folgende Unterlagen sind für die Wohnortänderung notwendig:
• der vollständig in deutscher Sprache und in Druckbuchstaben oder am PC ausgefüllte und unterschriebene Antrag auf Wohnortänderung
• alle derzeit gültigen deutschen Ausweisdokumente (insbesondere Zweitpässe)
• Abmeldebescheinigung des letzten deutschen Meldeortes
• Nachweis des Aufenthaltes in Aserbaidschan (Aufenthaltstitel, Arbeitserlaubnis usw.)

Im Einzelfall können weitere Dokumente nachgefordert werden. Die Eintragung der Wohnortänderung ist gebührenfrei.
missions-kinderreisepass-residence-chang.tr:
Change of place of residence in your German passport

If you are no longer registered in Germany, your Azerbaijani place of residence can be entered in a passport, temporary passport, children’s travel passport (Kinderreisepass) or child identity document (Kinderausweis).

If you do not attend in person to have your place of residence changed, you can authorise someone; they need written authorisation and must present an identity document.
Residence-change applications can only be accepted by appointment. [Contact] the embassy using the contact form.

The following documents are required for the residence change:
• the residence-change application, completed fully in German in block capitals or on a computer and signed
• all currently valid German identity documents (especially second passports)
• deregistration certificate from the last German registered place of residence
• proof of residence in Azerbaijan (residence permit, work permit etc.)

Additional documents may be requested in individual cases. The residence change is entered free of charge.
missions-kinderreisepass-residence-chang.law: Kinderreisepässe may not be newly issued, extended or updated from 1 January 2024. The 2023 passport reform repealed this document and associated procedures, effective under Article 7(3). Current PassVwV 4.4a expressly prohibits change stickers, including residence-change stickers, from that date; 5.4 reiterates the extension/change-sticker prohibition and addresses replacement of invalid documents. PassG §28 preserves qualifying older validity according to the application date, not a right to update an old document. Ordinary passports for children remain available.
missions-kinderreisepass-residence-chang.example: Hypothetical: a child under twelve has a reliably identifiable Kinderreisepass applied for and issued in December 2020, with a six-year expiry in December 2026 and no other invalidity ground. The family moves in October 2026 and requests a new residence-change sticker relying on the webpage. The document may retain its old validity, but a new residence-change sticker is no longer permitted.
missions-kinderreisepass-residence-chang.context: The retained narrative guidance is published by the embassies in Baku, Minsk and Moscow. Complete quoted passages preserve the conditions and proxy/free-of-charge qualifications. Form fields alone no longer support this finding.
missions-kinderreisepass-residence-chang.scope:
Only a new residence-change sticker requested after 1 January 2024 in the abolished Kinderreisepass is challenged. Ordinary passports for children, ordinary passport/identity-card address changes, historical identity evidence, remaining validity under PassG §28 and completion of any grandfathered pre-2024 application are separate. The ban concerns new change stickers; no independent allegation about every possible historical handwritten annotation is made. No actual update, refusal or consular practice was observed.

Baku: the complete German residence-change section expressly includes the Kinderreisepass and retains deregistration, appointment, authorisation, documentary and free-of-charge conditions. Its separate new-passport procedure correctly announces abolition on 1 January 2024 and preserves qualifying old validity. This finding concerns the distinct current residence-change statement, not new issuance or the generic minor form. Kinderausweise are mentioned but are not a separate allegation.

Minsk: the complete Allgemeines section expressly permits entry of a Belarusian residence in a Kinderreisepass if the holder is no longer registered in Germany; the free-of-charge and proxy conditions remain.

Moscow: German and Russian residence-change prose expressly include the child travel document. Russian terminology is identified by the aligned German counterpart. The country guidance expressly covers the embassy and consular offices and includes Moscow appointment/payment options; consulate-only St Petersburg pages are excluded. The separate main minor-passport page correctly announces abolition. The reviewed English translation of the Russian passage is labelled as a translation.

Form selectors and document-number fields alone are excluded by the 21 October 2026 editorial policy. The three retained embassy instances rest on quoted narrative guidance. Shared or translated publications do not establish independent drafting origins. This revision uses the existing 20 October evidence; it is not a fresh live-source check.

missions-eu-family-visa-fee-joining.law: Directive2004/38 Article2(2)(a) includes the spouse. Article3(1) protects qualifying family members accompanying or joining a Union citizen moving to or residing in a Member State other than their nationality. Article5(2) requires necessary entry visas to be issued free of charge. A qualifying spouse travelling to join the mobile EU citizen therefore does not lose the visa-fee exemption solely because they do not travel together. Relationship and protected journey must be proved; a valid Article10residence card may remove the visa requirement. Lawful public-policy/security/health and abuse/fraud grounds remain. External-provider service charges are separate.
missions-eu-family-visa-fee-joining.example: Hypothetical: an Indian citizen lawfully resident in Virginia applies in October2026 for a necessary short-stay entry visa to join her French spouse who has already moved to Germany to work. She supplies genuine marriage evidence, proof of her spouse's French nationality/residence and her joining journey, holds no Article10residence card, and has no public-policy/security/health or fraud issue. She travels on a later flight alone. The visa-fee exemption applies despite not travelling together; the page's 'only if' would wrongly exclude her. Separate BLS service charges are not treated as visa fees. For London: an Indian spouse lawfullyresident in the London consular district travels alone from the UK to join a French spouse alreadyworking/residinginGermany, proves marriage/joining, hasnoArticle10card and meetsprotectedeligibilitywithoutfraud/abuse. TheirseparatejourneydoesnotremoveArticle5(2)freevisa entitlement.

missions-schengen-urgent-lodging-bar.law: Visa Code Article9(1) ordinarily requires lodging at least15calendar days before the intended visit and permits lodging up to six months beforehand (nine for seafarers in performance of duties). That same paragraph permits the consulate or central authorities, in justified individual cases of urgency, to allow lodging later than15calendar days before the intended visit. Article9(3) separately permits urgent lodging without appointment or requires an immediate appointment. The categorical rejection of any such application wrongly rules out the Article9(1) discretion. This does not guarantee acceptance in every case, a decision before travel or visa issuance; Article23processing is distinct.
missions-schengen-urgent-lodging-bar.example: Hypothetical: a visa-required non-Russian resident of Côte d'Ivoire learns of an unforeseen serious illness of a close friend in Germany and seeks to lodge a fully documented visitor application10calendar days before departure. The consulate may permit late lodging in a justified individual urgent case under Article9(1); a categorical statement that every such application will be rejected removes that discretion. The applicant has no automatic right to a visa or guaranteed expedited decision.

missions-eu-family-visa-fee-general-requ.quote:
## Documentos generales – Por favor presentar los documentos en este orden
  * Formulario VIDEX†videx.diplo.de L88:  Importante: Solo aceptamos solicitudes en formato Videx. Nos reservamos el derecho de no aceptar solicitudes en el formato incorrecto.
  * Dos fotos biométricas tamaño: 35x45mm a color con fondo blanco con validez máxima de seis meses.
  * Pasaporte actual, copia del pasaporte (sólo de la página de los datos) y copias de visados schengen o de residencia anteriores (Advertencia: El pasaporte deberá tener una validez de por lo menos 3 meses más que la estadía programada y dos páginas en blanco)
  * Reserva de vuelo a nombre del solicitante (Código de reserva de la aerolínea, no de la agencia de viaje)
  * Seguro Médico Para Visado Schengen (cobertura mínima de 30.000,- Euros sin deducible)
  * Tarifa consular de la solicitud de visado: Deberá pagarse en el momento de presentar la solicitud,en efectivo y en dólares estadounidenses, de acuerdo con el tipo de cambio vigente del día (equivalente a EUR 90,00). Se aceptan únicamente billetes de hasta USD 20,00 de denominación.
## Justificativos acerca del financiamiento y arraigo
  * Para trabajadores en relación de dependencia: Certificado de trabajo (se debe especificar el tiempo de empleo, los ingresos brutos y los días de vacaciones concedidos) y roles de pago de los últimos tres meses.
  * Para estudiantes: certificado vigente del colegio o de la universidad que acredite la matrícula actual. Si el viaje se realiza fuera del período oficial de vacaciones, deberá presentarse adicionalmente un permiso de la institución educativa que autorice la ausencia durante el período de viaje.
  * Para personas independientes pueden presentar RUC, nombramiento y/o tabla de accionistas. No se necesitan las declaraciones del SRI.
  * Para jubilados o pensionistas: Certificado de jubilación del IESS o carnet y tres últimos roles de jubilación.
  * Estados de cuenta bancarios con movimientos bancarios de los últimos tres meses de cuentas corrientes y de ahorro. Los estados de cuenta de tarjetas de crédito son opcionales y, en caso de presentarse, deberán corresponder únicamente al último mes. Los documentos deberán indicar claramente el saldo o cupo disponible y el nombre del titular de la cuenta.En caso de contar con inversiones a plazo fijo, se recomienda presentar también las copias de los documentos correspondientes.
  * En caso de que los fondos personales del solicitante no sean suficientes, podrá presentar una "Garantía Económica Alemana" (Verpflichtungserklärung) emitida por un familiar u otra persona que lo invite y que tenga su domicilio en Alemania. Este es un documento oficial que debe ser solicitado en la Oficina de Extranjería (Ausländerbehörde) más cercana al lugar de residencia en Alemania.Para la solicitud de visa, deberá presentar el documento original de la Verpflichtungserklärung en la Embajada.
De manera excepcional, cuando no sea posible presentar el original, se podrá aceptar una copia del documento.Sin embargo, al momento de viajar, el solicitante deberá llevar consigo el documento original en el equipaje de mano, ya que podrá ser requerido al ingresar al territorio Schengen.
## Justificativos acerca del motivo del viaje

Los justificativos deben ser válidos para toda la estadía en Schengen, no solamente para el período de permanencia en Alemania
### Viajes de negocios

  * Carta(s) de invitación, reserva(s) de hotel o entrada(s) a una feria o evento.En caso de que la empresa cubra los gastos del viaje:
  * Certificado de la empresa en el que se indique que esta asumirá los gastos del viaje.
  * Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) de la empresa.
  * Estados de cuenta bancarios con movimientos de la empresa correspondientes a los últimos tres meses, con indicación de los saldos disponibles.
### Turismo

  * Itinerario detallado del viaje.
  * Reservas de alojamiento (hotel u otros).
  * Reservas o comprobantes de transporte interno, ya sea terrestre o aéreo, cuando corresponda.
  * Entradas o reservas para eventos, museos y otras actividades previstas, de acuerdo con el itinerario planificado.
### Visita de familiares/ amigos

  * Carta de invitación informal, firmada y escrita en alemán
  * Copia de la cedula alemana o titulo de residencia de la persona que invita.
  * Podrá presentar una "Garantía Económica Alemana" (Verpflichtungserklärung) emitida por un familiar u otra persona que lo invite y que tenga su domicilio en Alemania. Este es un documento oficial que debe ser solicitado en la Oficina de Extranjería (Ausländerbehörde) más cercana al lugar de residencia en Alemania.
## Casos excepcionales

  * Cónyuges de ciudadanos alemanes o europeos (provenientes de la UE-/CEE y de ciudadanos suizos): Adicionalmente a los requisitos mencionados arriba, certificado de matrimonio actualizado y copia del pasaporte del cónyuge. No podremos aceptar solicitudes que no cumplan con todos los requsitos que se mencionan en esta página.
  * Ciudadanos no ecuatorianos: Deberán presentarse el visado de residencia vigente y la cédula de identidad para extranjeros.
Se podrán aceptar solicitudes de visado de personas que hayan residido legalmente en Ecuador durante al menos seis meses.
  * Solicitantes menores de 18 años: Deben presentarse acompañados por al menos uno de sus representantes legales. En caso de que sólo se presente una de las partes, deberá estar anexada a la solicitud un poder especial notariado para el trámite de visado firmado y copia de la cédula del representante que no esté presente. No podemos aceptar el documento "Permiso de salida del país". Anexar copias de cédulas y certificado de nacimiento del solicitante de visado.
En caso de haber cedido, suspendido o perdido la patria potestad se debe presentar adicionalmente el extracto judicial en copia certificada a la fecha del juzgado pertinente.
### Info

La Embajada Alemana no podrá recibir solicitudes de visados incompletas. En este caso no se recibirá la solicitud en ventanilla y deberá tomar una nueva cita presentando la documentación completa.

En ciertos casos, la Embajada se reserva el derecho de solicitar mayor documentación de respaldo.
### Info

Aviso Importante:

Por motivos de seguridad, todas las personas que deseen ingresar al edificio Citiplaza deberán dejar en recepción un documento de identidad que no sea necesario para realizar el trámite de visa.

En caso de que la solicitud de visa sea denegada, la tasa de solicitud no será reembolsada, ya que corresponde a una tarifa por gastos administrativos.
Todos los datos de este artículo informativo se basan en conocimientos y valoraciones de la Embajada al momento de la escritura de texto. No se asume responsabilidad por integridad y exactitud, especialmente por cambios interinos.
missions-eu-family-visa-fee-general-requ.tr:
General documents – Please present the documents in this order
• VIDEX form
Important: We accept only applications in Videx format. We reserve the right not to accept applications in the wrong format.
• Two biometric colour photographs,35x45mm, with a white background, no more than six months old.
• Current passport, copy of the passport (data page only) and copies of previous Schengen visas or residence permits (Warning: the passport must be valid for at least3months beyond the planned stay and have two blank pages).
• Flight reservation in the applicant's name (airline booking code, not the travel agency's).
• Schengen visa medical insurance (minimum cover30,000euros without a deductible).
• Consular visa application fee: it must be paid when submitting the application, in cash and in US dollars at the day's prevailing exchange rate (equivalent to EUR90.00). Only notes with a denomination up to USD20.00 are accepted.
Evidence of financing and ties
• Employees: employment certificate (specifying duration of employment, gross income and days of leave granted) and payslips for the last three months.
• Students: current school or university certificate proving enrolment. If the trip is outside the official holiday period, permission for absence during the trip must additionally be provided.
• Self-employed persons may present their RUC, appointment document and/or shareholder list. SRI declarations are not needed.
• Pensioners: IESS retirement certificate or card and the last three pension slips.
• Current/savings bank statements with transactions for the last three months. Credit-card statements are optional and, if presented, must cover only the latest month. Documents must clearly show the balance or available credit and the account holder's name. Term investments should also be evidenced with corresponding copies.
• If the applicant's personal funds are insufficient, they may provide a German financial guarantee (Verpflichtungserklärung) issued by a relative or other inviter domiciled in Germany. This official document must be requested from the nearest foreigners authority in Germany. The original must be presented at the Embassy for the visa application.
Exceptionally, where the original cannot be presented, a copy may be accepted. However, when travelling the applicant must carry the original in hand luggage because it may be requested upon entry to Schengen.
Evidence of the purpose of travel
The evidence must cover the whole Schengen stay, not only the period in Germany.
Business travel
• Invitation letter(s), hotel booking(s) or ticket(s) to a fair/event. If the company covers the travel costs:
• Company certificate stating that it will assume the travel costs.
• The company's RUC.
• Company bank statements with transactions for the last three months and corresponding balances.
Tourism
• Detailed travel itinerary.
• Accommodation bookings (hotel or other).
• Internal transport bookings or receipts, by land or air as appropriate.
• Event/museum/other planned activity tickets or reservations, according to the itinerary.
Visits to family/friends
• Informal signed invitation letter written in German.
• Copy of the inviter's German identity card or residence permit.
• A German financial guarantee (Verpflichtungserklärung) issued by a relative or other inviter domiciled in Germany may be presented. This official document must be requested from the nearest foreigners authority in Germany.
Exceptional cases
• Spouses of German or European citizens (from the EU/EEA and Swiss citizens): In addition to the requirements mentioned above, an up-to-date marriage certificate and a copy of the spouse's passport. We cannot accept applications that do not meet all the requirements mentioned on this page.
• Non-Ecuadorian citizens: the current residence visa and foreigner's identity card must be presented.
Visa applications from people who have resided legally in Ecuador for at least six months may be accepted.
• Applicants under18 must be accompanied by at least one legal representative. If only one is present, a notarised special authorisation for the visa procedure and copy of the absent representative's identity card must be attached. We cannot accept an exit-permission document. Attach copies of identity cards and the applicant's birth certificate.
If parental authority has been transferred, suspended or lost, an up-to-date certified copy of the court record must additionally be presented.
Info
The German Embassy cannot receive incomplete visa applications. In that case the application will not be received at the counter and a new appointment with complete documentation will be necessary.
In certain cases, the Embassy reserves the right to request additional supporting documentation.
Info
Important notice:
For security reasons, everyone wishing to enter the Citiplaza building must leave an identity document not needed for the visa procedure at reception.
If the visa application is refused, the application fee is not refundable because it is a charge for administrative expenses.
All information in this article is based on the Embassy's knowledge and assessments at the time of drafting. No responsibility is assumed for completeness or accuracy, particularly intervening changes.

Article3(1) protects qualifying family members accompanying or joining a Union citizen moving to or residing in a Member State other than their nationality. Article5(2) requires necessary entry visas to be issued free of charge. A qualifying spouse travelling to join the mobile EU citizen therefore does not lose the visa-fee exemption solely because they do not travel together. Relationship and protected journey must be proved; a valid Article10residence card may remove the visa requirement. Lawful public-policy/security/health and abuse/fraud grounds remain.
