rail-snalltaget-night-train-180-minute-t.src: Rights in the event of a delay — night trains
rail-snalltaget-night-train-180-minute-t.claim: Its night-train explanation requires more than 180 minutes of departure delay before treating arrival as expected to be late.
rail-snalltaget-night-train-180-minute-t.quote: If your train is expected to arrive at your final destination at least 60 minutes late, you can choose between the following options: Cancel your journey: Choose not to continue your journey and receive a refund in accordance with the rules for delays. Rebook your journey: Rebook your journey to another departure with Snälltåget. Continue your journey: Continue travelling as planned. If you arrive at least 60 minutes late, you may be entitled to delay compensation. Night trains: As night trains can make up delays during the night, the expected arrival time at the final destination may differ from the delay at departure. For the train to be expected to arrive late at its final station, the delay at departure must therefore be more than 180 minutes. The timetable shown on the most recently issued ticket is compared with the actual arrival time.
rail-snalltaget-night-train-180-minute-t.law: Article 18(1) turns on a reasonable expectation of at least 60 minutes’ delay at the final destination under the transport contract. Recovery time may affect that forecast, but the law does not impose a separate rule that a night train must first be more than 180 minutes late at departure. The stated fixed requirement is too restrictive where the available forecast already establishes the statutory arrival-delay trigger.
rail-snalltaget-night-train-180-minute-t.example: Hypothetical: before departure of a covered Snälltåget night service within the EU, a passenger’s train is 120 minutes late at departure and a reliable operational forecast reasonably puts arrival at their contractual destination 90 minutes late, after allowing for time the train can make up. The passenger booked before the disruption and has not travelled any part. Article 18 requires the immediate choice of reimbursement or comparable continuation/rerouting; the departure delay being below 180 minutes does not postpone that choice.
rail-snalltaget-night-train-180-minute-t.context: The night-train paragraph follows the general statement that an expected final-destination delay of at least 60 minutes permits cancellation, rebooking or continuation. It explains that night trains may recover time, then adds the fixed more-than 180-minute departure requirement. Swedish and English versions match. The current FAQ, reached from the homepage, links this detailed rights page. The general transport conditions § 9.1 instead state the reasonable expected-arrival trigger without a 180-minute night-train proviso; that correct conflicting text is retained.
rail-snalltaget-night-train-180-minute-t.scope: Article 18 refund/rerouting choices on covered long-distance night services within the EU. A departure delay of 60 or 120 minutes alone does not prove eligibility: the reasonable arrival forecast must satisfy Article 18 after realistic recovery time. No finding about actual refused claims or the separate rules for compensation after arrival is made. Exclude Swedish domestic services whose whole operated service route is shorter than 150 km, and services outside the applicable EU scope.

rail-omio-through-ticket-force-majeure.src: Missed train connections in the EU
rail-omio-through-ticket-force-majeure.claim: Adds a force-majeure exception to the full-refund or free-rerouting promise for a single-ticket EU connecting journey.
rail-omio-through-ticket-force-majeure.quote: If your booking includes one single ticket for multiple connections operated by the same EU train operator, then the EU train operator should guarantee your connection by offering you either a full reimbursement or a rerouting option at no additional costs (except in some cases, such as force majeure events). You can find more detailed information about your rights here.
rail-omio-through-ticket-force-majeure.law: The FAQ says that the same EU operator should guarantee a single-ticket connection by offering full reimbursement or rerouting without added cost, then excludes cases such as force majeure. Article 18 retains the reimbursement/rerouting choice when a delay of at least 60 minutes is reasonably expected, including in qualifying extraordinary circumstances. Article 19(10) can remove percentage delay compensation; it does not create the stated exception to reimbursement or rerouting.
rail-omio-through-ticket-force-majeure.example: Hypothetical: a passenger holds a DB through-ticket for Hamburg–Munich via Frankfurt. An extraordinary natural event causes a missed connection and a reasonably expected three-hour final delay. Even if DB proves the Article 19(10) compensation defence, the passenger retains the Article 18 choice of qualifying reimbursement or comparable continuation/rerouting. This does not guarantee a physically unavailable route or an immediate departure during an unsafe event.
rail-omio-through-ticket-force-majeure.context: The current dedicated FAQ displays an update date of 22 June 2026. The same clause is repeated in Omio’s current public disruptions campaign FAQ; these are one drafting family. The next sentence links to Omio’s general EU-rights article, which states the reimbursement/rerouting options without this force-majeure exception. Read that as counterevidence rather than suppress it. Direct original-byte requests returned HTTP 403, so retained captures are explicitly labelled selected web-tool transcripts, not original HTML.
rail-omio-through-ticket-force-majeure.scope: Genuine through-ticket and covered EU long-distance rail service with an expected final delay of at least 60 minutes. The example avoids regional exemptions and separate-contract disputes. Compensation and Article 18 reimbursement are different remedies. The relevant operator still makes necessary arrangements under comparable conditions, and timetable/safety realities may affect the offered routing. The claim concerns Omio’s explanation of carrier duties, not an asserted duty for Omio itself to operate replacement transport or evidence of an actual refusal.

rail-raileurope-retailer-prior-notice.claim: Says a separate-contract statement on tickets or another reproducible document removes the retailer’s refund-plus-75% liability, without also requiring pre-purchase notice.
rail-raileurope-retailer-prior-notice.quote:
Where tickets are purchased in a single commercial transaction and the ticket vendor has combined the tickets on its own initiative, the ticket vendor shall be liable to:

• reimburse the total amount paid for that transaction for the tickets.
• pay compensation equivalent to 75 % of that amount in the event that the passenger misses one or more connections.

Compensation shall be paid within 30 days after the receipt of the request.

This rule will not apply if this is clearly mentioned on the tickets, or on another document or electronically in such a manner that allows the passenger to reproduce the information for future reference, that the tickets represent separate transport contracts.
rail-raileurope-retailer-prior-notice.law: The article first describes the vendor’s reimbursement-plus-75% liability for tickets it combines on its own initiative in one transaction. Its following exception treats a separate-contract statement on the tickets or another reproducible record as enough. Article 12(5) makes two conditions cumulative: that record and information before the passenger bought. A statement first delivered with the tickets after payment cannot by itself remove Article 12(4) liability.
rail-raileurope-retailer-prior-notice.example: Hypothetical: a retailer combines two covered long-distance rail tickets on its own initiative in a single €100 transaction. The customer is not informed before purchase that the legs are separate contracts; the tickets delivered afterwards clearly say so. The passenger misses a connection. Assuming Article 12(4)’s remaining conditions, the retailer owes the €100 ticket-price reimbursement plus €75 compensation. Clear post-purchase ticket wording alone does not remove that liability.
rail-raileurope-retailer-prior-notice.context: The page identifies the EU Rail Passenger Rights Regulation and displays a 5 May 2026 update date. The exception is the last paragraph under What is a Combined ticket, immediately after the total-refund and 75% bullets. It is linked from the current missed-connection help article, which is itself listed in the Get help inventory; those links were followed. Direct original-byte requests were forbidden, so only accurately labelled selected web-tool transcripts are retained.
rail-raileurope-retailer-prior-notice.scope: Only vendor-initiated combinations in a single commercial transaction and an actually missed connection on covered services. The exception is effective where BOTH adequate pre-purchase information and reproducible separate-contract documentation are provided; the seller bears the proof burden. This is not an allegation about a completed Rail Europe booking or its actual notices. It does not turn every separately purchased ticket into a through-ticket or promise free rerouting as the Article 12(4) retailer remedy.

rail-trainline-trenitalia-sixty-minute-b.claim: Pairs a delay of 60 minutes or more with 50% compensation in its Trenitalia table.
rail-trainline-trenitalia-sixty-minute-b.quote:
Train Company | Country | Delay Timetable | Compensation
Trenitalia | 🇮🇹 Italy 🇮🇹 | 30 - 59 Mins; 60 + Mins | 25%; 50%
rail-trainline-trenitalia-sixty-minute-b.law: The table presents Trenitalia’s delay bands as 30–59 minutes for 25%, then 60 minutes or more for 50%. Article 19(1) gives a minimum of 25% at 60–119 minutes and 50% at 120 minutes or more, while allowing greater contractual compensation. The discrepancy is an inaccurate account of the checked standard Trenitalia scheme: its current guidance also uses 25% at 60–119 minutes and 50% at 120 minutes or more. Its separate 25% Frecce bonus for 30–59 minutes is non-cumulative and cannot be added to compensation for longer delays.
rail-trainline-trenitalia-sixty-minute-b.example: Hypothetical: an eligible passenger on a standard €80 Frecciarossa ticket arrives 75 minutes late and has not chosen an Article 18 refund. Assume no Article 19 eligibility defence and no special enhanced promotional arrangement. EU law and Trenitalia’s checked standard policy provide €20. The table’s 50% band suggests €40.
rail-trainline-trenitalia-sixty-minute-b.context: The article is dated 5 August 2024 and remains available at its original URL. The current robots-linked US CMS sitemap still lists that exact URL, but no recent editorial review is inferred. The caption introduces the compensation schedule for delayed trains in Europe; column headers are Train Company, Country, Delay Timetable and Compensation. Original HTML confirms parallel cells with 30–59/60+ and 25%/50%, with no up-to or maximum qualifier. Both the old carrier link in the row and the link in Trainline’s current operator-specific Help article target the same obsolete Trenitalia URL and return 404. The working current Trenitalia policy was independently located and read. Trainline’s linked general-rights Help article correctly states the EU 25%/50% bands; the operator-specific Help article does not repeat the erroneous band but its outgoing carrier link is broken.
rail-trainline-trenitalia-sixty-minute-b.scope: Limit to the table’s general Trenitalia 60–119-minute band and a covered standard journey. EU percentages are minima, so greater contractual compensation is lawful where actually offered; the checked current Trenitalia guidance is needed to establish this discrepancy. Frecce’s 30–59-minute voucher bonus is a separate voluntary right, not a cumulative extra 25%. A 120-minute-or-longer delay may qualify for 50%. This overstates a standard payment rather than establishing passenger harm, actual payout or intent.

rail-bob-international-assistance-48-hou.claim: Says assistance abroad requires 48 hours’ advance notice.
rail-bob-international-assistance-48-hou.quote: Damit sich die Mitarbeiter auf Sie einstellen können, empfehlen wir Ihnen, Ihre Hilfeleistung bei der MSZ bis spätestens 20 Uhr am Vortag der Reise anzumelden. Bei Hilfeleistungen im Ausland sind 48 Stunden Vorlauf erforderlich.
rail-bob-international-assistance-48-hou.tr: So that staff can prepare for you, we recommend registering the assistance you need with the Mobility Service Centre by 20:00 on the day before travel at the latest. Assistance abroad requires 48 hours’ advance notice.
rail-bob-international-assistance-48-hou.law: The page’s domestic recommendation is followed by a categorical 48-hour requirement for assistance abroad through Deutsche Bahn’s Mobility Service Centre. For covered intra-EU rail assistance, Article 24(a) permits 24 hours’ notice. Even the transitional national 36-hour option ended on 30 June 2026. The directly linked current DB page itself says 24 hours abroad. The discrepancy concerns the longer stated notice requirement, not a claim that BOB operates the foreign train or that assistance is unconditional.
rail-bob-international-assistance-48-hou.example: Hypothetical: after 30 June 2026, a disabled passenger who bought a covered Germany–Austria rail journey from the railway undertaking notifies that undertaking’s designated Mobility Service Centre 30 hours before the first assistance is needed. Assume a valid ticket, suitable access and equipment, trained staff on duty and timely presentation at the designated meeting point. This satisfies Article 24(a)’s notice condition. The BOB page’s foreign 48-hour statement incorrectly describes this timely notification as too late.
rail-bob-international-assistance-48-hou.context: The live BOB service menu links this page. It says its own trains have ramps and its drivers help with boarding, then directs readers to DB’s Mobility Service Centre for station assistance. The 48-hour statement follows a domestic recommendation to book by 20:00 the previous day. Its direct DB link now leads to guidance stating 24 hours abroad. This conflicting service-provider guidance is retained; no actual refusal or recent editorial review is inferred.
rail-bob-international-assistance-48-hou.scope: Published German company guidance about assistance on covered international journeys within the EU after 30 June 2026. Does not assess foreign services outside the Regulation, bespoke rolling-stock changes, or voluntary travel-planning extras. Article 23 staffing and access conditions remain necessary, and shorter-notice requests still attract reasonable-effort duties under Article 24(c).

rail-trenord-separate-ticket-contracts.src: Passenger rights and responsibilities — connecting journeys on different tickets
rail-trenord-separate-ticket-contracts.claim: Its passenger-rights pages categorically treat connecting journeys on different tickets as separate contracts, without the single-transaction qualification.
rail-trenord-separate-ticket-contracts.quote: Ai fini dell'applicazione dei diritti e degli obblighi dei passeggeri nel trasporto ferroviario, può essere considerato un unico viaggio quello effettuato con più treni/servizi successivi in forza di un unico titolo di viaggio. In tutti gli altri casi in cui il passeggero utilizza più treni/servizi ferroviari successivi, in virtù di differenti biglietti, i viaggi devono essere considerati distinti e separati tra loro ed ognuno è riconducibile ad un singolo contratto di trasporto. Eventuali indennità saranno riconosciute con riferimento ai singoli contratti di trasporto.
rail-trenord-separate-ticket-contracts.tr: For the application of rail passengers’ rights and obligations, a journey made using several successive trains/services under a single travel document may be considered a single journey. In all other cases where the passenger uses several successive trains/rail services under different tickets, the journeys must be considered distinct and separate, each corresponding to an individual contract of carriage. Any compensation will be recognised by reference to the individual contracts of carriage.
rail-trenord-separate-ticket-contracts.law: The Italian and English passenger-rights summaries first describe a single journey on one travel document, then categorically treat other journeys using different tickets as separate contracts. Article 12(3) covers one ticket or several tickets purchased in a single commercial transaction from a railway undertaking. Under Article 12(5), excluding that liability requires reproducible separate-contract information and notice before purchase. Different tickets alone do not satisfy that exception. The operative conditions contain conflicting terminology and a one-contract/multiple-titles clause; this finding is confined to the clearer website summary.
rail-trenord-separate-ticket-contracts.example: Hypothetical: a passenger buys two connecting covered Trenord regional services in one commercial transaction from Trenord and receives two tickets for a genuine planned connection with a reasonable scheduled change time. Assume no pre-purchase separate-contract warning or corresponding durable disclosure. The first train is delayed and the connection is missed, making arrival at the contractual final destination 90 minutes late. Article 12(3) engages the through-ticket protections in Articles 18–20; issuing two tickets does not by itself split the claim into unrelated contracts.
rail-trenord-separate-ticket-contracts.context: The current Italian and English rights pages repeat the categorical split and cite Regulation 2021/782. Their general May 2023 update label does not establish fresh editorial review. The linked current conditions hub leads to the original 102-page PDF effective 1 September 2026. Its Article 4 uses different titles rather than the websites’ different tickets. Printed page 8 defines title as a transport contract, and page 9 permits one contract to be formalised by one or more titles. Those clauses support a narrower interpretation of the PDF and are substantial counterevidence. The websites do not state the Article 12 single-transaction qualification. No actual booking or claim-handling practice was observed.
rail-trenord-separate-ticket-contracts.scope: Connecting journeys on covered services bought in one commercial transaction directly from a railway undertaking, where Article 12(5)’s information exception is not satisfied. Separate purchases, properly disclosed separate contracts, unconnected journeys and tickets merely gathered by a passenger are outside the example. This does not claim that every multi-ticket purchase is a through-ticket or that the three statutory remedies always produce a payment.

rail-snalltaget-known-delay-refund.claim: Its terms extend the known-before-purchase delay exclusion to the full-ticket repayment in §9.1, although the statutory prior-notice exception concerns percentage delay compensation.
rail-snalltaget-known-delay-refund.quote: Resenär är inte berättigad till ersättning enligt punkt 9.1–9.3 om denne informerats om en försening före inköp av biljett.
rail-snalltaget-known-delay-refund.tr: A passenger is not entitled to compensation under points 9.1–9.3 if informed of a delay before purchasing a ticket.
rail-snalltaget-known-delay-refund.law: Article 18(1)(a) requires the reimbursement option where, at departure, arrival at the contractual final destination is reasonably expected to be at least 60 minutes late. For a journey not begun, choosing that option gives repayment of the unused ticket. Article 19(9) can exclude the separate percentage-of-ticket compensation when the delay was known before purchase; it does not add a prior-knowledge exception to Article 18. Section 9.4.1 expressly reaches §9.1, and the Swedish §9.1(2) itself calls full-ticket repayment ersättning, the noun used in the exclusion. The finding concerns that published monetary-refund cross-reference. It does not claim that all prior disruption information proves an eligible delay, or that a previously advertised arrival time must govern after a valid contractual timetable change.
rail-snalltaget-known-delay-refund.example: Hypothetical: a passenger genuinely buys a valid ticket for a covered Snälltåget long-distance EU service after being warned of a 90-minute operational disruption. The ticket and still-applicable published contractual timetable retain the original arrival time; no revised timetable is incorporated or accepted under § 3.4. At departure, a reliable forecast after recovery time still puts final arrival 90 minutes late. Before travelling any part, the passenger chooses to abandon the journey and asks for the ticket price back. Article 18(1)(a) retains that refund option despite prior notice. This assumes a genuine transport purchase and concerns neither percentage compensation nor private care costs.
rail-snalltaget-known-delay-refund.context: The exclusion is in the current general conditions. The Swedish §9.1(2) describes the full-ticket repayment using ersättning; §9.3 describes people remedied under §9.1 as compensated. The immediately following extraordinary-event exclusion is expressly limited to §9.3, whereas the prior-notice sentence names §§9.1–9.3. The English version uses refund in §9.1(2), but also describes §9.1 recipients as compensated in §9.3 and repeats the wider cross-reference. Material counterevidence remains: the introduction recognises mandatory law; the current delay page gives the ordinary expected-arrival refund choice and confines its prior-notice bullet to delay compensation; and §3.4 provides a mechanism for some preliminary timetable changes. The care-cost allegation has been excluded after the whole-subject review because its express reimbursement promise is in §9.4.2, outside the challenged cross-reference; this is a separately framed refund finding.
rail-snalltaget-known-delay-refund.scope: Published wording about the §9.1 monetary refund for a genuine covered transport contract, where the Article 18 expected delay remains at least 60 minutes against the still-applicable contractual/published timetable. Exclude a validly changed timetable producing no qualifying delay, Swedish domestic services whose whole service route is under 150 km, and non-EU services outside the applicable Regulation. Do not infer actual refusal, intent, universal booking practice, unconditional repayment after travel, care-cost exclusion or entitlement to both repayment and percentage compensation.

rail-interrail-international-assistance-.law: For covered EU international journeys, Article 24(a) requires notice at least 24 hours before assistance is needed. The temporary permission for 36 hours expired on 30 June 2026; it does not support 48 hours in October. At staffed stations with trained staff on duty, timely requested ordinary boarding, transfer and alighting assistance must be ensured. Interrail distinguishes assistance from seat reservations, so its 48-hour assistance entry is broader than a booking deadline. Its disclaimer advises checking with the carrier, whose current DB guidance states 24 hours for assistance abroad. This finding concerns the published country table, not an assertion that DB actually imposes 48 hours.
rail-interrail-international-assistance-.example: Hypothetical: in October 2026, a passenger has already booked an accessible Germany–Austria EU train journey and any required wheelchair space. They give complete notice 25 hours before ordinary boarding assistance is needed at a staffed station with trained staff on duty and arrive at the designated meeting point on time. The Article 24 notice condition is satisfied; the Germany table’s stated 48-hour minimum would tell them otherwise. All access and physical-capacity conditions are assumed met.
rail-interrail-international-assistance-.context: Both current support hubs link these guides. The same guide separates assistance from reservations and warns that carrier information may change; complete disclaimer and explanatory passages are retained. ctx.quote:
Passenger assistance in Europe

If you're embarking on your Interrail adventure with reduced mobility, you can request assistance with boarding and de-boarding the train to make sure you have a smooth experience on board.

Every country and train operator has their own policy for passenger assistance and reservations for people with reduced mobility, so we recommend checking for your relevant country of departure and arrival. The information per country is divided into two parts:

Assistance means that a railway company will assist you by getting into the requested train. It is always good to check each country and train operator about how, when and where to request passenger assistance. If you're a traveller with a disability or reduced mobility and need assistance along the way, you can arrange this assistance directly with the carrier.

Reservations can be made on many trains throughout Europe – there will be links in this page on where to find such information. It is often also possible to book a wheelchair space and a 'companion seat' next to it.

Fahrgast-Unterstützung in Europa

Wenn du dein Interrail-Abenteuer mit eingeschränkter Mobilität antrittst, kannst du Unterstützung beim Ein- und Aussteigen in den Zug anfordern, damit dein Reiseerlebnis sich reibungslos gestaltet.

In jedem Land und für jeden Zugbetreiber gelten eigene Richtlinien für die Unterstützung von Fahrgästen und Reservierungen für Personen mit eingeschränkter Mobilität. Deshalb empfehlen wir, dich über dein Abfahrts- und Ankunftsland zu informieren. Die landesspezifischen Informationen sind zweigeteilt:

Unterstützung bedeutet, dass eine Bahngesellschaft dir beim Einsteigen in den gewünschten Zug behilflich ist. Es ist immer gut, sich in den einzelnen Ländern und bei den einzelnen Zugbetreibern zu informieren, wie, wann und wo man Unterstützung für Fahrgäste anfordern kann. Wenn du als Fahrgast mit einer Behinderung oder eingeschränkter Mobilität unterwegs Unterstützung benötigst, kannst du diese direkt bei der Beförderungsgesellschaft organisieren.

Reservierungen können für viele Züge in ganz Europa vorgenommen werden. Auf dieser Seite findest du Links zu den entsprechenden Informationen. Oft ist es auch möglich, einen Rollstuhlplatz und einen „Begleitsitz“ daneben zu buchen.
ctx.tr:
Passenger assistance in Europe

If you start your Interrail adventure with reduced mobility, you can request help getting on and off the train so that your journey goes smoothly.

Every country and train operator has its own policies for passenger assistance and reservations for people with reduced mobility. We therefore recommend checking your departure and arrival countries. Country information is divided into two parts:

Assistance means that a railway company helps you board the requested train. It is always good to check with individual countries and operators how, when and where to request passenger assistance. If you travel with a disability or reduced mobility and need assistance along the way, you can arrange it directly with the carrier.

Reservations can be made for many trains throughout Europe. This page provides links to the relevant information. It is often also possible to book a wheelchair space and a companion seat next to it.

rail-oebb-easy-language-international-no.claim: States a 36-hour international assistance deadline in its easy-language guide.
rail-oebb-easy-language-international-no.quote:
Wir wollen Ihnen am Bahnhof die beste Unterstützung anbieten.

Darum empfehlen wir Ihnen, sich vor Ihrer Reise anzumelden.

Teilen Sie uns Ihren Reisewunsch mindestens 12 Stunden vor der Abreise mit.

Beginnt ihre Reise vor 9 Uhr, geben Sie uns Ihren Wunsch am Vortag bis 18 Uhr bekannt.

Wenn Sie ins Ausland reisen, geben Sie uns 48 Stunden vor der Abreise Bescheid.

Wie funktioniert die Voranmeldung?

Damit wir Ihnen am Bahnhof die beste Hilfe bieten können, brauchen wir Ihre Voranmeldung.

Wenn Sie in Österreich reisen: Spätestens 12 Stunden vor der Abreise.

Sie fahren schon vor 09:00 Uhr ab? Dann melden Sie Ihren Reisewunsch bitte am Vortag bis 18:00 Uhr bei der Mobilitätsservice-Zentrale an.

Wenn Sie ins Ausland reisen: 36 Stunden vor der Abreise. Das gilt für Reisen nach, von und über Deutschland, Dänemark oder Rumänien.

24 Stunden vor der Abreise bei allen anderen Reisen ins Ausland.

Wenn Sie mit dem Postbus reisen: 2 Werktage vor der Reise.

Nicht als Werktage gelten Sonntag und Feiertage.
rail-oebb-easy-language-international-no.tr:
We want to offer you the best support at the station.

We therefore recommend registering before your journey.

Tell us your travel request at least 12 hours before departure.

If your journey starts before 9 a.m., tell us your request by 6 p.m. on the previous day.

If you travel abroad, let us know 48 hours before departure.

The staff forward your requests to the right place.

How does advance registration work?

So that we can offer you the best help at the station, we need your advance registration.

If you travel within Austria: no later than 12 hours before departure.

Are you leaving before 9 a.m.? Then register your travel request with the Mobility Service Centre by 6 p.m. on the previous day.

If you travel abroad: 36 hours before departure. This applies to journeys to, from and through Germany, Denmark or Romania.

24 hours before departure for all other journeys abroad.

If you travel with Postbus: 2 working days before the journey.

Sundays and public holidays do not count as working days.
rail-oebb-easy-language-international-no.law: Article 24(a) uses at least 24 hours before assistance is needed for covered rail journeys. The temporary permission to extend notification to 36 hours ended on 30 June 2026. Under how advance registration works, the easy-language guide says it needs registration and gives 36 hours for journeys to, from and through Germany, Denmark or Romania; its adjacent 24-hour entry applies only to other international journeys. ÖBB’s current standard service page instead gives 24 hours for all international journeys to or from Austria. The earlier 48-hour paragraph is explicitly introduced as a recommendation and is retained as context, without alleging that it establishes a binding refusal rule. The finding concerns the 36-hour instruction after the temporary extension expired, not actual refusal or a voluntary recommendation to plan earlier.
rail-oebb-easy-language-international-no.example: Hypothetical: a passenger has already booked an accessible Vienna–Munich journey in October 2026, with required seats or wheelchair space confirmed. They notify ordinary assistance needs 25 hours before help is needed at staffed stations with trained staff on duty, provide full journey details and reach each meeting point on time. The statutory notification condition is met, but the easy-language Germany entry still describes 36 hours. No special carriage or Postbus service is requested.
rail-oebb-easy-language-international-no.context: The current accessibility hub and standard mobility page directly link Leichter Lesen. The first paragraph is framed as a recommendation; its 48-hour wording is contextual and unmarked. The subsequent 36-hour advance-registration instruction and current standard 24-hour section are retained in full to show the precise discrepancy. The same easy-language guide later cites repealed Regulation 1371/2007 and its Article 19 as the passenger-rights framework. That complete old-law framing is retained as countercontext. Current navigation makes the guide presently offered; it does not establish recent editorial review.
rail-oebb-easy-language-international-no.scope: Current German easy-language rail guidance, restricted to covered intra-EU international assistance after 30 June 2026. The domestic and Postbus entries are retained for context and are not challenged. Physical access, staffing, available capacity and meeting-point conditions still apply.

rail-odeg-separate-assistance-notificati.quote:
Wir möchten dazu beitragen, Ihre Fahrt mit der ODEG zu einem besonders angenehmen Reiseerlebnis zu machen. Unser kostenfreier Einstiegsservice unterstützt Sie beim Einstieg und sorgt auch während der Fahrt für Ihre Sicherheit.

rail-odeg-separate-assistance-notificati.tr:
We would like to help make your journey with ODEG a particularly pleasant travel experience. Our free boarding service supports you when boarding and also ensures your safety during the journey.

For travel on ODEG trains, please register directly with us. If a section of your journey is operated by another railway undertaking, please contact that railway undertaking.

If you create your journey in DB Navigator or on www.bahn.de, the relevant railway undertakings will be shown.
rail-odeg-separate-assistance-notificati.law: Article 24(a) makes a single notification per journey sufficient and requires the receiving railway, station manager, ticket vendor or tour operator to forward it to all other railway undertakings and station managers involved. ODEG instead tells passengers to register directly with it and contact another railway if that railway operates another part of their journey. The form repeats that instruction while offering a more favourable 120-minute notice period. The discrepancy is the separate-contact instruction for one covered connecting journey, not the shorter period or a claim that all unstaffed facilities must provide every form of assistance. Chapter V assistance rights cannot be removed for covered German regional services through Article 2(8).
rail-odeg-separate-assistance-notificati.example: Hypothetical: a passenger buys one connecting regional rail journey involving ODEG and a second railway. To the relevant railway or ticket seller from which they bought the journey, or the applicable designated notification point, they provide complete assistance and timing details for both legs 25 hours before the first help is needed. Both relevant stations have trained staff on duty, the trains and stations are accessible and any required reservations are already arranged. They reach the designated meeting points on time. One notification satisfies Article 24(a); they do not also have to notify the second railway personally. This does not assume that every operator sells every possible connecting ticket.
rail-odeg-separate-assistance-notificati.context: Current home navigation directly links the assistance form and the Reiseplanung hub; that hub’s current tile links the accessibility guide. The form distinguishes train boarding from station transfer assistance and identifies the station company for transfers; that information is retained. A separate RB37 platform-access problem is not treated as evidence of this legal discrepancy.
rail-odeg-separate-assistance-notificati.scope: One covered connecting German regional rail journey with assistance needs notified through an appropriate channel. Excludes unrelated journeys, urban/suburban services subject to different exemptions, third-country exemptions and special capacity or reservation requests. No finding of actual failed forwarding or denied assistance.

rail-bdz-international-assistance-48-hou.src: Currently linked passenger-rights guidance → complete reduced-mobility unit
rail-bdz-international-assistance-48-hou.claim: still offers guidance requiring 48 hours’ notice for international assistance.
rail-bdz-international-assistance-48-hou.quote:
Railway transport services to passengers must be used by the citizens as a whole. Disabled people, including physically handicapped, have the same right to free movement, freedom of choice and non-discrimination as all other citizens.
The transport servicing of people with reduced mobility is carried out by the station services of the Bulgarian Red Cross at the railway stations of Sofia, Plovdiv, Stara Zagora, Burgas and Varna, and by the Information Desks at the railway stations of Pleven, Cherven bryag, Gorna Oryahovitsa, Yambol and Shumen. It is at these stations or through the telephone numbers shown in the Internet site of the Bulgarian State Railways that orders for organizing their transport are received.
The terms for making the order are the following:
- for carrying out the transport service within the country – at least 24 hours before the traveling;
- for carrying out the transport service outside the country or in the cases of necessity of using combined Train-Automobile transport – at least 48 hours before the traveling;
People with reduced mobility can travel on the territory of the country in certain trains in which there are specialized cars with special seats for people moving in wheelchairs and their accompanying persons. There are toilets in these trains meeting the international requirements.
This category of passengers can also use without any problem the diesel and electrical Desiro multiple units traveling on various routes in the country. Each multiple unit is equipped with a portable folding platform for servicing people with reduced mobility. No preliminary order is necessary for traveling in these trains. The servicing of people with reduced mobility for their getting on and off the train is carried out by the transport personnel.
rail-bdz-international-assistance-48-hou.law: For a covered rail journey wholly within the EU, Regulation 2021/782 Article 24(a) requires notification at least 24 hours before assistance is needed. A permitted extension to 36 hours could not continue beyond 30 June 2026. At a staffed station with trained staff on duty, Article 23(1)(e) requires the notified boarding, connection or alighting assistance. Article 24(c) also requires reasonable efforts without timely notification. The published international 48-hour minimum is longer. This does not require a new special carriage or road transfer, override access/safety rules or promise assistance at an unstaffed location. Article 2 exclusions and current national exemptions do not displace the rule for the specified covered intra-EU service.
rail-bdz-international-assistance-48-hou.example: Hypothetical: in October 2026 a passenger on a covered BDZ international rail service wholly within the EU needs boarding assistance at a staffed station with trained staff on duty. A suitable accessible carriage is already available; no extra coach, road transfer or unavailable reservation is requested. The passenger notifies the relevant railway, station manager or seller from which the ticket was bought 30 hours before assistance is needed and follows the designated meeting arrangements. That meets Article 24(a)’s 24-hour condition, although the currently offered guidance says at least 48 hours. No actual denial or particular timetable is asserted.
rail-bdz-international-assistance-48-hou.context: The current English homepage directly links the Bulgarian rights page, and its Useful information menu leads to an index directly linking the English rights page. The Bulgarian useful-information index also links the Bulgarian page. Both carry explicit 1371/2007 historical legal framing, retained below; their current offered status is distinguished from recent editorial revision. The full reduced-mobility unit retains domestic 24-hour notice and Desiro no-prior-request exceptions. The separate current exemptions hub links Regulation 2021/782 and a November 2024 exemptions matrix; the current July 2026 Commission matrix is retained separately. No claim that every BDZ assistance service applies 48 hours or that the historical law itself was wrong.
rail-bdz-international-assistance-48-hou.scope: Published notice guidance for covered intra-EU international rail assistance, after 30 June 2026. Excludes third-country services, historical/touristic or exempt urban services, adding a special coach, road transfers, reservation availability, unstaffed locations without trained staff and actual office practice. One repeated bilingual drafting origin.

Услугите за железопътен превоз на пътници следва да се ползват от гражданите като цяло. Лицата с увреждания и лицата с ограничена подвижност имат същото право на свободно движение, свобода на избор и недискриминация като останалите граждани.
Транспортно обслужване на лица с ограничена подвижност се извършва чрез гаровите служби на БЧК в железопътните гари София, Пловдив, Стара Загора, Бургас и Варна, както и чрез гишетата "Информация" в железопътните гари Плевен, Червен бряг, Горна Оряховица, Ямбол и Шумен. В тези гари или на посочените на интернет сайта на "ХОЛДИНГ БДЖ" ЕАД телефони се приемат заявки за организиране на превоза. Сроковете за подаване на заявката са следните:
- За извършване на превозната услуга в страната – минимум 24 часа преди пътуването;
- За извършване на превозната услуга в чужбина или при необходимост от ползване на комбиниран транспорт "влак – автомобил"- минимум 48 часа преди пътуването.
Лица с ограничена подвижност могат да пътуват на територията на страната в определени влакове, в които са включени специализирани вагони с обособени места за лица, придвижващи се с инвалидни колички и техните придружители. Във вагоните има изградени санитарни възли, отговарящи на международните стандарти.
Тази категория пътници могат безпроблемно да ползват и дизеловите и електрическите мотриси "Дезиро", които се движат по различни маршрути в страната. Всяка мотриса е оборудвана с подвижна сгъваема платформа за обслужване на лица с намалена подвижност. При пътуване с тези влакове не е необходима предварителна заявка. Обслужването на лицата с намалена подвижност при качване и слизане от влака се извършва от превозния персонал.
versions.tr:
Rail passenger services should be used by citizens as a whole. Persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility have the same right to free movement, freedom of choice and nondiscrimination as other citizens.
Transport assistance for persons with reduced mobility is provided through Bulgarian Red Cross station services in Sofia, Plovdiv, Stara Zagora, Burgas and Varna, and the information counters in Pleven, Cherven Bryag, Gorna Oryahovitsa, Yambol and Shumen. Requests to organise transport are accepted at those stations or at the telephone numbers listed on Holding BDZ’s website. The deadlines for submitting requests are:
- For transport within the country: at least 24 hours before travel;
- For transport abroad, or where combined train–car transport is needed: at least 48 hours before travel.
Persons with reduced mobility can travel within the country on certain trains with specialised carriages containing spaces for wheelchair users and their companions. These carriages have sanitary facilities meeting international requirements.
These passengers can also use the diesel and electric Desiro multiple units running on various domestic routes. Each unit has a portable folding platform for persons with reduced mobility. No advance request is needed for these trains. Train staff assist persons with reduced mobility when boarding and alighting.

INFORMATION
On the enforcement of REGULATION (EC) No 1371/2007 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 October 2007 on rail passengers’ rights and obligations
On 3 December 2009, Regulation (EC) No 1371/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council on rail passengers’ rights and obligations entered into force.
The aim of this Regulation is to guarantee the rights of passengers using rail transport and to improve the quality and efficiency of rail transport services.

ИНФОРМАЦИЯ
за прилагането на Регламент (ЕО) № 1371/2007 НА ЕВРОПЕЙСКИЯ ПАРЛАМЕНТ И НА СЪВЕТА от 23 октомври 2007 г. относно правата и задълженията на пътниците, използващи железопътен транспорт
На 3-ти декември 2009 г. влезе в сила Регламент (ЕО) № 1371/2007 на Европейския парламент и на Съвета относно правата и задълженията на пътниците, използващи железопътен транспорт.
Целта на този регламент е да се гарантират правата на пътниците, използващи железопътен транспорт, както и да се подобрят качеството и ефктивността на услугите за железопътен превоз на пътници.

rail-vr-sweden-english-self-rerouting-de.claim: Its English conditions deny reimbursement for all alternative travel the passenger arranges, despite the conditional 100-minute right.
rail-vr-sweden-english-self-rerouting-de.quote:
b) Alternative carriage eg to the final destination when travelling with VR: In the event the passenger cannot commence or complete his or her journey, or if the journey to the final destination will be delayed by more than 60 minutes and the passenger chooses not to cancel the journey, VR shall, as soon as possible, organize alternative carriage for the passenger. Such carriage may also take place by means of transport that do not belong to VR.
There is no obligation to arrange alternative carriage by taxi.
If alternative carriage cannot be arranged and carried out within a reasonable period of time, VR shall offer the passenger free travel, combined in the same way as the original journey, as soon as possible on the same day or on a later day of the passenger’s choosing.
The passenger is not entitled to compensation for costs of alternative travel arranged by the passenger himself/herself.
rail-vr-sweden-english-self-rerouting-de.law: Article 18(3) of Regulation (EU) 2021/782 gives a passenger the right to arrange alternative public rail, coach or bus transport if rerouting options have not been communicated within 100 minutes of the applicable scheduled departure. Necessary, appropriate and reasonable costs must be reimbursed. A categorical exclusion of all passenger-arranged travel omits that entitlement. The right does not create an unrestricted taxi or flight entitlement.
rail-vr-sweden-english-self-rerouting-de.example: Hypothetical: a passenger with a valid ordinary VR Stockholm–Göteborg ticket faces an expected 90-minute arrival delay. No available rerouting options are communicated within 100 minutes of the scheduled departure. The passenger then buys a necessary, appropriate and reasonably priced public-rail ticket to Göteborg. Article 18(3) requires reimbursement of those reasonable alternative-transport costs; the English final sentence says none is payable. Assume no adequate options were communicated and no duplicate refund.
rail-vr-sweden-english-self-rerouting-de.context: Current guidance opened from live operator navigation on 20 October 2026.
rail-vr-sweden-english-self-rerouting-de.scope: English publication only. The Swedish version of the same current conditions expressly recognises 100-minute public rail/bus self-rerouting, and general clause 2 says mandatory law prevails. This is conflicting published guidance, not proof of current claim-handling policy. The example uses a wholly Swedish Stockholm–Göteborg long-distance service whose entire route exceeds 150 km, outside Lag (2015:953) §4 exemption.

rail-sj-known-delay-refund.claim: Its conditions apply a pre-purchase-known-delay exclusion to disruption ticket reimbursement.
rail-sj-known-delay-refund.quote:
16.1 SJ is liable to refund the passenger all or parts of the ticket fare (price reduction) in respect of quality shortcomings in accordance with 17.1 a).

16.2 In the event of traffic disruptions, SJ shall be liable to refund all or part of the ticket fare in respect of such traffic disruption in accordance with the provisions set forth in section 17.1 b) – d).

16.3 SJ shall not be liable under section 16.2 where the traffic disruption was known to the passenger by virtue of information that he or she received prior to the ticket purchase or if, notwithstanding the traffic disruption or following a rebooking, the passenger arrives at the destination station for the train journey with SJ on time or subject to a delay of less than 60 minutes.
rail-sj-known-delay-refund.law: Article 18(1) of Regulation (EU) 2021/782 requires the qualifying reimbursement or comparable rerouting choice when arrival at the contractual final destination is reasonably expected to be delayed by at least 60 minutes. This finding concerns the explicit extension of the known-delay exception to ticket reimbursement, not the validity of an amended timetable. The comparison is confined to an operational delay of a still-operating train; advance cancellation is excluded in light of the adverse 2015 interpretative guidance disclosed in scope.

The journey has not started and the 90-minute delay remains expected. The passenger then elects Article 18 reimbursement. Assume the contract was not validly changed to a later arrival time and its purpose is no longer served. Percentage delay compensation may be excluded under Article 19(9), but the Article 18 choice remains. The train will still operate; this is an operational delay, not an advance cancellation or artificial booking.

rail-mav-international-delay-bands.claim: Describes the ordinary international compensation bands as more than 60 and more than 120 minutes.
rail-mav-international-delay-bands.quote:
Delays? Missed connections? Passenger right regulations allow to get help and compensation for international journeys within the European Union.

For delays occuring within EU territory – regardless to its reason – passengers are entiltled for a compensation, based ont the price of tickets, reservations and surcharges:
• by 25% at delays more than 60 minutes
• by 50% at delays more than 120 minutes
• The delay is counted on journeys, covered by one contract.
rail-mav-international-delay-bands.law: Article 19(1) requires at least 25% of the ticket price for 60–119 minutes and 50% from 120 minutes. The summary instead says more than 60 and more than 120. Taken literally, exactly 60 receives no stated compensation and exactly 120 remains in the 25% band. This concerns those two boundaries only. Article 19(9) and(10) eligibility/exceptions still apply. The current linked GCC-CIV/PRR 10.2.1 correctly states 60 minutes or more and 120 minutes or more;10.3.3 permits money on request. The contradiction in the public English summary is retained, not treated as proof of incorrect payment practice.
rail-mav-international-delay-bands.example: Hypothetical: a passenger holds a single Budapest–Vienna international ticket on a regular service whose entire route is within Hungary and Austria. The ticket identifies MÁV Személyszállítási Zrt. as contractual carrier for the Hungarian leg. An ordinary operational delay on that leg causes final arrival exactly 60 minutes late, or in the second illustration exactly 120 minutes late. Assume no Article 18 refund and no Article 19(9)–(10) defence. The EU minima are respectively 25% and 50% of the applicable Article 19(3) delayed-service fare; no cross-carrier fare allocation is assumed. The English summary’s more-than thresholds omit those exact boundaries, while the current GCC states them correctly. The current Austria destination page supports the route; the timetable ending 14 October is not used as proof of the assessment-date schedule.

rail-italo-four-euro-money-threshold.src: Transportation contract effective 1 October 2026 — section 17 compensation voucher
rail-italo-four-euro-money-threshold.claim: Refuses money conversion of statutory delay compensation when the amount is exactly €4.
rail-italo-four-euro-money-threshold.quote: Il Passeggero potrà richiedere tramite Sito Internet e il numero 060708 (“Pronto Italo”) la monetizzazione del Voucher da indennizzo, per la quale dovrà fornire il codice del voucher ed il Nominativo associato a tale codice. ITALO, verificata la legittimità della richiesta, procederà con la monetizzazione, che avverrà a mezzo bonifico bancario sulle coordinate, comunicate per iscritto dal Passeggero. La monetizzazione avverrà con valuta in euro ed entro 30 giorni dalla richiesta. ITALO si accollerà esclusivamente le spese relative al bonifico bancario che siano conoscibili al momento dell’effettuazione dello stesso. Non potrà essere chiesta la monetizzazione del Voucher da indennizzo nel caso in cui il relativo importo sia pari o inferiore ad euro 4,00.
rail-italo-four-euro-money-threshold.tr: The Passenger may request conversion of the compensation voucher to money through the Website and number 060708 (“Pronto Italo”), for which the voucher code and the name associated with that code must be provided. After verifying that the request is legitimate, ITALO will convert it to money by bank transfer to the account details communicated in writing by the Passenger. Conversion will be in euros within 30 days of the request. ITALO will bear only bank-transfer charges known when making the transfer. Conversion of the compensation voucher to money cannot be requested where its amount is equal to or less than €4.00.
rail-italo-four-euro-money-threshold.law: Article 19(7) of Regulation 2021/782 requires eligible delay compensation to be paid in money on the passenger’s request. Article 19(8) permits a minimum threshold below which compensation is not paid, but that threshold may not exceed EUR 4. A compensation amount exactly EUR 4 cannot be excluded from money payment under that permission. Current section 16.4 routes non-wallet passengers’ statutory delay compensation into the section 17 voucher; section 17 then excludes conversion at an amount equal to EUR 4. Italy has no listed relevant domestic long-distance exemption. This concerns the original full statutory amount, not a small residue after spending a voucher.
rail-italo-four-euro-money-threshold.example: Hypothetical: a passenger pays €16 for a domestic Rome–Florence Italo high-speed ticket and arrives 75 minutes late. Assume no reimbursement under Article 18, no Article 19(9)–(10) exception, a valid request, no Italo Wallet membership, an unused full compensation voucher and a request for money. The 25% amount is exactly €4. Article 19(7)–(8) preserves money on request at that amount; section 17 says conversion cannot be requested for €4 or less.
rail-italo-four-euro-money-threshold.context: The current terms hub expressly links contract rel 610, valid from 1 October 2026. Section 16.3 correctly states the bands and exceptions; section 16.4 routes statutory compensation for passengers without the wallet into section 17 vouchers. Section 17 generally permits conversion to bank money and denies conversion only at €4 or below. No allegation that issuing credit first or using bank transfer is itself unlawful.
rail-italo-four-euro-money-threshold.scope: Eligible original statutory delay compensation exactly €4 on Italian domestic long-distance rail, requested in money. Excludes voluntary goodwill, voucher residue after use, other credit, refunded journeys and Article 19 defences. Money is required on request, not automatically. This records published wording; actual handling is not established. Section 16.4 routes compensation for non-Wallet customers to a voucher; the challenged rule is refusal to convert the entire unused statutory €4 voucher into money on request, rather than automatic voucher issuance or a €4 residue after partial use.

rail-eurostar-continental-force-majeure-.pub: THI Factory SA / Eurostar Continental Routes
rail-eurostar-continental-force-majeure-.src: Eurostar Continental Routes conditions of carriage, §2.8.3.4
rail-eurostar-continental-force-majeure-.claim: Continental conditions expressly deny the Article 18 rerouting and Article 20 assistance duties for listed CIV exonerating causes.
rail-eurostar-continental-force-majeure-.quote:
2.8.3.4 Rerouting and assistance

Pursuant to article 32 RU CIV (specific legal regime of rail transport law on exonerating causes), also appended to the PRR, Carriers are not legally bound to reroute or assist Passengers, as defined by articles 18 and 20 PRR, when the delay, missed connection or cancellation is due to one of the following causes:
1. circumstances beyond the control of the railway operations which the Carrier, despite due diligence in the particular circumstances of the case, could not avoid and the consequences of which it was unable to prevent, or
2. an error by the Passenger, or
3. the behaviour of a third party which the Carrier, despite due diligence in the particular circumstances of the case, could not avoid and the consequences of which it was unable to prevent. Other companies using the same rail infrastructure are not considered to be third parties. The right to appeal is not affected.
rail-eurostar-continental-force-majeure-.law: Articles 18 and 20 of Regulation (EU) 2021/782 retain qualifying reimbursement/rerouting and care rights despite an Article 19(10) exception from percentage compensation. CIV Article 32 defences against consequential actual-loss liability do not remove the explicit Article 18 and 20 duties. Necessary overnight accommodation and station transfers remain due where physically possible; a three-night accommodation limit is permitted only in the circumstances specified by Article 20(2)(b), not a total abolition of assistance. Article 7 prevents contractual waiver of the Regulation’s obligations.
rail-eurostar-continental-force-majeure-.example: Hypothetical: a passenger holds a direct Paris–Brussels ticket on a THI Factory continental service wholly within the EU. An extraordinary storm, which could qualify for the Article 19(10) compensation exception, cancels the train. Arrival is reasonably expected to be delayed at least 60 minutes; comparable continuation is available only next morning, an overnight stay is necessary, and hotel accommodation and station transfers are physically possible. Article 18 choices and Article 20 care remain due, subject to their conditions and any applicable three-night accommodation limit. The cited paragraph instead denies a legal duty under both articles. Assume no passenger fault and no refund election that makes overnight care unnecessary.
rail-eurostar-continental-force-majeure-.context: Current official publication and its incoming navigation checked 20 October 2026. Conflicting or qualifying guidance is displayed in scope.
rail-eurostar-continental-force-majeure-.scope: Specific express contractual denial, alongside conflicting favourable guidance: the current generic Eurostar rights page promises necessary and adequate accommodation/snacks where necessary and materially possible, and the contract hierarchy gives the PRR priority. Both must remain visible; the case concerns misleading conflicting publication, not demonstrated claim handling. The Paris–Brussels example is THI Factory carriage in France and Belgium, with no UK/Swiss segment; the July 2026 Commission table shows no relevant FR/BE exemption. EIL’s separate London Routes contract is not the same wording. No unrestricted self-booked taxi/flight or unlimited hotel entitlement is inferred. Section 2.8.3.1 separately sets out ordinary reimbursement and earliest/later rerouting choices. Necessary care remains subject to Article 20 availability and physical possibility, including the permitted three-night accommodation limit only in the specified Article 19(10) circumstances.

rail-sz-announced-own-staff-strike-compe.src: SŽ passenger conditions, §5.2 compensation and exclusions
rail-sz-announced-own-staff-strike-compe.claim: Its current own GCC/PRR summary excludes delay compensation for an announced strike by the carrier’s staff.
rail-sz-announced-own-staff-strike-compe.quote:
5.2. Nadomestilo za zamudo

Vsak potnik, ki ima zaradi zamude vlaka ob prihodu v namembno postajo, če je zamuda nastala na območju EU, v Švici ali na Norveškem, pravico do nadomestila:

 • 25% cene za relacijo, kjer je zamuda nastala, kadar vlak zamuja od 60 min do 119 minut
 • 50% cene za relacijo, kjer je zamuda nastala, kadar vlak zamuja 120 minut ali več

Zahtevek za nadomestilo se lahko vloži pri kateremkoli v prevozu sodelujočem prevozniku, rešuje pa ga tisti prevoznik, ki je vozovnico izdal.

Izključitev odgovornosti prevoznika

Pravice do kompenzacije potnik nima:
 • če je bil pred nakupom vozovnice obveščen o pričakovani zamudi
 • kadar mu je bil zagotovljen nadomestni prevoz, tako da je ob prihodu v namembno postajo zamuda znašala manj kot 60 minut
 • če je bil prevoz v celoti ali deloma opravljen izven EU
 • če je zamuda nastala zaradi okoliščin, ki niso povezane z železniškim prometom in se jim prevoznik kljub ustreznim varnostnim ukrepom ni mogel izogniti, njihovih posledic pa ne preprečiti
 • če je zamuda nastala po krivdi potnika ali tretje osebe
 • v primeru napovedane stavke osebja prevoznika
rail-sz-announced-own-staff-strike-compe.tr:
5.2. Compensation for delay

Every passenger has the right to compensation because of a train delay on arrival at the destination station if the delay arose within the EU, Switzerland or Norway:
• 25% of the price for the route where the delay arose, when the train is delayed from 60 to 119 minutes
• 50% of the price for the route where the delay arose, when the train is delayed 120 minutes or more

A compensation request may be filed with any carrier participating in the carriage, but it is handled by the carrier that issued the ticket.

Exclusion of carrier liability

The passenger has no right to compensation:
• if informed of the expected delay before buying the ticket
• where alternative transport was provided so that the delay on arrival at the destination station was less than 60 minutes
• if the carriage was performed wholly or partly outside the EU
• if the delay arose from circumstances unconnected with railway traffic which the carrier, despite appropriate safety measures, could not avoid and whose consequences it could not prevent
• if the delay arose through the fault of the passenger or a third party
• in the event of an announced strike by the carrier’s staff
rail-sz-announced-own-staff-strike-compe.law: Article 19(1) of Regulation (EU) 2021/782 gives the ordinary minimum 25% compensation for 60–119 minutes and 50% for 120 minutes or more. Article 19(10) expressly excludes strikes by the railway undertaking’s own personnel from its third-party compensation defence. Announcement alone does not create an exception. Article 19(9) separately permits refusal where the passenger knew about the delay before buying the ticket; the hypothetical therefore assumes purchase before that information became known. Article 7 prevents less favourable contractual waiver.
rail-sz-announced-own-staff-strike-compe.example: Hypothetical: a passenger buys a valid €40 SŽ Ljubljana–Maribor InterCity ticket before a later announcement of an SŽ staff strike. The covered wholly Slovenian train arrives 90 minutes late because of that strike. Assume no pre-purchase knowledge of the delay, no other Article 19 exception and no Article 18 ticket reimbursement. Ordinary minimum compensation is 25%, or €10. The announced-own-staff-strike bullet says no compensation is due.
rail-sz-announced-own-staff-strike-compe.context: Current official publication and its incoming navigation checked 20 October 2026. Conflicting or qualifying guidance is displayed in scope.
rail-sz-announced-own-staff-strike-compe.scope: The source’s first page expressly applies the regime to both international and domestic SŽ traffic. The current domestic tariff effective 1 July 2026 refers delay claims to the Regulation and GCC/PRR. The full §5.2 exclusions are displayed, including the separate pre-purchase knowledge exception. Other current SŽ material, including the claim form, correctly states 25%/50% and money payment; this is a specific contradictory exception, not an allegation that all staff-strike claims are refused. Example assumes an ordinary operating IC service and unchanged contractual arrival, not a timetable already revised before purchase. Slovenia has no relevant exemption entry in the July 2026 Commission table; regional-only and non-EU journeys are not used. The current Slovenian Railway Transport Act informational consolidation, effective 14 March 2026, applies EU duties and penalises Article 19 non-payment; no applicable InterCity exemption was located.

banking-isybank-residence.claim: says its statutory basic account is only for residents of Italy.
banking-isybank-residence.quote: Il Conto di Base isybank, come tutti gli altri prodotti, è dedicato ai soli residenti in Italia.
banking-isybank-residence.tr: The isybank Basic Account, like all its other products, is intended only for residents of Italy.
banking-isybank-residence.law: Italy’s Banking Act gives consumers legally resident in the EU a right to a basic account regardless of where they live. Article 126-vicies permits refusal for the statutory eligibility and existing Italian payment-account grounds, subject to anti-money-laundering rules. Residence in another EU country is not itself a ground for refusal.
banking-isybank-residence.example: Hypothetical: A consumer legally resident in France, with no payment account in Italy, applies for a basic account and meets the identification and anti-money-laundering requirements. The published Italy-only restriction excludes that person even though living in France does not itself remove the statutory right.
banking-isybank-residence.context: The product page identifies this as the statutory Conto di Base and links it from the bank’s current account menu. Its application instructions also ask applicants to declare lawful stay in the EU. That broader declaration does not explain the page’s express Italy-only restriction; the linked information sheet dated 12 October 2026 repeats that account and card contracts are reserved for Italian residents (page 4). These are publications by the same bank, not independent drafting origins. The official Italian law capture is a March 2025 consolidation; the 2017 enactment and the regulator’s 19 August 2026 explanation were also checked. The live Normattiva article endpoint was unavailable. The Bank of Italy’s supervisory explanation published 5 August 2026 expressly confirms that the duty extends to lawful residents across the EU; its 30 November 2026 internal review deadline does not postpone the underlying statutory entitlement.
banking-isybank-residence.scope: Italian statutory basic accounts, reviewed on 18 October 2026. The right is for consumers legally resident in the EU and remains subject to identification and anti-money-laundering checks. An existing qualifying payment account in Italy can justify refusal, with switching and notice-of-closure exceptions. This is a finding about published eligibility wording; no actual application or refusal was tested. Standard accounts need not have identical conditions, and the basic account is not necessarily free.

banking-caixa-popular-obsolete-free-acco.src: Cuenta de Pago Básica — vulnerability criteria
banking-caixa-popular-obsolete-free-acco.claim: uses income limits for a free basic account that were raised in December 2022.
banking-caixa-popular-obsolete-free-acco.quote: Criterios que determinan la situación de vulnerabilidad o de riesgo de exclusión social Para determinar esta situaciones, se evaluará la renta y el número de miembros de la unidad familiar utilizando el Indicador de Rentas de Efectos Múltiples (IPREM). Se considerará dentro de este colectivo al cliente que no supere los siguientes umbrales: Personas no integradas en ninguna unidad familiar : ingresos inferiores a dos veces el indicador público de renta. Personas integradas en una unidad familiar con menos de cuatro miembros : ingresos inferiores a dos veces y media el indicador público de renta. Personas integradas en unidades familiares compuestas por cuatro o más miembros , o que tengan reconocida su condición de familia numerosa: ingresos inferiores a tres veces el indicador público de renta. Personas integradas en unidades familiares que tengan en su seno a una persona con grado de discapacidad igual o superior al 33% (reconocido oficialmente por resolución expedida por el Instituto de Mayores y Servicios Sociales o por el órgano competente de la Comunidad Autónoma en la que reside): ingresos inferiores a tres veces el indicador público de renta. Si alguno de los titulares fuese víctima de trata o explotación sexual , quedará exento de cumplir los requisitos anteriores de ingresos económicos brutos, computados anualmente y por unidad familiar. Esta situación podrá acreditarse a través del modelo unificado de acreditación expedido por los servicios sociales o entidad especializada en la materia. Además de lo anterior, se requiere que: No concurran titularidad, directa o indirecta, o derecho real alguno sobre bienes inmuebles , excluida la vivienda habitual. Ni sean titulares reales de sociedades mercantiles , por parte de ninguno de los miembros que integren la unidad familiar.
banking-caixa-popular-obsolete-free-acco.tr: Criteria determining vulnerability or risk of social exclusion. To determine these situations, income and the number of family members will be assessed using the Multiple Effects Income Indicator (IPREM). Customers who do not exceed the following thresholds will be included: people outside a family unit: income below twice the public income indicator. People in a family unit with fewer than four members: income below two and a half times the public income indicator. People in family units with four or more members, or recognised as a large family: income below three times the public income indicator. People in family units with a person with a disability of 33% or more (officially recognised by a decision of the Institute for Older Persons and Social Services or the competent body of their autonomous community): income below three times the public income indicator. If any holder is a victim of trafficking or sexual exploitation, they are exempt from the preceding gross annual household income requirements. This may be proved using the standard accreditation form issued by social services or a specialist organisation. In addition: no family member may have direct or indirect ownership or any real right over immovable property, excluding the main home, or be a beneficial owner of a commercial company.
banking-caixa-popular-obsolete-free-acco.law: Real Decreto 164/2019 Article 3(1)(a), amended by Real Decreto-ley 20/2022 Article 75 from 28 December 2022, sets ceilings of 3, 3.5 and 4 times the twelve-payment IPREM. Caixa Popular instead uses the earlier 2, 2.5 and 3 multipliers. The ordinary asset test, all account holders and authorised persons, application and proof requirements still apply. This is Spain’s enhanced fee regime under Directive Article 18(4), not an EU-wide income ceiling.
banking-caixa-popular-obsolete-free-acco.example: Hypothetical: A sole holder, with no authorised persons and outside any family unit, has annual gross income equal to 2.5 times the applicable annual twelve-payment IPREM. Assume they meet basic-account eligibility, have no disqualifying property or company ownership and submit complete proof and an application for the fee exemption. Their income is within the legal 3-times ceiling but exceeds the page’s 2-times ceiling. No euro IPREM figure or guaranteed remedy is inferred.
banking-caixa-popular-obsolete-free-acco.context: The current product page expressly makes the account free for vulnerability and then lists all four earlier income ceilings. It separately explains the asset test and the trafficking/sexual-exploitation route. The currently linked document labelled precontractual is a 2019 zero-fee information document headed Banco Cooperativo Español; it gives fees and does not correct the income criteria.
banking-caixa-popular-obsolete-free-acco.scope: Eligibility for Spain’s fee exemption for covered basic-account services. This finding does not treat vulnerability as necessary for opening the ordinary fee-paying basic account, and does not claim that all transactions outside the statutory service/quantity limits must be free. Published guidance only; no actual application decision, charging, harm or intent established. Selected sources do not establish a population error rate.

banking-bnf-standard-account-eligibility.src: Basic Payment Account · Who Can Open a Basic Payment Account?
banking-bnf-standard-account-eligibility.claim: limits the basic account to people who are ineligible for a standard deposit account.
banking-bnf-standard-account-eligibility.quote:
Who Can Open a Basic Payment Account?
EU residents
You can only open a Basic Payment Account if you don’t have another account with similar features with another bank in Malta and are not eligible for a Standard Deposit Account.
banking-bnf-standard-account-eligibility.law: MFSA R.5.6.144 establishes eligibility for lawful residents of Malta or another Member State. R.5.6.146 permits genuine-interest checks, R.5.6.147 addresses an existing equivalent Payment Account with a closure-notice exception, R.5.6.148 prohibits refusal based on financial circumstances, and R.5.6.153 requires AML/CFT refusal. R.5.6.151 also prohibits burdensome restrictions dissuading exercise of the right. Eligibility for a commercial standard deposit account is not an additional exclusion from the basic-account right. These are the current 6 October 2026 Rules under L.N.258/2026 Reg.44, with repeal and transition in Regs.57–58; S.L.371.18 is historical.
banking-bnf-standard-account-eligibility.example: Hypothetical: An adult legally resident in Malta has no equivalent Maltese payment account, needs ordinary daily banking and passes the required identity and anti-money-laundering checks. Even if BNF would accept them for its standard deposit account, that fact alone does not remove their right to choose the basic account.
banking-bnf-standard-account-eligibility.context: The disputed sentence appears under the basic account eligibility heading. The linked April 2025 terms use EU/Member State residence and an equivalent-existing-account rule, including closure notice, without the standard-deposit-account condition. Those terms qualify any conclusion about the contract or actual processing.

banking-crelan-unindexed-asset-ceiling.src: Basisbankdienst · Voor wie is de basisbankdienst bestemd?
banking-crelan-unindexed-asset-ceiling.claim: still sets the savings ceiling at €10,000 instead of the indexed 2026 ceiling of €10,239.43.
banking-crelan-unindexed-asset-ceiling.tr: You qualify for a basic banking service if you meet the following conditions: you are a natural person; you use the current account solely for private purposes; you reside legally in an EU Member State, or you have Belgian nationality, reside outside a Member State and were removed from the Belgian population register no more than ten years ago; you do not have a current account or basic banking service at another credit institution in Belgium; you have no more than 10,000 euros in debts or funds in an account at another bank.
banking-crelan-unindexed-asset-ceiling.law: Belgium permits an asset-based refusal where the relevant cumulative average annual credit balance exceeds the statutory ceiling, excluding the specified rental guarantees. The Royal Decree of 17 July 2024 raised the base amount from €6,000 to €10,000 from 1 December 2024 and introduced annual indexation. The official Gazette notice 2025009110 fixes €10,239.43 from 1 January 2026 under CDE VII.59 § 1 and § 2. Thus a balance above €10,000 but below €10,239.43 is not by itself this refusal ground. A qualifying lawful-residence status, no usable equivalent Belgian payment account (subject to closure notice), and AML/identity requirements remain necessary. This finding addresses savings balances only, not the separate treatment of consumer-credit contracts.
banking-crelan-unindexed-asset-ceiling.example: Hypothetical: An adult consumer lawfully resident in Belgium has no payment account in Belgium, no credit contracts and one Belgian savings account that does not provide the equivalent everyday payment services with a constant balance of €10,200 throughout the relevant year. The consumer satisfies identity and AML checks and all other statutory conditions. The average annual savings balance is €10,200, which exceeds the page’s €10,000 ceiling but is below the effective 2026 ceiling of €10,239.43; that balance alone cannot justify refusal.
banking-crelan-unindexed-asset-ceiling.context: The product page introduces these as the conditions which must be met. Its current account-listing navigation links the statutory Basisbankdienst page. The directly linked information sheet dated 29 November 2024 also requires a cumulative average annual balance no greater than €10,000 (rental deposit excluded), calls these statutory conditions, and says Crelan will refuse if the conditions are unmet. The directly linked application incorporates that information sheet. Neither checked document states indexation of the asset ceiling.
banking-crelan-unindexed-asset-ceiling.scope: Finding restricted to Crelan’s published Dutch statutory-account savings guidance accessed 18 October 2026. No allegation about the separate credit-contract criterion, actual refusals, harm or intent.

ctx.quote: Wijzigingen aan uw account Als uw basisbankdienstrekening niet langer geschikt is voor uw behoeften of als u niet langer in aanmerking komt voor de basisbankdienstrekening, kunt u contact met ons opnemen via de Revolut-app. U heeft dan twee opties: u kunt overstappen van uw basisbankdienstrekening (d.w.z. een rekening met basisfuncties) naar een gewone Revolut-rekening; of u kunt uw basisbankdienstrekening volledig afsluiten. U hebt niet de mogelijkheid om uw basisbankdienstrekening volledig af te sluiten als u een aparte overeenkomst met ons of een andere Revolut-onderneming bent aangegaan die vereist dat u uw persoonlijke rekening bij ons openhoudt totdat die andere overeenkomst wordt beëindigd (bijv. een persoonlijke lening). In die omstandigheden zal alleen de optie om uw basisbankdienstrekening om te wisselen voor u beschikbaar zijn. Overstappen naar een standaard Revolut rekening Als u overstapt naar een standaard Revolut rekening, zullen kosten en vergoedingen van toepassing zijn in overeenstemming met de informatie over de vergoedingen op onze webpagina voor België. Wij zullen uw basisbankdienstrekening overschakelen naar een standaard Revolut rekening met een opzegtermijn van twee maanden in de volgende omstandigheden: u heeft meer dan 10.000 euro aan geaccumuleerd jaarlijks tegoed. U kunt voorkomen dat wij u omschakelen naar een standaard Revolut account door binnen deze opzegtermijn contact met ons op te nemen om uw basisbankdienstrekening volledig te sluiten (tenzij wij uw rekening niet kunnen sluiten zoals beschreven in deze voorwaarden).
