groups.title: Airlines
groups.who: Airlines selling flights to and from EU airports

qs.title: Hotel and meals
qs.q: Does the airline offer a hotel when you are stranded overnight, even if the cause was outside its control?
qs.law: Free hotel and transfers when a night's stay becomes necessary, even if the cause was extraordinary. After a cancellation or delay, this applies when the new departure is expected the day after or later.
qs.lawText: An airline must offer a hotel and transport between the airport and the hotel, free of charge, where a stay of one or more nights, or a stay additional to the one the passenger intended, becomes necessary (Art. 9(1)(b)-(c)). Meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to the waiting time and two calls or messages come with it (Art. 9(1)(a), 9(2)). Passengers denied boarding against their will are owed this with no day-after condition (Art. 4(3)). After a cancellation, a hotel is owed when the passenger is rerouted and the new flight is expected to leave at least the day after the planned departure (Art. 5(1)(b)). After a delay, it is owed when the airline reasonably expects a delay of two, three or four hours or more (by distance) and a departure at least the day after the announced time (Art. 6(1)(ii)). The extraordinary-circumstances defence in Art. 5(3) frees the airline only from paying compensation under Art. 7. Art. 9 contains no such exception, so a cause outside the airline's control does not remove the right to a hotel; the Court of Justice confirmed this for cancellations caused by the 2010 volcanic ash cloud (McDonagh, C-12/11).

qs.title: Refunds
qs.q: After a delay of five hours or more, does the airline explain your right to a refund?
qs.law: Delay of at least five hours (exactly five counts): the airline must offer a refund of the unused flights, paid within 7 days. From two hours' delay it must also hand over a written notice of your rights.
qs.lawText: When an airline reasonably expects a flight to leave at least five hours late, it must offer the passengers reimbursement (Art. 6(1)(iii)). Under Art. 8(1)(a) this is the full ticket price for the parts of the journey not made, paid within seven days in cash, by electronic bank transfer, bank orders or bank cheques (a voucher only with the passenger's signed agreement, Art. 7(3)). Parts already flown are refunded too, but only if the flight no longer serves any purpose in relation to the passenger's original travel plan. Where relevant, the airline must also offer a return flight to the first point of departure at the earliest opportunity. The five-hour mark is the same for every distance. The shorter two-, three- and four-hour limits (by distance) trigger care instead: meals, refreshments and two calls or messages, plus a hotel if the departure is expected the day after the announced time (Art. 6(1)(i)-(ii)). The extraordinary-circumstances defence in Art. 5(3) names compensation under Art. 7 only; Arts 6 and 8 contain no such exception. The rules cover passengers departing from an EU airport, and from a non-EU airport to the EU on an EU carrier unless they already received benefits or compensation and were given assistance there (Art. 3(1)); passengers need a confirmed reservation and, for a delay, a timely check-in (Art. 3(2)). The airline must give every passenger delayed two hours or more a written notice setting out the rules for compensation and assistance, with the contact details of the national enforcement body (Art. 14(2)).

qs.title: Rerouting after cancellation
qs.q: After a cancellation, does the airline offer a refund or a new flight, including on other airlines?
qs.law: After a cancellation you choose between a refund within 7 days, rerouting at the earliest opportunity under comparable conditions, or a later flight at your convenience. The airline must explain alternative transport. The Regulation does not say whether the new flight may be on another airline.
qs.lawText: When a flight is cancelled, the airline must offer the passenger a choice between three options (Art. 5(1)(a) with Art. 8(1)): reimbursement of the full ticket price within seven days for the parts of the journey not made (and for parts already flown if they no longer serve any purpose), together with a return flight to the first point of departure where relevant; rerouting to the final destination under comparable transport conditions at the earliest opportunity; or rerouting to the final destination under comparable transport conditions at a later date at the passenger's convenience, subject to availability of seats. When passengers are told of the cancellation, the airline must explain possible alternative transport (Art. 5(2)). The text does not say whether the replacement flight may be on another airline: it neither names nor excludes other carriers. The Commission's non-binding interpretative guidelines say rerouting should cost the passenger nothing extra even when it is on another air carrier.

qs.title: Compensation for late cancellations
qs.q: When does a cancelled flight earn compensation? We check the notice period and the rebooking times.
qs.law: Notice rule: no compensation if you were told at least 14 days ahead; or, with 7-14 days' notice, if you were offered a replacement leaving up to 2 h earlier and arriving less than 4 h later; or, with under 7 days' notice, up to 1 h earlier and less than 2 h later. Both limits must hold. Extraordinary circumstances are a separate defence.
qs.lawText: A passenger whose flight is cancelled has the right to compensation (Art. 5(1)(c)): €250 for flights of 1,500 km or less, €400 for flights within the EU of more than 1,500 km and for other flights between 1,500 and 3,500 km, and €600 for all other flights (Art. 7(1)), unless one of these applies. (i) The airline told the passenger at least two weeks before departure. (ii) It told the passenger between two weeks and seven days before departure and offered rerouting that allows departure no more than two hours before the scheduled time and arrival less than four hours after the scheduled arrival. (iii) It told the passenger less than seven days before departure and offered rerouting that allows departure no more than one hour before the scheduled time and arrival less than two hours after the scheduled arrival. In (ii) and (iii) both the departure limit and the arrival limit must be met. Separately, the airline owes no compensation if it proves that extraordinary circumstances caused the cancellation and could not have been avoided with all reasonable measures (Art. 5(3)). The airline must prove whether and when the passenger was told (Art. 5(4)). If the passenger is offered rerouting under Art. 8 that arrives no more than two hours (flights up to 1,500 km), three hours (the €400 band) or four hours (all other flights) after the scheduled arrival, the airline may cut the compensation by 50 % (Art. 7(2)).

groups.title: Rail operators
groups.who: Passenger rail operators in the EU

qs.title: Choices after cancellation or delay
qs.q: Does the operator offer a refund or rerouting when you will arrive 60 minutes or more late?
qs.law: Expected final delay of at least 60 minutes

qs.title: Costs of an alternative journey
qs.q: May you book your own onward trip if the operator offers none within 100 minutes?
qs.law: Yes, by rail, coach or bus, once 100 minutes pass from the scheduled departure without rerouting options from the operator; it must repay necessary, appropriate and reasonable costs. Some local services may be exempt
qs.lawText: Where it is reasonably expected that you will reach your final destination 60 minutes or more late, the operator must offer refund or rerouting. If it has not told you the available rerouting options within 100 minutes of the scheduled departure of the delayed or cancelled train (or of the missed connection), you may book your own journey with another provider of public transport by rail, coach or bus. The operator must then repay the necessary, appropriate and reasonable costs. The 100 minutes run from the scheduled departure, not from when you ask. Member States may exempt urban and suburban services from this right, and regional services until 7 June 2028.
qs.prov: Regulation (EU) 2021/782, Art. 18(1) and (3), with Art. 2(6)(a) and (8)

qs.title: Care in extraordinary events
qs.q: Do meals and a hotel still apply when the disruption has an extraordinary cause?
qs.law: Meals and a hotel are still owed. The operator may limit the hotel to three nights only when the cause is extraordinary and outside the railway's operation, the passenger's fault or a third party
qs.lawText: Once a delay reaches 60 minutes or the service is cancelled, the operator must offer meals and refreshments free of charge, in reasonable relation to the waiting time, if they are available on the train or in the station or can reasonably be supplied. It must also offer a hotel or other accommodation, and transport to it, where a stay of one or more nights becomes necessary and is physically possible. The Regulation makes no exception for these duties because of the cause. Only where the stay is needed because of the circumstances in Article 19(10) may the operator limit the accommodation to a maximum of three nights. Those circumstances are extraordinary circumstances not connected with the operation of the railway (such as extreme weather, major natural disasters or major public health crises), fault on the part of the passenger, and behaviour of a third party; for the first and third, the operator must also have been unable to avoid them or prevent their consequences despite the care required. The limit is a permission, not an automatic cap, and it does not apply to meals. In some Member States certain domestic services may be exempt from this duty for a transitional period (Article 2(4)).
qs.prov: Regulation (EU) 2021/782, Art. 20(2)(a)-(b), with Art. 19(10) and Art. 2(4)

qs.title: Compensation in money
qs.q: Is delay compensation paid in money on request, not only as a voucher?
qs.law: Where compensation is due, you can ask for it in money, not only as a voucher; at least 25% of the ticket price from 60 minutes late, 50% from 120

qs.title: Notice before disability assistance
qs.q: How far ahead must you notify the operator to get help travelling with a disability?
qs.law: At least 24 hours before assistance is needed. If you notify later, the operator and station manager must still make all reasonable efforts to help

qs.title: Contract renewal
qs.q: Can you cancel on one month’s notice once your contract has renewed itself?
qs.law: After the first term, a contract that renews itself can be cancelled at any time on one month’s notice, at no cost
qs.lawText: If a contract is set to renew itself when you do not cancel in time, you can end it at any time after the initial term on one month’s notice. The cancellation must not cost you anything. Before the renewal, the provider has to tell you on a durable medium that the contract renews itself, that you can prevent this by cancelling in time, and that you can cancel a renewed contract. The rule protects every end user, not only consumers. It does not cover contracts that only offer number-independent messaging services or machine-to-machine transmission.

qs.title: Number porting
qs.q: Is moving your number described correctly: free of direct charge, and possible until one month after your contract ends?
qs.law: No direct charge to you; you can port up to one month after the contract ends, and with a mobile contract at any time before that too
qs.lawText: A provider of number-based communications services must let you keep your number when you switch. If you cancel a contract, you can apply to port the number up to one month after the contract ends. For mobile services you can also demand porting at any time, and your existing contract stays untouched, so it does not end by itself. The Bundesnetzagentur has to ensure that end users are charged no direct fees for porting, and that prices between providers do not exceed the one-off costs. That is a duty on the regulator; the old provider may still charge for service it has to keep providing until the switch, with connection fees cut by 50% after the contract ends. The number must be ported and activated on the agreed day, at the latest on the following working day; for each day of delay beyond that, the provider at fault owes €10.

qs.title: Outage compensation
qs.q: What do you get when a broken connection is not fixed within two days?
qs.law: Consumers get, for each day of complete outage from day 3 after the fault report: €5 or 10% of the monthly fee, from day 5 €10 or 20%, whichever is higher
qs.lawText: A consumer can demand that a provider fixes a fault without delay and free of charge. If it is not fixed within two calendar days after the provider received the fault report, the consumer can claim compensation for each following day on which the service is completely down. On the third and fourth day it is €5 or 10%, from the fifth day €10 or 20% of the agreed monthly fee, whichever is higher; the percentages are set for contracts with a constant monthly fee. Only a complete failure counts, not a slow or partial one. There is no claim if the consumer caused the fault or its continuation, or if the outage results from measures required by the Telecommunications Act or Regulation (EU) 2015/2120, security-authority orders or force majeure. A price reduction for the same fault is deducted from the compensation, and further damages remain possible, with the compensation and the damages counted against each other. Micro and small businesses and non-profits are covered too, unless they expressly agreed to waive the rule.

qs.title: Contract changes
qs.q: Can you cancel at no cost after the provider changes your contract terms?
qs.law: Cancel at no cost within 3 months of receiving the notice, unless the change only favours you, is purely administrative or required by law
qs.lawText: If the provider has reserved the right in its general terms to change the contract on its own and it does so, the end user can cancel without a notice period and without cost. This does not apply if the change is only to the user’s advantage, is purely administrative with no negative effect, or is directly required by EU or national law. The user can cancel within three months from the time a notice that meets the requirements below reaches them. The provider must send that notice clearly and on a durable medium, at least one and at most two months before the change takes effect, and state what changes, when, and that the user can cancel. The contract can end at the earliest on the day the change would take effect. The rule protects every end user, not only consumers, but not contracts that only cover number-independent interpersonal services.

qs.title: Roaming fair-use checks
qs.q: When may a provider limit EU roaming for people who mostly use the SIM abroad?
qs.law: A surcharge only if, over at least 4 months, neither your use nor your presence is mostly at home (or other listed signs apply); the provider must alert you first and allow at least 2 weeks to show home use
qs.lawText: A provider may apply a fair-use policy only to prevent abusive or anomalous use of EU roaming, such as using the SIM in another country for purposes other than periodic travel. To check, it may use objective indicators of presence and consumption, observed together over at least four months. If either your domestic consumption or your domestic presence prevails, that counts as proof of normal use. So on this test a provider may treat you as a risk only if neither is mostly domestic. Two other indicators are allowed: a long inactive SIM used mostly or only while roaming, and subscription to and sequential use of several SIMs while roaming. Where it can show with objective evidence that SIM cards were resold in an organised way to people who do not live in or have stable links to the country, it may take immediate proportionate measures. Before applying a surcharge the provider must alert you and say that, unless your usage changes within a period of at least two weeks and shows actual domestic use or presence, a surcharge may be applied to further roaming use. The surcharge may not exceed the maximum wholesale roaming charges, and it must stop once your usage no longer shows a risk. Separately from this test, a provider may cap domestic-price data roaming at a volume set by a formula (at least twice the bundle price divided by the wholesale cap) for open data bundles; for prepaid plans, at the remaining credit divided by that cap.
qs.prov: Regulation (EU) 2022/612, Art. 5(1), 7(5) and 8(1); Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2286, Art. 4(2)–(5) and 5(3)–(5)

groups.title: German embassies
groups.who: German embassies abroad, one in each host country

qs.title: Dual citizenship
qs.q: Does the embassy say you lose German citizenship, or need a retention permit, when you take another citizenship?
qs.law: No loss and no retention permit for foreign citizenship acquired since 27 June 2024; earlier acquisitions fall under the old rule
qs.lawText: From 27 June 2024, taking another citizenship no longer ends German citizenship. The Act to Modernise Nationality Law of 22 March 2024 repealed § 25 StAG (Art. 1 No. 16; in force three months after promulgation, Art. 6(1)). Under the old § 25, a German lost citizenship on acquiring a foreign one only if the acquisition was on their own application (or their legal representative’s), and not if it was the citizenship of another EU state, Switzerland or a treaty state, or if a retention permit (Beibehaltungsgenehmigung) had been granted beforehand. The current Act has no retention permit. German citizenship can still be lost on other grounds, such as renunciation (§ 26), joining without consent the armed forces of a state whose citizenship one holds or fighting for a terrorist group abroad (§ 28), and withdrawal of a naturalisation obtained by deceit (§ 35) (§ 17). The 2024 Act contains no provision that restores citizenship lost earlier under the old § 25, and the Federal Foreign Office says that for earlier cases the old grounds of acquisition and loss continue to apply; so an acquisition before 27 June 2024 is judged under the law that applied then. The other country’s law on dual citizenship is separate.
qs.prov: StAG § 25 (repealed; old text in force until 26 June 2024), § 17 · Act of 22 March 2024 (BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 104), Art. 1 No. 16, Art. 6(1)

qs.title: Children’s passports
qs.q: Does the embassy still offer or update the children’s passport (Kinderreisepass), which ended on 1 January 2024?
qs.law: No new or extended Kinderreisepass since 1 January 2024; ones applied for before then stay valid until the date printed in them
qs.lawText: Since 1 January 2024 the Passport Act no longer lists the children’s passport among the passports it recognises: § 1(2) names only the Reisepass, the provisional Reisepass and official passports. The Act of 8 October 2023 deleted the Kinderreisepass from § 1(2), deleted § 5(2) (its validity) and deleted § 5(4) sentences 2 and 3, all with effect from 1 January 2024 (Art. 7(3)). Those two sentences had said that a Kinderreisepass could be extended by one year at a time until the child’s 12th birthday, and that it needed a current photo; § 5(4) now says only that extending a passport’s validity is not permitted. § 28 keeps only the old validity rule (§ 5(2)) for Kinderreisepässe applied for before 1 January 2024, so those documents stay valid until the date printed in them. The Federal Foreign Office also says they can no longer be extended. Children can get an ordinary Reisepass, valid six years under age 24 (§ 5(1)).
qs.prov: PassG § 1(2), § 5(2), § 5(4), § 28 · Act of 8 October 2023 (BGBl. 2023 I Nr. 271), Art. 1 Nos. 1(a), 4 and 17, Art. 7(3)

qs.title: Visa application window
qs.q: Does the embassy say when you may apply for a short-stay visa: from six months before travel, ordinarily up to 15 days before?
qs.law: Apply at most 6 months before travel (9 months for seafarers on duty) and as a rule at least 15 calendar days before; justified urgent cases may be later
qs.lawText: A short-stay visa application may be lodged no more than six months before the start of the intended visit. Seafarers performing their duties may apply up to nine months before. As a rule the application must be lodged no later than 15 calendar days before the visit starts. In justified individual cases of urgency the consulate or the central authorities may allow it later. An appointment may be required; as a rule it takes place within two weeks of the date it was requested. In justified cases of urgency the consulate may allow an application without an appointment, or give one immediately.
qs.prov: Visa Code (Regulation 810/2009), Art. 9(1)-(3), as amended by Regulation 2019/1155

qs.title: Passport validity
qs.q: Does the embassy ask for more passport validity than the rules require: three months beyond your stay and two blank pages?
qs.law: Valid 3 months after planned departure, 2 blank pages, issued within the last 10 years; the 3 months can be waived in a justified emergency
qs.lawText: For a short-stay (Schengen) visa the applicant must present a valid travel document that meets three criteria: its validity extends at least three months after the intended date of departure from the Schengen states (after the last intended departure, if the visa covers several visits); it has at least two blank pages; and it was issued within the previous 10 years. Only the three-month validity may be waived, and only in a justified case of emergency. Article 12 sets no other validity or blank-page criterion. Family members protected by Directive 2004/38 (valid passport, Art. 5(1)) and national long-stay visas follow separate rules.

qs.title: Visa fee for EU-citizen families
qs.q: Does the embassy charge a visa fee to non-EU family members who accompany or join an EU citizen?
qs.law: Free for non-EU family members who accompany or join an EU citizen living in or moving to another EU state; otherwise the standard visa fee applies (€90; €45 for children aged 6 to 11; none under 6)
qs.lawText: A non-EU family member of a Union citizen who moves to or lives in a Member State other than their own, and who accompanies or joins that citizen, is covered by Directive 2004/38. Such a family member needs only the entry visa that EU or national visa rules require, and the state must give them every facility to get it; the visa is issued free of charge, as soon as possible and in an accelerated procedure (Art. 5(2)). Family members are the spouse; the registered partner, if the host state treats registered partnerships as equivalent to marriage; children, and those of the spouse or partner, who are under 21 or dependants; and dependent relatives in the ascending line, and those of the spouse or partner (Art. 2(2)). A family member with a valid residence card under Art. 10 needs no visa. The Visa Code applies without prejudice to these free-movement rights (Art. 1(2)(a)). Its own fee is €90 (children aged 6 to 11: €45; under 6: free; higher if the Council has set a surcharge for a country under Art. 25a(5)(b)), with waivers for listed groups and individual cases (Art. 16); family members of Union citizens are not a listed group there. Other relatives and partners in a durable relationship fall under Art. 3(2): the Directive only requires the host state to facilitate their entry under national law and does not say their visa is free. The Directive does not cover family of a citizen who has not used free movement, such as a German living in Germany: it gives them no fee exemption, and the Visa Code fee rules (short stays) or national law (longer stays) apply. The Directive speaks of the visa being free; it does not mention an external service provider’s fee (Visa Code Art. 17).
qs.prov: Directive 2004/38/EC, Art. 5(2) with Art. 2(2), 3(1), 3(2), 10 · Visa Code (Regulation 810/2009), Art. 1(2)(a), Art. 16

groups.who: Banks offering consumer payment accounts in Germany

qs.title: Existing accounts
qs.q: When does another account prevent you from obtaining a Basiskonto?
qs.law: Only an actually usable German payment account can support refusal on this ground; terminated or notified closure is an exception.
qs.lawText: A bank may refuse a qualifying Basiskonto application on this ground where the applicant already holds a payment account at an institution in Germany and can actually use it for basic payment services. An account abroad, a savings account without payment facilities or a pending application alone does not suffice. The bank may not refuse on this ground if the existing account has been terminated or its closure notified. This is a limit on the statutory right to compel opening, not a general prohibition on holding two Basiskonten. Other statutory refusal grounds remain possible. The separate one-P-Konto rule applies to attachment-protected accounts.

qs.title: Cash deposits and withdrawals
qs.q: Can you deposit and withdraw cash with a Basiskonto?
qs.law: Cash services must be available to the extent the bank generally offers them to ordinary consumer account holders.
qs.lawText: The statutory basic services include cash deposits and withdrawals. They must be available to the extent the bank generally offers those services to ordinary consumer payment-account holders, including the relevant counter, ATM or network facilities. The bank need not create cash facilities it offers to nobody. The absence of cash deposits across all account models does not itself establish that the law prevents the bank from offering any Basiskonto. There is no universal entitlement to free cash transactions, every ATM or every branch. Prices, identity checks and applicable service conditions must be read separately; the number of services may not be capped merely because the holder has a Basiskonto. For a foreign institution operating through a German branch, the comparison is with the ordinary consumer offering of that branch.

qs.title: Transfers, direct debits and card payments
qs.q: Can you make transfers, direct debits and card payments with a Basiskonto?
qs.law: Basic services include transfers, standing orders, direct debits and payment-card transactions within the bank’s general offering.
qs.lawText: The basic payment services include transfers and standing orders, direct debits including one-off debits, and payment-card transactions or an equivalent payment instrument, without a credit entitlement. These services include payments involving another payment-service provider in the EEA. They must be provided to the extent generally offered to ordinary consumer account holders, through the bank’s usual payment-order channels. A bank need not supply channels it offers to nobody. A credit card, a particular card brand, foreign-currency service or every country in SEPA is not automatically required. A free-transaction allowance followed by charges is not a prohibition on further transactions; the number of basic services may not itself be restricted. For a foreign institution operating through a German branch, the comparison is with the ordinary consumer offering of that branch.

qs.title: P-Konto on request
qs.q: Can your Basiskonto be opened or converted into a P-Konto?
qs.law: P-Konto treatment can be requested at application or later; each person may hold only one P-Konto.
qs.lawText: An applicant may already request that a Basiskonto be operated as a Pfändungsschutzkonto (P-Konto) in the statutory application. A natural person may also require an existing payment account to be operated as a P-Konto, including when its balance is negative. Only one P-Konto may be held per person, and a P-Konto must operate on a credit-balance basis. Merely opening an ordinary Basiskonto does not automatically create attachment protection. This question concerns availability on request, not protection amounts or conversion-processing deadlines.

qs.title: Extra products and membership
qs.q: Must you buy another product or become a member to get a Basiskonto?
qs.law: No tied additional services; narrow exceptions permit certain occupational restrictions and uniformly required cooperative shares.
qs.lawText: Opening, the statutory content and use of a Basiskonto may not be tied to additional services such as another account product, insurance or an overdraft. Optional extras and ordinary account or transaction charges are not prohibited tied services. An occupational restriction is permitted only where the bank’s account business exclusively serves that occupational group. Requiring cooperative shares is permitted only if the institution imposes that condition equally on all customers. A discount condition is not automatically an opening condition. Read the actual product conditions and ordinary bank offering before classifying a profession or membership restriction.

groups.title: Pflegekassen
groups.who: German statutory long-term care insurance funds

qs.title: Prior care
qs.q: Must someone have cared for you for six months before you can claim replacement care?
qs.law: No six-month prior-care requirement; the other eligibility conditions still apply.
qs.lawText: Since 1 July 2025, Verhinderungspflege no longer requires the usual carer to have provided six months of prior care. The person receiving care must have at least Pflegegrad 2, normally be cared for at home by a care person, and need replacement care because that person is prevented by holiday, illness or another reason. Necessary replacement costs must be proved. This does not abolish the separate insurance-history requirement in §33(2). For replacement care carried out from 1 January 2026, current §39 also permits an application after the care and requires the reimbursement application with cost evidence by the end of the following calendar year.

qs.title: Shared annual budget
qs.q: How much is available annually for replacement care and short-term residential care?
qs.law: From Pflegegrad 2, up to €3,539 shared between both benefits per calendar year.
qs.lawText: Since 1 July 2025, people with at least Pflegegrad 2 have one common annual amount of up to €3,539 for Verhinderungspflege under §39 and Kurzzeitpflege under §42 together. Spending on either reduces what remains for the other; it is not €3,539 for each and not an automatic cash payment. Each service must meet its own statutory conditions. The eight-week duration limits for each benefit, and the special reimbursement rules for close relatives and household members, also apply. Amounts already used in the first half of 2025 counted towards the common amount for that year; 2026 has its own calendar-year budget.

qs.title: Replacement care by relatives
qs.q: How much replacement care can close relatives or household members be reimbursed for?
qs.law: For non-commercial care, normally two months’ Pflegegeld, plus proved necessary expenses within the shared annual budget.
qs.lawText: Replacement carers related or related by marriage to the person receiving care within the second degree, or living in the same household, are not excluded from reimbursement. For non-commercial replacement care, reimbursement normally may not exceed two months of the Pflegegeld for the person’s Pflegegrad. Since 1 July 2025 these amounts are €694 for grade 2, €1,198 for grade 3, €1,600 for grade 4 and €1,980 for grade 5. Proved necessary expenses connected with the replacement care can be reimbursed above that amount, for example travel costs or lost earnings. The combined reimbursement remains within the common annual budget, allowing for other spending. If those relatives or household members provide replacement care commercially, §39(3) instead allows reimbursement up to the common annual amount. These are cost-reimbursement limits, not guaranteed lump-sum payments.

qs.title: Relief allowance
qs.q: Can people with Pflegegrad 1 receive the relief allowance, and how much is it?
qs.law: Yes: up to €131 a month for eligible expenses, including Pflegegrad 1.
qs.lawText: People receiving care at home, including those with Pflegegrad 1, can receive reimbursement of eligible expenses of up to €131 a month through the Entlastungsbetrag. It is earmarked for the services listed in §45b(1), including recognised everyday-support services; it is not unrestricted cash paid automatically. For grades 2–5 it cannot cover self-care services from an outpatient care service; that particular exclusion does not apply to grade 1. Unused amounts can carry over into the following half-year. Entitlement arises without a prior application, but reimbursement requires a claim and receipts. General benefit conditions remain applicable.

qs.title: Pflegegeld during hospital treatment
qs.q: How long does Pflegegeld continue during an inpatient hospital stay?
qs.law: Generally at its existing level for the first eight weeks of inpatient treatment.
qs.lawText: Since 1 January 2026, an existing entitlement to Pflegegeld under §37 or proportionate Pflegegeld under §38 continues for the first eight weeks of fully inpatient hospital treatment. The same continuation provision covers the specified home nursing and admission to qualifying preventive or rehabilitation facilities. It preserves the existing payment level; it does not turn proportionate Pflegegeld into full Pflegegeld. Where the person employs special care workers and §63b(6), sentence 1, SGB XII applies, payment continues beyond eight weeks too. The distinct half-rate continuation rules for Verhinderungspflege and Kurzzeitpflege do not determine payment during a hospital stay.

qs.title: Required advice visits
qs.q: How often must Pflegegeld recipients obtain a compulsory advice visit?
qs.law: Once per half-year for grades 2 to 5 receiving Pflegegeld without outpatient care services; quarterly advice is optional for grades 4 and 5.
qs.lawText: Since 1 January 2026, people in grades 2–5 who receive Pflegegeld without outpatient benefits in kind from a care service must obtain a consultation in their home once per half-year. People in grades 4–5 can use quarterly consultations, but the extra frequency is optional. The compulsory advice duty also applies when the outpatient benefit amount is used solely for recognised everyday-support services through the conversion entitlement under §45a(4). Grade 1 and people receiving outpatient benefits in kind from a care service have a voluntary half-yearly consultation entitlement under this provision. At the person’s request, every second consultation may be by video until 31 March 2027; the first must take place at home. The fund bears the consultation costs. Failure to obtain compulsory advice can lead to appropriate reduction and, for repeated failure, withdrawal of Pflegegeld under §37(6). This check concerns the required frequency, not whether a consultation is advisable.

cities.claim: Retroactive Wohngeld start tied to the earlier benefit application month; the relevant refusal month can differ.
cities.q: Wohngeld kann auch rückwirkend beantragt werden, wenn in der Regel innerhalb von 4 Wochen nach Kenntnis von der Entscheidung über Ablehnung oder Aufhebung von Bürgergeld/Arbeitslosengeld II oder Grundsicherung, der Wohngeldantrag gestellt wird. Der Beginn des Bewilligungszeitraumes von Wohngeld beginnt dann nicht mit dem Monat der Antragstellung auf Wohngeld, sondern mit dem Monat der Antragstellung auf die oben genannte Leistung (Bürgergeld/Arbeitslosengeld II oder Grundsicherung).
cities.why: Retroactive Wohngeld start tied to the earlier benefit application month; the relevant refusal month can differ. Applicable provisions: WoGG §25 Abs.3; Abs.4 Second-sweep scope: Retain only narrow later-period revocation scenario: Bürgergeld applied January and validly paid January–March, award revoked only April onward under SGBX48; WoGG8(1)S3Nr3 treats exclusion as not occurred only revoked period. A timely Wohngeld claim can start April, not January (all other conditions assumed). Source expressly includes Aufhebung and next sentence categorically ties start to original transfer-application month. Read current SGBX48 too. Ordinary wholly refused initial claims may coincide, retained as counterevidence; in der Regel grammatically qualifies four-week condition, not categorical second sentence.

cities.claim: Requires a translator sworn in Germany; covered EU documents also admit certified translations by persons qualified in another Member State.
cities.q:
Dokumente in deutscher Sprache
Sollten die erforderlichen Unterlagen / Urkunden nicht in deutscher Sprache vorliegen, so müssen diese durch eine/n in Deutschland beeidigte/n Dolmetscher/in übersetzt werden (unter "Weiterführende Informationen").
Für einige Länder ist zudem eine Überbeglaubigung (Apostille oder Legalisation) erforderlich. Die Apostille (von der zuständigen Heimatbehörde im Heimatland ausgestellt) oder die Legalisation (von der deutschen Botschaft ausgestellt) muss direkt auf dem Original angebracht oder damit verbunden sein (mehr unter "Weiterführende Informationen").
Bei Urkunden, die im Original in arabisch, griechisch, hebräisch oder kyrilisch ausgestellt wurden, muss die Übersetzung von Personennamen (wie Vor- und Familiennamen, Geburtsnamen) zwingend nach den Transliterationsnormen (ISO 9-1995 / ISO 843 / DIN 31634 / ELOT 734 usw.) erfolgen.
cities.why: Requires a translator sworn in Germany; covered EU documents also admit certified translations by persons qualified in another Member State. Applicable provisions: Regulation(EU)2016/1191 Art2(1),(3),(4); Art6(2); Art27(2) Second-sweep scope: Original complete document-language passage and surrounding document lists freshly read. Official EU Art2,6,27 freshly retrieved from PublicationsOffice: translations certified by legally qualified person in any MemberState accepted for covered EU-issued public civil-status documents. Not oral interpretation or third-country documents, nor recognition of substantive legal effects.

cities.claim: Absolute 14-month window and 12-month individual cap omit statutory extensions for qualifying premature births.
cities.q:
Basiselterngeld
Basiselterngeld kann nur in den ersten 14 Lebensmonaten des Kindes bezogen werden. Der Anspruch besteht für 12 Lebensmonate Ihres Kindes.
Soweit sich bei mindestens einem Elternteil das Erwerbseinkommen nach der Geburt mindert, können Sie zwei zusätzliche Basiselterngeldmonate nutzen.
Sie müssen mindestens zwei Monate und können höchstens zwölf Monate Basiselterngeld in Anspruch nehmen.
Ein gleichzeitiger Bezug von Basiselterngeld ist nur innerhalb der ersten zwölf Lebensmonate des Kindes und maximal für einen Monat möglich. Eltern von Frühchen, Mehrlingen oder neugeborenen Kindern mit Behinderung oder Geschwisterkindern mit Behinderung können nach Bedarf und für mehr als einen Monat gleichzeitig Basiselterngeld beziehen.
cities.why: Absolute 14-month window and 12-month individual cap omit statutory extensions for qualifying premature births. Applicable provisions: BEEG §4 Abs.5; §28 Second-sweep scope: Full Basiselterngeld section unchanged; express nur-first14 and höchstens12 affirmative caps differ from4(5)qualifying preterm extension. Correct adjacent simultaneous-receipt exception4(6) is preserved and does not state duration extension. This is stronger than omitted detail in a neutral overview.

cities.claim: Requires a German residence-title copy from all non-EU foreign applicants, including qualifying Norwegian EEA residents who need no such title.
cities.q:
Erforderliche Unterlagen
Aktuelles Lichtbild (ab dem 10. Lebensjahr)
Die Ausstellung eines Schwerbehindertenausweises beantragen Sie, indem Sie dem Versorgungsamt ein Lichtbild/Passfoto von sich zukommen lassen (es muss nicht biometrisch sein). Das können Sie online erledigen, per E-Mail (im JPG-Format), mit der Post oder vor Ort.
Für ausländische Bürgerinnen und Bürger aus Nicht-EU-Staaten: gültiger Aufenthaltstitel in Deutschland (in Kopie)
Falls Sie einem Staat der Europäischen Union (EU) angehören, genügt dazu in der Regel die Kopie Ihres Ausweis-Dokuments.
Falls Sie einem anderen Staat angehören, benötigen wir eine Kopie von Ihrem Aufenthaltstitel, zum Beispiel von Ihrer Aufenthaltserlaubnis oder Ihrer Aufenthaltsgestattung.
Bei Vertretung: Vollmacht
Wenn eine andere Person für Sie den Schwerbehindertenausweis erhalten soll, muss diese Person eine schriftliche Vollmacht einreichen.
cities.why: FreizügG/EU §12 extends the positive title exemption in §2a(1) to qualifying Norwegian EEA nationals; §2(2) no. 1 covers workers. SGB IX §§2(2) and 152(5) provide the card framework for otherwise eligible lawfully resident or working disabled people. A universal title-copy requirement adds a document condition where no title is required. SchwbAwV §6(5) limits validity when an existing permission is limited; it does not require a title from every foreign applicant.

cities.claim: Four-week wording for retroactive Wohngeld; an exclusive shorter deadline is not established.
cities.q: Wohngeld kann auch rückwirkend beantragt werden, wenn in der Regel innerhalb von 4 Wochen nach Kenntnis von der Entscheidung über Ablehnung oder Aufhebung von Bürgergeld/Arbeitslosengeld II oder Grundsicherung, der Wohngeldantrag gestellt wird. Der Beginn des Bewilligungszeitraumes von Wohngeld beginnt dann nicht mit dem Monat der Antragstellung auf Wohngeld, sondern mit dem Monat der Antragstellung auf die oben genannte Leistung (Bürgergeld/Arbeitslosengeld II oder Grundsicherung).
cities.why: Not reconfirmed in this conservative third sweep. Fresh full Fristen passage and full current WoGG25/8/28 read. Statutory calendar-month mismatch is real, but kann auch/wenn/in der Regel does not expressly state an exclusive expiry. After independent peer challenge and comparison with other sufficient-subset cases, Fristen heading alone is insufficient to confirm a four-week cutoff. Preserve prior allegation and law/history; do not infer every later filing barred. Separate explicit starting-month formula remains distinct. Third-reader challenge after researcher retained and peer questioned exclusivity. Fresh full relevant municipal HTML core read, including Fristen, eligibility, application documents and statutory links; current full WoGG25 and8 read.25(3) positively allows before the end of the calendar month following knowledge, so four weeks is numerically shorter. But the publication says kann auch ... wenn in der Regel innerhalb4Wochen and does not expressly state nur, spaetestens, expiry or rejection of later applications. Under the conservative sufficient-subset standard used for other cases, an earlier timely filing condition remains a credible reading. A Fristen heading and normative tone support the former allegation but do not decisively establish the exclusive shorter deadline. No confirmed misstatement on this timing sentence; do not infer the whole page accurate. Separate affirmative start-month formula is a different stable case, still independently assessed. WoGG28 web access failed; no fresh28 check claimed and no conclusion on that separate start-month case is made here. Full Fristen paragraph says kann auch, wenn, in der Regel within four weeks, without nur/spätestens/late exclusion. Current WoGG25(3) allows filing before expiry of calendar month following knowledge of refusal, also corresponding undone-exclusion cases. Four weeks is sufficient subset. Normative heading supports concern but conservative exclusive-bar allegation not established; root and north independently agree downgrade.

cities.claim: Potential discrepancy: municipal prerequisites present four weeks from the attachment as the condition for retroactive protection. Current899(1) instead allows actual conversion before one month from service of the transfer order. But this is not yet a confirmed exclusive deadline claim: source says wenn/veranlassen and does not say nur/spätestens.
cities.page: Zwangsvollstreckung – Pfändungsschutzkonto – Erweiterung des Pfändungsschutzes beantragen
cities.q:
Um Pfändungsschutz zu erhalten, müssen Sie Ihr Girokonto in ein Pfändungsschutzkonto umwandeln lassen. Die Kündigung Ihres Girokontos ist dazu nicht erforderlich. Sie müssen der Bank unter Angabe der IBAN schriftlich mitteilen, dass Sie die Umwandlung in ein P-Konto wünschen. Der Schutz gilt rückwirkend zum Monatsersten, wenn Sie die Umwandlung in ein P-Konto vor Ablauf von 4 Wochen seit der Pfändung veranlassen, das heißt seit dem Eingang des Pfändungsbeschlusses bei der Bank.
• Die Umwandlung können Sie auch vorsorglich verlangen, ohne dass eine Pfändung besteht.
• Sie dürfen nur ein einziges Girokonto als P-Konto führen. Die Führung eines P-Kontos wird an die SCHUFA mitgeteilt. Sie müssen im Umwandlungsschreiben versichern, dass Sie kein weiteres P-Konto führen.
cities.why: Potential discrepancy: municipal prerequisites present four weeks from the attachment as the condition for retroactive protection. Current899(1) instead allows actual conversion before one month from service of the transfer order. But this is not yet a confirmed exclusive deadline claim: source says wenn/veranlassen and does not say nur/spätestens.

cities.claim: The service prerequisites require having been summoned to and attended a hearing. JVEG19(1) expressly also covers court-ordered written answers to the evidentiary question, which ZPO377(3) permits without an ensuing hearing. A qualifying written witness can have a compensation claim without attending. Pending review whether this page is sufficiently confined to the attendance-service branch.
cities.page: Zeuginnen und Zeugen – Entschädigung in zivilrechtlichen Verfahren beantragen
cities.q:
Waren Sie als Zeugin oder Zeuge beteiligt in einem zivilrechtlichen Verfahren
• der Berliner Amtsgerichte,
• des Landgerichts Berlin,
• des Kammergerichts?
Dann können Sie entschädigt werden für
• Verdienstausfall,
• Zeitversäumnis,
• Fahrtkosten und
• sonstige Aufwendungen.
Voraussetzungen
• Sie waren zu einem Termin als Zeuge/in geladen und sind zum Termin erschienen
• Sie haben nicht auf die Zeugenentschädigung verzichtet
• Beantragung innerhalb von 3 Monaten
cities.why: The service prerequisites require having been summoned to and attended a hearing. JVEG19(1) expressly also covers court-ordered written answers to the evidentiary question, which ZPO377(3) permits without an ensuing hearing. A qualifying written witness can have a compensation claim without attending. Pending review whether this page is sufficiently confined to the attendance-service branch.

cities.claim: Care-assistance means test includes a separated wife or female civil partner; direct joint means testing concerns non-separated partners.
cities.q:
Sie sind pflegebedürftig im Sinne des § 61a SGB XII.
Sie können den notwendigen Pflegebedarf nicht aus eigenen finanziellen Mitteln sicherstellen.
Gegebenenfalls: Ihrem nicht getrenntlebenden Ehegatten oder Lebenspartner beziehungsweise Ihrer getrenntlebenden Ehegattin oder Lebenspartnerin ist nicht zuzumuten, die benötigten Mittel aus Einkommen und Vermögen aufzubringen, um Ihren Pflegebedarf zu decken.
cities.why: Care-assistance means test includes a separated wife or female civil partner; direct joint means testing concerns non-separated partners. Applicable provisions: SGB XII §19 Abs.3 Second-sweep scope: Fresh full core still says female separated spouse but male non-separated spouse. SGBXII19(3)joint means applies non-separated only. Actual maintenance income and civil maintenance recovery remain separate;94full freshly read, no assertion separated spouse immune from support liability.

cities.claim: Requires 400 supplementary media/presence hours; qualifying first-level part-time courses can meet a 200-hour combined minimum under current law.
cities.q:
Ihre Fortbildung erfüllt die erforderliche Mindestdauer.
Maßnahmen der ersten beruflichen Fortbildungsstufe müssen mindestens 200 Unterrichtsstunden umfassen. Weitere Maßnahmen müssen mindestens 400 Unterrichtsstunden umfassen.
Wenn Sie eine mediengestützte Fortbildung absolvieren, muss diese durch Präsenzunterricht oder eine vergleichbare verbindliche mediengestützte Kommunikation im Umfang von mindestens 400 Stunden ergänzt werden. Zudem müssen regelmäßige Erfolgskontrollen durchgeführt werden.
cities.why: Requires 400 supplementary media/presence hours; qualifying first-level part-time courses can meet a 200-hour combined minimum under current law. Applicable provisions: AFBG §4a Abs.3; §2 Abs.3 Satz2; §30 transition Second-sweep scope: Fresh core correct200firstlevel general minimum followed by explicit media400requirement. Current4a(1)requires presence supplement and controls;4a(3)aggregates presence plus qualified media hours against2(3).2(3)S2 specifically permits qualifying firstlevelparttime200hours/36months. No400 media-specific floor for that scenario. Do not claim every200hourcourse eligible; exclude self-study/nonqualifying media/absence of presence/control.

cities.claim: The source expressly limits tax classII to full calendar months during which the conditions are met. Federal24b(4) removes one twelfth only for a full calendar month without conditions;39(6) makes a favourable tax-class change effective from the first day of the month when conditions first arise. Conditions can arise part-way through a qualifying month.
cities.q: Teilen Sie der zuständigen Stelle schriftlich mit, wenn die Voraussetzungen für den Entlastungsbetrags für Alleinerziehende wegfallen. Die Steuerklasse II steht Ihnen nur für jeden vollen Kalendermonat zu, in dem die Voraussetzungen vorliegen. Die Voraussetzung für die Berücksichtigung der Steuerklasse II entfällt zum Beispiel, wenn Sie eine eheähnliche Gemeinschaft begründen.
cities.why: The source expressly limits tax classII to full calendar months during which the conditions are met. Federal24b(4) removes one twelfth only for a full calendar month without conditions;39(6) makes a favourable tax-class change effective from the first day of the month when conditions first arise. Conditions can arise part-way through a qualifying month.

cities.claim: Restricts passport applications outside the home municipality to urgent overseas residents; an important reason can require processing for other applicants too, with issuance authorisation.
cities.q:
Sie können den Reisepass grundsätzlich nur bei der Passbehörde an Ihrem Hauptwohnsitz beantragen.

Eine Ausnahme gibt es nur für Bundesbürger, die im Ausland leben, sich zu Besuch in München aufhalten und zwingend einen neuen Pass brauchen. In diesem Ausnahmefall können Sie keinen Termin in einem Bürgerbüro buchen, da die Sachbearbeitung zentral erfolgt. Für Informationen zur Antragstellung und Terminvereinbarung benutzen Sie bitte das Kontaktformular.
cities.why: Restricts passport applications outside the home municipality to urgent overseas residents; an important reason can require processing for other applicants too, with issuance authorisation. Applicable provisions: PassG §19 Abs.3–4 Second-sweep scope: The sentence Ausnahme gibt es nur restricts processing outside home municipality to urgent overseas residents. PassG19(4) affirmatively requires processing for a demonstrated important reason without that geographic restriction, subject to issuance authorisation.

cities.claim: Tests the caring parent's non-receipt of SGB II in the age-12 maintenance-advance alternative; that alternative concerns the child's receipt.
cities.q:
Anspruch hat
• jedes Kind, das mit einem seiner Elternteile, welches ledig, verwitwet oder geschieden ist, lebt und
• monatlich weniger Unterhalt oder Waisenbezüge erhält, als Leistungen nach dem Unterhaltsvorschussgesetz (UVG) möglich wären und
• wer die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit oder die Berechtigung zur Freizügigkeit (EU / EWR-Staatsangehörigkeit); eine Niederlassungserlaubnis oder Aufenthaltserlaubnis (Berechtigung zur Erwerbstätigkeit; Daueraufenthalt) besitzt.
• ab dem 12. Lebensjahr:
  • betreuendes Elternteil bezieht keine Leistungen nach dem SGB II oder
  • bei laufendem Bezug von Leistungen nach dem SGB II erzielt der betreuende Elternteil Einkommen in Höhe von monatlich mindestens 600 Euro brutto oder die Hilfebedürftigkeit des Kindes beziehungsweise der Bedarfsgemeinschaft wird durch die Gewährung von Unterhaltsvorschuss-Leistungen vermieden
cities.why: Tests the caring parent's non-receipt of SGB II in the age-12 maintenance-advance alternative; that alternative concerns the child's receipt. Applicable provisions: UhVorschG §1 Abs.1a Satz1 Nr.1–2 Second-sweep scope: Current1(1a)Nr1 tests the child’s non-receipt of SGB II, whereas the municipal first age12 alternative tests the caring parent.600Euro parental earnings and avoiding child need are different statutory alternatives; their presence does not make the wrong-person wording accurate.

cities.claim: The blanket non-EU residence-permit requirement includes EEA nationals such as a Norwegian eligible self-employed trader. FreizügG/EU12 applies the positive no-residence-title rule in2a(1) to those EEA nationals. A residence permit permitting self-employment is therefore not a universal additional document/condition for non-EU traders.
cities.q:
Was ist bei Nicht-EU-Bürgern*innen zu beachten?
Sie benötigen eine in Deutschland ausgestellte, gültige Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur Ausübung einer selbstständigen Erwerbstätigkeit. Der Aufenthaltstitel wird bei der Online-Anmeldung im Meldevorgang hochgeladen.
cities.why: The blanket non-EU residence-permit requirement includes EEA nationals such as a Norwegian eligible self-employed trader. FreizügG/EU12 applies the positive no-residence-title rule in2a(1) to those EEA nationals. A residence permit permitting self-employment is therefore not a universal additional document/condition for non-EU traders. Applicable provisions: FreizügG/EU12; FreizügG/EU2a(1)S1; FreizügG/EU2(2)Nr2

cities.claim: The complete meal-cost exception categorically denies BuT on attending a Hort. Current28(6) positively covers a qualifying school pupil’s communal lunch provided in school responsibility or under a school–daycare cooperation agreement. The statutory daycare category can include a Hort; attendance alone is not a categorical bar.
cities.page: School-meal support in a qualifying Hort
cities.q:
Hinweis zum Essensgeld
Die Übernahme des Essensgeldes (Verpflegungskosten) erfolgt beim Bezug von Grundsicherungsgeld, Wohngeld, Kinderzuschlag oder Leistungen nach dem Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz über Leistungen zur Bildung und Teilhabe (BuT). Bitte beantragen Sie die Kostenübernahme des Essensgeldes bei Grundsicherungsgeld bei Ihrem Jobcenter, bei Wohngeld und Kinderzuschlag beim Amt für soziale Sicherung und bei Bezug von Leistungen nach dem Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz beim Amt für Wohnen und Migration. Eine Übernahme des Essensgeldes durch die Wirtschaftliche Jugendhilfe ist in diesem Fall nicht möglich.
Ausnahme:
Beim Besuch eines Kinderhortes besteht kein Anspruch auf BuT. Hier werden die Kosten der Verpflegung von der Wirtschaftlichen Jugendhilfe übernommen.
cities.why: The complete meal-cost exception categorically denies BuT on attending a Hort. Current28(6) positively covers a qualifying school pupil’s communal lunch provided in school responsibility or under a school–daycare cooperation agreement. The statutory daycare category can include a Hort; attendance alone is not a categorical bar.

cities.claim: Unclear whether completed paternity establishment is required before applying for maintenance advance.
cities.q: Wenn Sie einen Unterhaltsvorschuss beantragen wollen, muss der Vater rechtsverbindlich durch eine Urkunde oder ein Urteil festgestellt werden.
cities.why: Not reconfirmed in this conservative third sweep. Fresh full current UVG1 read. Section1(1) grants the public benefit on stated child/household/support conditions;1(3) excludes refusal to cooperate in paternity/location ascertainment, not the mere absence of completed legal establishment. Full municipal page distinguishes civil maintenance from the public advance; nevertheless its lead expressly connects wanting to apply with legally established paternity. Main UVG page repeats the lead as related service and lists acknowledgment evidence. Exact interpretation and linked leaflet qualification remain open for peer challenge; no rule of entitlement despite noncooperation is asserted. Fresh entire short paternity service and full linked main UVG body read; necessary linked easy-language leaflet pages5and8 independently read in memory. Fresh own UhVorschG1 positive entitlement/cooperation framework clear. HTML says father must be established if seeking benefit, but does not expressly say completed establishment before application/payment. The process-focused Vaterschaftsbefragung service and linked possible-father/cooperation and conditional existing-certificate instructions make an ongoing cooperation-duty reading plausible. Preserve ambiguous, not confirmed completed-establishment application bar; do not assert statutory law itself is uncertain.

cities.claim: Describes the full six/four-year integration residence period as lawful residence; the statute expressly also counts qualifying tolerated or asylum-permitted periods.
cities.q:
Voraussetzungen
• Anmeldung des Hauptwohnsitzes in München
• Gültiger Nationalpass oder zumindest geklärte Identität
• Besitz einer Aufenthaltserlaubnis gemäß § 104c AufenthG oder einer Duldung
• Ununterbrochener rechtmäßiger Aufenthalt von sechs Jahren oder vier Jahren (bei häuslicher Ge-meinschaft mit einem minderjährigen, ledigen Kind) im Bundesgebiet
• Überwiegende Sicherung des Lebensunterhalts durch Erwerbstätigkeit oder bei der Betrachtung der bisherigen Schul-, Ausbildungs-, Einkommens- sowie der familiären Lebenssituation ist zu erwarten, dass der Lebensunterhalt gesichert wird
cities.why: Not confirmed in the conservative second sweep. Technically rechtmäßiger Aufenthalt is narrower than25b(1)S2Nr1 geduldet/gestattet/permit history;60a(3) leaves duty to depart intact. However the same page explicitly includes tolerated people. Do not count a confirmed material misstatement absent a stronger exclusionary reading. Fresh introduction explicitly addresses Geduldete/104c holders; description, complete requirements and shorter family/30-month routes read. Complete current25b read. Technically lawful residence is narrower than tolerated/gestattet time, but the page repeatedly includes tolerated people. A material exclusion of their prior time is not securely established under conservative whole-page reading; rechtmäßig may be lay shorthand. Do not confirm based only on a technical term detached from the explicit audience.

cities.claim: Makes zero own income a maintenance-advance condition; general-school pupils' earnings and partially counted low earnings can coexist with entitlement.
cities.q:
Wer hat Anspruch auf Unterhaltsvorschuss?
Minderjährige Kinder, deren Eltern keinen Unterhalt leisten und die kein eigenes Einkommen haben.
In besonderen Situationen, kann es Ausnahmen geben.
Mit dem Schnell-Check können Sie prüfen, ob ein Anspruch besteht.

Wie lange wird Unterhaltsvorschuss gewährt?
Bis zur Vollendung des 18. Lebensjahres, wenn kein eigenes Einkommen erzielt wird.
cities.why: Not confirmed in the conservative second sweep. Duration answer makes no own income a general condition.2(4) disregards earnings/asset income for general-school pupils and only partly offsets covered earnings for others, so positive earnings can coexist with ongoing entitlement. Fresh both complete FAQs, main eligibility list and income-proof documents read. Current UhVorschG2 fully independently read: general-school earnings and partially counted other earnings can coexist with payment. However Wer hat Anspruch gives an eligible no-income subset and explicitly acknowledges special exceptions; duration answer Bis18,wennkeinEinkommen does not say nur/solange or expressly deny income-earner claims. Under conservative standard used for Dortmund threshold/Hannover subset, a plausible sufficient-case summary prevents confirmation. The counterexample proves legal eligibility, not that this wording excludes it.

cities.claim: Rejects email and requires a signed parental-leave request; text form suffices for children born or placed for adoption from 1 May 2025.
cities.q: Die Beantragung der Elternzeit muss zwingend schriftlich erfolgen. Es muss deshalb von der* dem Arbeitnehmer*in eigenhändig durch Namensunterschrift oder mittels notariell beglaubigten Handzeichens unterzeichnet werden. Ein Telefax oder eine E-Mail reicht nicht aus (Pressemitteilung Nummer 23/16 des Bundesarbeitsgerichtes auf sein Urteil vom 10. Mai 2016 – 9 AZR 145/15).
cities.why: Rejects email and requires a signed parental-leave request; text form suffices for children born or placed for adoption from 1 May 2025. Applicable provisions: BEEG §16(1) in conjunction with §28(1b) Second-sweep scope: Fresh full substantive page read. Mandatory signed writing/email rejection remains unqualified by birth date. Specific 2016 judgment parenthesis identifies an old legal basis but wording still addresses all applicants. BEEG16 current Textform and28 cohort saving read in full. Retain only births/adoption placements from1May2025; old cohorts retain written-form rule. Labour rule uniform; municipal/state advice cannot change private employment form.

cities.claim: Requires German appointment or swearing-in for translators of foreign records; covered EU documents admit qualified translations from another Member State.
cities.q:
Entsprechend dem Personenstand der Mutter ist die Vorlage unterschiedlicher Urkunden notwendig. Bei ausländischen Urkunden wird zudem eine Übersetzung durch eine dolmetschende Person oder ein*e Übersetzer*in benötigt. Diese*r müssen in Deutschland öffentlich bestellt oder beeidigt sein. Urkunden und Übersetzungen müssen im Original vorgelegt werden. 

verheiratete Mutter

• beglaubigte Abschrift aus dem Familienbuch oder

• Ablichtung aus dem Eheregister oder

• Heiratsurkunde/Eheurkunden und die Geburtsurkunden beider Elternteile

ledige Mutter

• die eigene Geburtsurkunde

geschiedene Mutter

• die eigene Geburtsurkunde, die Eheurkunde/Heiratsurkunde und das rechtskräftige Scheidungsurteil oder

• die beglaubigte Abschrift aus dem Familienbuch und das rechtskräftige Scheidungsurteil oder 

• die beglaubigte Ablichtung des Eheregisters mit Scheidungsvermerk

Gegebenenfalls ist die Anerkennung der ausländischen Scheidung für den deutschen Rechtsbereich erforderlich.

verwitwete Mutter

• die eigene Geburtsurkunde, die Eheurkunde/Heiratsurkunde und Sterbeurkunde oder

• die beglaubigte Abschrift aus dem Familienbuch und Sterbeurkunde oder

• die beglaubigte Ablichtung des Eheregisters mit Vermerk über den Tod des Ehemannes

Im Einzelfall können nach Prüfung weitere Unterlagen erforderlich sein.
cities.why: Requires German appointment or swearing-in for translators of foreign records; covered EU documents admit qualified translations from another Member State. Applicable provisions: Verordnung (EU)2016/1191 Art2,6(2),27 Second-sweep scope: All three current municipal publications impose Germany appointment/sworn requirement. Retain only qualified certified German translations of covered EU-authority-issued civil-status records. Article6(2) expressly requires acceptance irrespective of qualifying Member State; national PStV translation provision does not create geographical override. No claim about oral-interpreter appointments.

cities.claim: Requires an EU/EEA driving licence still valid at application; the federal expiry route can cover previously recognised licences, with its other conditions.
cities.q:
Ausländischer Führerschein im Original
Der ausländische Führerschein muss zum Zeitpunkt der Beantragung der Umschreibung noch gültig sein. Im Einzelfall kann es erforderlich sein, dass Sie den Führerschein übersetzen lassen müssen.
cities.why: Requires an EU/EEA driving licence still valid at application; the federal expiry route can cover previously recognised licences, with its other conditions. Applicable provisions: FeV §30(1),(2) Second-sweep scope: Fresh complete service page read including extra C/D documents, age50, probation, legal links and fees. Unqualified must-still-be-valid appears under required original foreign licence, with no expired-route qualification. Primary30 read all paragraphs: explicit expired route under30(2) covers AM/A/B etc previously recognised, including expiry before residence subject to authority information; C/D separate24(2)route. Retain narrow AM/A/B previously recognised licence scenario, not right to drive on expired document. State local authority arrangements do not remove federal30(2)route.

cities.claim: Categorically denies statutory representation of adults by relatives, including spouses.
cities.q: Bei Volljährigen gibt es - auch für nahe Angehörige - kein gesetzliches Vertretungsrecht. Um stellvertretend für eine volljährige Person rechtswirksame Erklärungen oder Handlungen vornehmen zu können, bedarf es eben einer gerichtlichen Bestellung zur*zum Betreuer*in oder aber einer ausreichenden Bevollmächtigung. Diese Bevollmächtigung wird Vorsorgevollmacht genannt.
cities.why: §1358 creates a statutory spouse right for defined healthcare matters without appointment as guardian or a power of attorney. The categorical no-right sentence is contradicted within that limited scenario. No claim is made that all relatives or all affairs are covered. Applicable provisions: BGB §1358 Abs.1–6

cities.claim: States that the disability tax allowance begins at a disability degree of25.
cities.q:
Abhängig von dem bei Ihnen festgestellten "Grad der Behinderung" können Sie einen Pauschalbetrag für außergewöhnliche Belastungen bei der Einkommenssteuer geltend machen. Die Kosten, die Sie geltend machen können, müssen eine Folge Ihrer Behinderung sein. Gewährt wird dieser Pauschalbetrag ab einem Grad der Behinderung von 25 Prozent. Diesen Betrag können Sie sich auch im Voraus als Freibetrag auf Ihrer Lohnsteuerkarte beim Finanzamt eintragen lassen. Als außergewöhnliche Belastungen gelten die Kosten für:
• eine Haushaltshilfe
• häusliche oder stationäre Pflegeleistungen
• Kinderbetreuungskosten
• unvermeidbare Fahrten für Freizeit-, Erholungs- und Besuchsfahrten bis zu 15.000 km jährlich
• Taxi-Fahrten, wenn es kein eigenes Auto gibt
• Unterbringung und Verpflegung der Begleitperson
cities.why: Since assessment year2021 the statutory minimum is20, not25. The municipal phrase ausdrücklich ab25 presents a minimum rather than merely describing a qualifying subset. Narrow finding on threshold only; cost-list and outdated Lohnsteuerkarte wording not separate findings. Applicable provisions: EStG §33b Abs.1–3; §52 Abs.33c

cities.claim: The stated competent-office formula treats every deceased AsylbLG recipient as triggering the former paying office. For the narrow independently eligible§74claimant/basic§3AsylbLG-deceased case, §98(3) instead uses the deathplace because the deceased received no Sozialhilfe. The current NRW default local-träger rules do not change that comparison.
cities.page: Bestattungskosten – zuständiges Sozialamt bei früheren AsylbLG-Grundleistungen
cities.q:
Die verstorbene Person hat Sozialhilfe, wie Grundsicherung im Alter oder bei Erwerbsminderung nach dem SGB (Sozialgesetzbuch) XII oder Leistungen nach Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz bezogen? Dann ist das Sozialamt, welches die Leistung gewährte, zuständig. Für das Sozialamt Köln ist das immer die Außenstelle Lindenthal (siehe Link am Ende dieses Artikels).
Hinweis: Grundsicherung für Arbeitssuchende nach dem SGB (Sozialgesetzbuch) II und Pflegewohngeld zählen nicht zur Sozialhilfe.
Die verstorbene Person hat keine Sozialhilfe oder Leistungen nach Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz bezogen? Dann ist das Sozialamt des Sterbeortes zuständig.
Ist der Sterbeort Köln, dann ist das Amt für Soziales und Senioren - Außenstelle Lindenthal zuständig.
Um Ihnen die Antragstellung so einfach wie möglich zu machen, wird unbedingt eine vorherige telefonische Kontaktaufnahme empfohlen.
Ihre Ansprechpartner finden Sie unter folgendem Link:
cities.why: The stated competent-office formula treats every deceased AsylbLG recipient as triggering the former paying office. For the narrow independently eligible§74claimant/basic§3AsylbLG-deceased case, §98(3) instead uses the deathplace because the deceased received no Sozialhilfe. The current NRW default local-träger rules do not change that comparison.

cities.claim: Source-and-law assessment remains unresolved.
cities.q: Bei der Anmeldung Ihres Wohnsitzes müssen Sie eine Bescheinigung des*der Vermieter*in oder des*der Hauptmieter*in über Ihren tatsächlichen Einzug vorlegen – die Wohnungsgeberbescheinigung. Das Einzugsdatum darf nicht in der Zukunft liegen. Aus der Bescheinigung muss der*die Eigentümer*in der Wohnung hervorgehen. Sie können die Bescheinigung nicht nachreichen.
cities.why: Source-and-law assessment remains unresolved. Applicable provisions: BMG §19(2), §23(1), BMGVwV23.0.1; requires proper primary-law assessment, not mere absence

cities.claim: Absolute German-family exclusion overlooks12a’s positive corresponding application for family of Germans who sustainably exercised Article21freedom. An eligible non-EU spouse in a qualifying return scenario can receive a residence card under the corresponding rules, rather than being categorically diverted to an AufenthG title.
cities.q:
Drittstaatsangehörigen Familienangehörigen eines freizügigkeitsberechtigten EU/EWR-Bürgers wird eine Aufenthaltskarte nach dem Freizügigkeitsgesetz ausgestellt, sofern sie mit der Bezugsperson eine familiäre Lebensgemeinschaft führen.

Applicable provisions: FreizügG/EU1(1)Nr6,12a,3(1),5(1)

cities.claim: Says acquiring a foreign nationality on application generally loses German nationality without prior retention permission; that loss ground was repealed from 27 June 2024.
cities.q:
Die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit geht in der Regel mit dem Erwerb einer ausländischen Staatsangehörigkeit verloren, wenn der Erwerb auf Antrag erfolgt.
Das gilt nicht, wenn Deutsche die Staatsangehörigkeit eines anderen Mitgliedstaates der Europäischen Union, der Schweiz oder eines Staates, mit dem die Bundesrepublik Deutschland einen entsprechenden völkerrechtlichen Vertrag abgeschlossen hat, erwerben.
Die Staatsangehörigkeit verliert auch nicht, wer vor dem Erwerb der ausländischen Staatsangehörigkeit auf Antrag die schriftliche Genehmigung zur Beibehaltung seiner deutschen Staatsangehörigkeit erhalten hat.
Zuständig für die Bearbeitung Ihres Antrags und für die Erteilung der Beibehaltungsgenehmigung ist die Bezirksregierung Düsseldorf. Unter dem Link erhalten Sie weiterführende Informationen zum Verfahren.

cities.claim: Sets a 20-hour weekly ceiling for part-time work during lecture periods. Under AufenthG §16b(3), 20 hours is a condition of one favourable weekly accounting option; daily accounting can permit more within the annual 140-day limit.
cities.page: Study residence: part-time work in lecture period
cities.q:
Ich möchte während meines Studiums arbeiten. Auf was muss ich achten? 

Internationale Studierende, die nicht aus der EU oder dem EWR und der Schweiz kommen, dürfen 140 volle Tage im Jahr arbeiten, wobei studentische Nebentätigkeiten hierbei nicht angerechnet werden. Bei Teilzeitbeschäftigungen dürfen diese während der Vorlesungszeit bis zu 20 Stunden/Woche ausgeübt werden. Für die Ausübung einer solchen Beschäftigung benötigen Sie -neben Ihrer Aufenthaltserlaubnis zum Zweck des Studiums- keine gesonderte Genehmingung. 
 
 Internationale Studierende aus Drittstaaten dürfen nur mit Genehmigung der Ausländerbehörde selbständige Tätigkeiten ausüben. In einigen Aufenthaltstiteln ist die Erlaubnis zur selbständigen Tätigkeit bereits vermerkt und muss dann nicht gesondert beantragt werden. Eine Ausnahme ist allerdings die Arbeit als wissenschaftliche oder studentische Hilfskraft an der Hochschule oder als Tutor im Studierendenwerk: Solange das Studium nicht gefährdet ist, kann diese Tätigkeit zeitlich unbegrenzt ausgeübt werden. Die Ausländerbehörde muss aber darüber informiert werden.

Under AufenthG §16b(3), 20 hours is a condition of one favourable weekly accounting option; daily accounting can permit more within the annual 140-day limit. Applicable provisions: AufenthG §16b Abs.3, especially Satz3 Nr.1–2 and weekly favourable accounting

cities.q:
Ich möchte eine Niederlassungserlaubnis während bzw. nach dem Studium erhalten. Welche Voraussetzungen muss ich erfüllen?

Eine Niederlassungserlaubnis kann weder während eines Studienaufenthalts noch während einer Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur Arbeitsplatzsuche erteilt werden. Erst wenn ein Aufenthaltstitel zu Erwerbszwecken erteilt wurde, wird auch die Aufenthaltsverfestigung durch eine Niederlassungserlaubnis möglich. Hierfür gelten verschiedene besondere Voraussetzungen, insbesondere Voraufenthaltszeiten.

Bei der Berechnung der Voraufenthaltszeiten werden die Zeiten des Aufenthalts zu Studienzwecken mit der Hälfte, höchstens aber mit zwei Jahren, angerechnet.

Welche Voraufenthaltszeiten erfüllt werden müssen, können Sie unter dem Reiter "Ihr Weg in die Niederlassungserlaubnis" auf der Seite der entsprechenden Aufenthaltserlaubnis im Bereich Beschäftigung, Selbstständigkeit und Forschung entnehmen.

cities.q:
Das Kind verheirateter Eltern erhält den Ehenamen der Eltern als Familiennamen.

Wenn die Eltern keinen gemeinsamen Ehenamen haben und sie gemeinsam die Sorge für das Kind tragen, müssen sie gegenüber dem Standesamt durch eine verbindliche Namenserklärung (PDF 247 KB) bestimmen, welcher Name als Geburtsname des Kindes festgelegt wird. Entweder den Namen, den der Vater oder die Mutter zur Zeit der Erklärung führt.

Die Bestimmung des Familiennamens der gemeinsam sorgeberechtigten Eltern gilt auch für deren weitere Kinder.

Steht der Mutter das alleinige Sorgerecht zu, erhält das Kind mit der Geburt den Familiennamen der Mutter. Die sorgeberechtigte Mutter kann jedoch dem Kind den Namen des nicht sorgeberechtigten Vaters erteilen. Hierzu muss eine Erklärung beim Standesamt von den Eltern persönlich abgegeben werden.

Wird eine gemeinsame Sorge der Eltern erst nach der Geburt begründet, können Sie innerhalb von drei Monaten den Familiennamen beim Standesamt neu bestimmen.

Hinweis: Alle Erklärungen zu einem Namen werden unwiderruflich durch die Eltern abgegeben! Eine spätere Änderung wegen Irrtums ist durch das Standesamt nicht möglich!

cities.q:
Ablauf und Verfahren
Antragsvoraussetzungen
Ihr Haupt- oder Nebenwohnsitz ist in Leipzig
Sie müssen persönlich im Bürgerbüro erscheinen
Personen, die von der Meldepflicht befreit oder ohne festen Wohnsitz sind, können ihren Führungszeugnisantrag bei der Meldebehörde stellen, in deren Bezirk sie sich gewöhnlich aufhalten
Beantragung
Das Führungszeugnis beantragen Sie persönlich in einem Bürgerbüro ganz in Ihrer Nähe. Eine Bevollmächtigung zur Antragstellung ist nicht möglich. Wird die betroffene Person gesetzlich vertreten (zum Beispiel Minderjährige), ist auch die Vertretungsperson antragsberechtigt.
Selbstverständlich können Sie Ihr Führungszeugnis auch online über das Online-Portal des Bundesamts für Justiz beantragen. Hierfür benötigen Sie den neuen elektronischen Personalausweis beziehungsweise einen elektronischen Aufenthaltstitel und ein Kartenlesegerät oder ein Smartphone mit AusweisApp2.
Übermittlung
Das Führungszeugnis wird durch das Bundesamt für Justiz ausgestellt. Ein Privatführungszeugnis übersendet das Bundesamt für Justiz nur an die antragstellende Person. Ein Führungszeugnis zur Vorlage bei einer deutschen Behörde wird der betreffenden Behörde durch das Bundesamt für Justiz unmittelbar übersandt.

cities.claim: Imposes a 30-hour weekly limit during Elterngeld receipt. BEEG §1(6) permits up to 32 hours averaged over the child’s life-month for the current cohort. A constant 31-hour week therefore does not itself defeat entitlement.
cities.q:
Kann ich in Teilzeit arbeiten, während ich Elterngeld bekomme?
Während Sie Elterngeld bekommen, dürfen Sie wöchentlich bis zu 30 Stunden (Lehrer: entsprechend ermäßigte Pflichtstundenzahl) arbeiten.
Erhalten Sie Elterngeld aus einem vorangegangen Erwerbseinkommen, so wird Ihr Einkommen aus der Teilzeittätigkeit während des Elterngeldbezuges ebenso angerechnet, wie mögliche Einkünfte aus selbständiger Arbeit, Gewerbebetrieb oder Land- und Forstwirtschaft. Auch sogenannte Minijobs werden berücksichtigt, einen Freibetrag gibt es nicht. Der Mindestbetrag (300,- Euro Basiselterngeld/150 Euro Elterngeld Plus) steht jedoch weiterhin zu.
Die Höhe des ElterngeldPlus liegt dabei bei höchstens der Hälfte des monatlichen Elterngeldbetrags, das Eltern ohne Teilzeiteinkommen zustünde. Der Mindestbetrag von Elterngeld, der Mindestgeschwisterbonus, der Mehrlingszuschlag sowie die von der Anrechnung freigestellten Elterngeldbeträge nach § 3 Abs. 2 BEEG werden ebenfalls halbiert.
cities.why: Imposes a 30-hour weekly limit during Elterngeld receipt. BEEG §1(6) permits up to 32 hours averaged over the child’s life-month for the current cohort. A constant 31-hour week therefore does not itself defeat entitlement.

cities.claim: Expressly denies the transport concession to severely disabled people without significant street-mobility impairment. SGB IX §228(1) separately covers qualifying deaf people who can meet the Gl criteria without meeting G.
cities.page: Feststellungsverfahren nach dem SGB IX - Schwerbehindertenrecht
cities.q:
Was ist der Unterschied zwischen dem grünen und dem grün-orangenen Ausweis?
Ausweise in grüner Farbe erhalten schwerbehinderte Menschen, also alle, bei denen ein Grad der Behinderung von mindestens 50 besteht. Der grün-orange Ausweis ist für schwerbehinderte Menschen, bei denen eine erhebliche Beeinträchtigung der Bewegungsfähigkeit im Straßenverkehr vorliegt. Sie haben das Recht auf unentgeltliche Beförderung im öffentlichen Personenverkehr oder hälftige Ermäßigung der Kfz-Steuer.
Umgekehrt bedeutet dies: Schwerbehinderte, die keine solche Beeinträchtigung haben, haben trotz der Behinderung keinen Anspruch auf die kostenlose Nutzung der Verkehrsmittel.
Wenn eine erhebliche Beeinträchtigung im Straßenverkehr vorliegt, hat man als schwerbehinderte Person Anspruch auf unentgeltliche Beförderung im Personenverkehr. Ganz kostenlos ist die Beförderung für schwerbehinderte Personen mit erheblicher Beeinträchtigung der Bewegungsfähigkeit im Straßenverkehr im Grunde genommen aber nicht: Beim Versorgungsamt muss man zunächst eine Wertmarke für die "Freifahrt" kaufen. Diese kostet für ein halbes Jahr 53 Euro, für ein ganzes Jahr 104 Euro.
Einige Personengruppen bekommen die Wertmarke auf Antrag tatsächlich kostenlos. Dies sind unter anderem Personen, die "H" (hilflos) oder "Bl" (blind) in ihrem Ausweis vermerkt haben. Auch Empfänger von u.a. ALG II, Leistungen nach dem SGB VIII und Leistungen nach dem Dritten und Vierten Kapitel des SGB XII (Hilfe zum Lebensunterhalt, Grundsicherung) können die Wertmarke kostenlos erhalten.
cities.why: Expressly denies the transport concession to severely disabled people without significant street-mobility impairment. SGB IX §228(1) separately covers qualifying deaf people who can meet the Gl criteria without meeting G.

Die Eltern können in der Zeit vom Tag der Geburt bis zur Vollendung des 18. Lebensmonats des Kindes Elterngeld beantragen.
